author: tiancaiamao
body:
## Fix

Restore proper `get_session_stats` handler instead of aliasing to `/session`.

### Root Cause

`get_session_stats` was incorrectly aliased to `/session` which returns `SessionState`, not `SessionStats`, causing all-zero stats in the frontend.

### Fix

Create a dedicated hidden `get_session_stats` handler that:
- Calls `collectSessionUsage()` for message counts and token tracking
- Supplements with `SystemPromptTokens`, `SystemToolsTokens`, `ActiveWindowTokens` estimates
- Populates `TokenRate` from agent metrics
- Returns proper `rpc.SessionStats` struct

Token counting follows the original design: only accumulate `OutputTokens` across messages (unique), use last `InputTokens` as representative value (since each LLM call's input includes full history).

### Testing

- `go build ./cmd/ai/...` ✅
- `go test ./cmd/ai/... ./pkg/rpc/...` ✅

This pull request introduces password reset functionality, email sending capabilities, and several related enhancements to the CRM system. It adds new endpoints and DTOs for password reset, integrates email services (including dependency setup), and improves the `UserDTO` to provide richer user information. Additionally, it makes minor updates to test and environment configuration.

**Password Reset Functionality:**

- Introduced password reset endpoints in `UsersController`, allowing users to request and perform password resets via `/password-reset/request` and `/password-reset/validate` endpoints. Corresponding request/response forms (`PasswordResetRequestForm`, `PasswordResetForm`) and a `PasswordResetToken` entity were added to support this workflow. author: seckatie
body:
## Summary

Adds an interactive item selector to `lola install` so users can opt out of skills, commands, agents, MCPs, or `AGENTS.md` instructions they don't want without forking the module. Closes #119.

- New CLI flags: `--skill` / `--command` / `--agent` / `--mcp` (each repeatable and comma-separated), `--instructions / --no-instructions`, plus `-y/--yes` to skip the picker.
- In TTY mode, `lola install` first asks "install everything?"; choosing no opens a fuzzy-searchable multi-select picker. Entries are type-prefixed (`skill: …`, `cmd: /…`, `agent: @…`, `mcp: …`, `instructions: AGENTS.md`). All entries start **deselected**; **Tab** toggles a single item and **Alt-A** inverts the current selection (toggle-all). Submitting with nothing checked is treated as a cancel.
- On reinstall, the picker pre-selects items already installed for the module (annotated `(installed)`) and marks newly-upstream items `(new)` so users can see the delta at a glance.
- New `Installation.full_install` flag locks cherry-picked installs to the original selection on `lola update` — newly-upstream items (skills, commands, agents, MCPs, or AGENTS.md) are not silently picked up. Full installs keep tracking upstream. Renamed registry entries are reapplied so picks survive reloads. Legacy `installed.yml` entries load as `full_install=True`; the field is only emitted to YAML when `False`.
- File-conflict prompts (skill / command / agent) gain an **Overwrite All** action that auto-overwrites every remaining collision of that kind for the current install.

## Related Issues

Closes #119

## Test Plan

- [x] `pytest` — 962 tests passing (new tests in `tests/test_cli_install_cherry_pick.py`)
- [x] `ruff check src tests` — clean
- [x] `bandit -r src` — clean (false-positive `B105` on the `__all__` sentinel suppressed with `# nosec`)
- [ ] Manual: `lola install <module>` asks "install everything?"; declining opens the fuzzy picker with everything deselected; Alt-A toggles all on; subsetting writes only chosen files and `full_install: false` to `installed.yml`
- [ ] Manual: `lola install <module> --skill foo --command bar` installs just `foo` + `bar`; omitted categories install nothing; `AGENTS.md` instructions are only written when `--instructions` is passed
- [ ] Manual: cherry-pick install + add a new skill upstream + `lola update` does **not** pick up the new skill; same flow with a full install does
- [ ] Manual: cherry-pick install that skipped instructions + drop an `AGENTS.md` upstream + `lola update` does **not** install instructions

## CLI shape

```
lola install my-module                            # asks "install everything?", then picker if no
lola install my-module -y                         # install everything, no prompt
lola install my-module --skill pr-review --skill commit
lola install my-module --skill pr-review,commit --command review
lola install my-module --skill pr-review --instructions
```

author: ohmspectator
body:
## Description

Replaces the raster (Atrament) border layer in `ClusterPaintEditor` with an **SVG vector border overlay** (ADR-0014).

**Backend (`wvImportMatchBorderTrace.ts`, ~150 LOC + 39 LOC tests):**
- New pure-compute module that extracts cluster borders from a pixel-label map using OpenCV's `findContours` (via the existing `__cv` global handle).
- Returns an array of `BorderPath` objects: `{ id, points: [x,y][], type: 'internal' | 'external', clusters: [a, b] }` — Douglas-Peucker simplified for compactness.
- Wired into the existing `cluster-review` payload alongside the cluster overlay PNG so the frontend gets vector paths and raster preview in one round-trip.
- No new endpoints, no DB writes. No transactions.

**Frontend:**
- `svgBorderUtils.ts` (~177 LOC + 82 LOC tests): SVG path serialization, point-in-path hit testing, polyline-split-at-cursor for the eraser, polyline endpoint snapping for the line tool.
- `ClusterPaintEditor.tsx` (538 LOC, replacing the 524-LOC Atrament version): renders borders as `<svg>` with smoothed cubic-bezier paths over the color canvas. Border eraser splits paths at the cursor; line tool draws new polylines with auto-snap to existing endpoints. Flood fill rasterizes the SVG on demand and stops at the vector borders.
- `atrament` removed from `package.json` and `frontend/src/types/atrament.d.ts` deleted (now dead code per ADR-0014).

3 commits, ~857 LOC net add.

## Related Issues

Implements ADR-0014 (added in this PR: `docs/decisions/0014-vector-border-editing.md`). No issue number — tracked via the rebuild plan.

## How Was This Tested?

All four pre-commit gates green locally:
- `npm run check` (lint + typecheck): ✅
- `npm run knip` (unused files / deps): ✅
- `TEST_REPORT_LOCAL=1 npm test` (backend + frontend, includes 39-line backend trace test + 82-line `svgBorderUtils.test.ts`): ✅
- `npm run security:all` (Semgrep + npm audit): ✅ (0 findings, 0 vulns)

## Checklist
- [x] Commit messages follow the standard template.
- [x] All commits are signed.
- [x] Related issues are mentioned in the description above.
- [x] Linter checks have been passed.

## Additional Comments

- No new admin routes added; no new DB writes; no transactions. The border-trace function returns its result through the existing `cluster-review` callback that PR #351 already added.
- `atrament` package and the `frontend/src/types/atrament.d.ts` shim are removed (the SVG approach replaces all raster brush/polygon/eraser functionality with native SVG path operations + on-demand canvas rasterization for flood fill).
- `ClusterPaintEditor.tsx` is 538 LOC — slightly above the ~1000-line CLAUDE.md guidance threshold isn't crossed; will revisit if it grows.
- During the rebase onto main, preserved the ovImg `crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` fix and the corrected effect dependency array (`[canvasSize.w, canvasSize.h, overlayImageUrl, saveSnapshot]`) that landed in PR #351.

author: luthermonson
body:
## Summary

Closes #211 in the non-breaking direction. Proxmox returns indexed device entries past 9 (e.g. `net0..net31`, `scsi0..scsi30`, `virtio0..virtio15`, `unused0..unused255`, `hostpci0..hostpci15`, `ipconfig0..ipconfig31`, `mp0..mp255`, `dev0..dev255`), but the existing `UnmarshalJSON` populated the helper maps via reflection over the struct, so any index >9 was silently dropped — `encoding/json` discards JSON keys that have no matching struct field before reflection ever runs.

This rewrites `VirtualMachineConfig.UnmarshalJSON` and `ContainerConfig.UnmarshalJSON` to also parse the body into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and route every `<prefix><digits>` key into the corresponding helper map. The explicit `Net0..Net9` (and friends) fields stay populated unchanged for back-compat — adding `// Deprecated:` markers and removing them is the v0.7.x step, called out in the package comment on the new `indexedDeviceMaps` helper.

The router uses prefix-then-pure-digits, not `strings.HasPrefix`, so:

- `scsihw` stays in `SCSIHW` (does **not** leak into `SCSIs`)
- the bare `numa` scalar stays in `Numa` (does **not** leak into `Numas`)

This is the latent collision bug that the closed PR #217 would have introduced; we have an explicit unit test guarding against it.

## What changed

- `types.go` — new `indexedDeviceMaps()` per-config helper plus a shared `indexedDeviceKey()` parser; rewritten `UnmarshalJSON` for both configs.
- `virtual_machine_config_test.go` — direct-unmarshal tests covering net15/net31, scsi30, unused15/unused255, hostpci15, ipconfig20, the two prefix collisions, and a unit test for `indexedDeviceKey`.
- `containers_test.go` — direct-unmarshal test for mp42/mp255, dev15, net20, unused100.
- `tests/mocks/pve9x/{virtual_machines,containers}.go` — new gock mocks at `qemu/102/{config,status/current}` and `lxc/102/{config,status/current}` so the parsing fix is also exercised end-to-end through `node.VirtualMachine(ctx, 102)` / `node.Container(ctx, 102)`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` (main package green; failing `tests/integration` is the live-Proxmox suite that needs credentials, unrelated)
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] New direct-Unmarshal unit tests cover indices >9 and prefix collisions
- [x] New integration-shape tests assert the maps are populated when configs are fetched through `node.VirtualMachine` / `node.Container`
- [x] Existing `Merge*` helper tests still pass — helpers remain idempotent for hand-built configs that bypass `UnmarshalJSON`

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- v0.7.x: add `// Deprecated: use Nets/SCSIs/...` markers to the explicit indexed fields and `Merge*` helpers, then remove them in a later release.

body:
## Summary

Third Live diagram plugin: a procedural city street network with an animated shortest-path search between two points. Inspired by the user's Buenos Aires reference — the network expands outward from the start node until it reaches the destination, then traces the shortest route in a different color. Loops on a configurable cadence.

## What changed

### New files
- [animation diagrams/map-route.jsx](animation diagrams/map-route.jsx) — \`window.MapRouteDiagram\` component.
  - **Procedural network**: NxN perturbed grid (default 24×24) with ~22 % edges randomly removed, picked from a seeded RNG (mulberry32) so the layout is reproducible. Edges incident to either endpoint are always kept so the graph stays connected around the dots.
  - **Dijkstra** (O(n²); fine for ≤ ~1500 nodes) computes distances and parent pointers from the start node once.
  - **Three-phase rAF animation**: \`search\` (cutoff grows linearly over \`searchDuration\`) → \`path\` (stroke-dashoffset reveal over \`pathDuration\`) → \`pause\` (\`pauseDuration\`). Loops when \`loop\` is true.
  - **Performance**: edges are presorted by their reach time and the search-overlay path string is rebuilt each frame from the prefix inside the cutoff, so the per-frame cost is O(visited). Base network is rendered once.
  - Endpoint dots have a soft pulsing halo; the found route gets a drop-shadow glow when drawn.
- [animation diagrams/Map Route.html](animation diagrams/Map Route.html) — minimal studio (same shape as the others). Reads \`#tweaks=…\` and posts \`gs:diagram-pick:select\` back when \`?from=editor\`.

### Registry
- [animation diagrams/diagrams-registry.jsx](animation diagrams/diagrams-registry.jsx) — new \`mapRoute\` entry with defaults, \`tweaksToProps\`, schema. Schema introduces a new field type \`color\` (single picker), used for the 4 colors. Labels in en + es.

### Editor
- [editor/EditorShell.jsx](editor/EditorShell.jsx) \`DiagramTweaksForm\` gains a \`color\` field renderer: native HTML5 color picker plus a JetBrains-Mono hex text input that accepts partial typing and only commits valid hex.

### Plumbing
- [Goal Slide Editor.html](Goal Slide Editor.html) loads \`map-route.jsx\` so \`window.MapRouteDiagram\` is available at render time.
- [animation diagrams/Diagram Library.html](animation diagrams/Diagram Library.html) — new live "Map Route" card (DIAG-006) with a hand-drawn SVG thumbnail. Catalog header and footer counters bumped (2 → 3 live).

## Configurable parameters

| Group | Field | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Network | density | 8–36 grid size |
| Network | seed | RNG seed |
| Animation | searchDuration / pathDuration / pauseDuration | ms |
| Animation | loop | restarts the cycle |
| Colors | networkColor | streets (faint base) |
| Colors | searchColor | visited overlay |
| Colors | routeColor | found shortest path |
| Colors | nodeColor | endpoint dots |

The two endpoint *positions* are fixed (deterministic from the network grid) — only their **colors** are user-controlled, as requested.

## Test plan

- [ ] Insert a Diagram block → **Open Diagram Library** → click the new **Map Route** card → studio opens with the live animation.
- [ ] In **From editor** mode, click **Use in slide**. The cell now shows the animated map.
- [ ] In the right panel, change \`Density\` from 24 → 30 — the grid gets denser; change \`Seed\` — a different layout appears, two dots stay roughly in their corners.
- [ ] Change each of the four colors via the new color picker — preview updates live.
- [ ] Set \`Search duration\` to 1000 ms, \`Path duration\` to 400 ms, \`Pause\` to 2000 ms — animation feels much faster, holds the route longer between cycles.
- [ ] Toggle \`Loop\` off — the animation runs once and stops at the final state.
- [ ] Switch the editor language to Spanish — labels translate (Red, Densidad, Semilla aleatoria, Animación, Colores, Calles, Resaltado de búsqueda, Ruta encontrada, Puntos…).

author: amsach
body:
## Summary

Fixed TypeError in InfobloxDataSource.run() by properly passing *args **kwargs to the base class.

## Root Cause

The initial fix (PR #1) removed explicit kwargs from super().run(), which fixed the TypeError. However, the subclass's run() signature still had named parameters like dryrun, memory_profiling, and debug. When Python sees named parameters in the signature, it strips those keys from kwargs *before* resolving the call. This meant the base class DataSyncBaseJob never received dryrun, memory_profiling, etc.

## Fix

1. Both InfobloxDataSource and InfobloxDataTarget now extract kwargs values for their instance attributes using kwargs.get()
2. They then pass *args **kwargs to super().run()
3. Added getattr() guard for enable_sync_to_nautobot/infoblox checks to prevent AttributeError if config is None

This preserves the kwargs dict for the base class while allowing the subclass to use the parameter values.

## Reviewer Feedback

This addresses the concern raised by @molhamalnasr in nautobot/nautobot-app-ssot#1191.

## Testing

- Syntax check passed
- Pattern matches how DataSyncBaseJob.run() handles kwargs

author: kitplummer
body:
## Summary

Closes [#108](https://github.com/defenseunicorns/peat-gateway/issues/108). Before this PR, a control-plane payload whose handler kept returning \`Err\` would be retried up to \`max_deliver\` times and then **silently dropped** — operators had no way to inspect or replay the failed payload. This PR adds a Dead Letter Queue: on the final attempt the dispatch loop publishes the original payload (with metadata headers) to a dedicated JetStream stream before terminating the message.

## DLQ design

- **Single shared stream** \`peat-gw-dlq\` capturing the literal-prefix subject space \`peat.gw.dlq.>\`. Created idempotently by \`IngressEngine::new\` when ingress is enabled. Literal prefix means no overlap with per-org control-plane subjects.
- **Subject convention**: \`peat.gw.dlq.{org_id}\` (literal, not a pattern). Per-org isolation comes from the \`org_id\` token; primary tenant boundary remains broker-level account ACLs (#97).
- **Headers** (every entry): \`Peat-Org-Id\`, \`Peat-Original-Subject\`, \`Peat-Delivery-Count\`, \`Peat-Last-Error\`.
- **Payload**: original message bytes verbatim, suitable for replay.

## Dispatch loop wiring

- Handler \`Err\` with \`msg.info().delivered >= max_deliver\` → publish DLQ + \`term\` (broker stops redelivering, cursor advances).
- Handler \`Err\` with attempts remaining → \`nack\` as before.
- DLQ publish failure → log + fall back to \`nack\` so the message isn't lost while the DLQ stream is broken.

## Config

- \`max_deliver\` and \`ack_wait_secs\` are now fields on \`NatsIngressConfig\` with \`PEAT_INGRESS_MAX_DELIVER\` and \`PEAT_INGRESS_ACK_WAIT_SECS\` env-var fallbacks. Defaults unchanged (5 / 30s). Tests pass low values for fast poison-pill scenarios.

## Test plan

- [x] New \`poison_pill_payload_routes_to_dlq_on_max_deliver\`: malformed JSON payload, \`max_deliver=1\` + \`ack_wait_secs=1\`, asserts payload + 4 headers round-trip via a JetStream pull consumer on \`peat.gw.dlq.{org}\`. Test runs in ~140ms.
- [x] \`cargo fmt --check\` ✅
- [x] \`cargo clippy -- -D warnings\` (default + \`--features nats\`) ✅
- [x] \`cargo test\` — 126 lib + 320+ integration tests, all green
- [x] \`cargo test --features nats\` — **25/25 NATS-feature tests** (18 ingress + 2 jetstream sanity + 5 sink)
- [x] \`cargo build --features full\` + per-feature test builds (postgres / aws-kms / vault / kafka) all clean
- [ ] CI matrix
- [ ] Peat QA Review

## Out of scope (deliberate, follow-ups not yet filed)

- **Handler panic recovery** — a panicking handler still crashes the per-org dispatch task. Documented in the new docs section + module-level comment.
- **Admin API endpoint** for DLQ inspection / replay — operators use the \`nats\` CLI today (workflow documented in \`docs/control-plane-ingress.md\`). REST surface lives behind the same IDAM federation work as #99.

## Docs

New "Dead Letter Queue" section in \`docs/control-plane-ingress.md\` with subject convention, headers, tunables, an inspection workflow (\`nats consumer add\` + \`nats consumer next\`), and the out-of-scope notes.

Refs #91 #94 #108
Closes #108 (subject to QA Review)

author: abrhamt
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the 8x loop of `lodash.shuffle` with a single Fisher-Yates algorithm, and changed `draw()` to use `pop()` instead of a random `splice()`.
🎯 **Why:** The previous approach took O(n) time for every single draw and redundantly shuffled the deck 8 times (O(n * 8)). Since the deck only needs to be randomized once, Fisher-Yates shuffle provides a mathematically uniform shuffle in O(n) time. By randomly popping from the end, we achieve O(1) time complexity for draws.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces deck creation time from ~145ms per 10k decks to ~31ms (nearly 5x speedup) and reduces per-draw complexity from O(n) to O(1).

## Security research probe — non-destructive (Codex AGENTS.md injection)

This PR exists ONLY to verify FINDING-PGCLI-CODEX (Codex instruction injection
via fork-controlled AGENTS.md). It WILL BE CLOSED without merge.

### What the PoC does

Adds `AGENTS.md` containing a canary instruction directing Codex to include
a specific string (`CANARY-FINDING-PGCLI-CODEX-INJECTION-CONFIRMED-SC017`) in its
review output. If the canary appears in the PR comment posted by `post-feedback` job,
fork AGENTS.md injection is confirmed.

### What it does NOT do

- Does not exfiltrate `OPENAI_API_KEY` value
- Does not make unauthorized API calls
- Does not modify any source code or tests

### Why

`codex-review.yml` triggers on `pull_request_target` for all non-draft PRs (no gate).
Checks out `refs/pull/{N}/merge` (fork code). `openai/codex-action@v1` reads
instruction files including `AGENTS.md` from the working directory before reviewing.

PR closed within 1 hour.

body:
## Summary

PR 4 of the agent-slack-notification feature ([spec](docs/agent-slack-notification-tool.md), [plan](docs/agent-slack-notification-tool-implementation-plan.md)). Wires the control-plane `POST /sessions/:id/slack-notify` endpoint that sandboxes will call from the new tool in PR 5.

- Sandbox-authenticated route validates against the session DO, then loads session metadata + resolved Slack settings from D1.
- Sanitizes the agent's text via `@open-inspect/shared/slack/mrkdwn` (broadcast strip → link sanitize → mentions policy → length cap).
- Forwards the agent's channel input verbatim to `chat.postMessage`; channel access is delegated to Slack's bot-membership model (no Open-Inspect-side allowlist).
- Categorized denial reasons: `feature_unavailable` (no token), `feature_disabled` (master switch off), `empty_message_after_sanitization`, `channel_not_found_or_forbidden`, `rate_limited`, `slack_api_error`.
- Emits `tool_call` (completed/error) + `tool_result` events on success and a single failed `tool_call` on denial, with attribution metadata (prompt author, trigger source, parent session, channel input/ID, message ts, permalink, sanitization metadata) — visible in the session transcript.
- `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` added to control-plane `Env` (optional) and bound via Terraform when the variable is non-empty. Bot token never leaves the control plane.
- Adds `chat.getPermalink` to `@open-inspect/shared/slack` (was missing) and surfaces `channel` on `chat.postMessage` responses so the success result can include a permalink for the user.

The endpoint is reachable but no sandbox can call it yet — the tool itself ships in PR 5. Integration tests exercise it directly via `SELF.fetch`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -w @open-inspect/control-plane` — 1078/1078 pass (15 new unit tests for slack-notify).
- [x] `npm run test:integration -w @open-inspect/control-plane` — 332/332 pass (5 new workerd integration tests covering 401/403/200/404/channel-passthrough).
- [x] `npm test -w @open-inspect/shared` — 135/135 pass (shared client additions).
- [x] `npm test -w @open-inspect/slack-bot` — 48/48 pass (additive shared changes don't regress slack-bot).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean across all packages.
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean.
- [ ] Smoke in dev: configure global Slack settings via PR 3's UI, then `curl /sessions/:id/slack-notify` with a synthesized sandbox-auth token; observe message in Slack and tool-call events on the session.
- [ ] `grep` dev logs for the bot token after the smoke test — must not appear.

## Notes for review

- Channel passthrough is intentional per spec §6.1 — agent input goes to Slack verbatim; Slack does the lookup and rejects forbidden channels with `not_in_channel`/`channel_not_found`/`is_archived`, all mapped to `channel_not_found_or_forbidden`.
- Tool events are emitted via the existing `/internal/sandbox-event` DO endpoint with `sandboxId: "control-plane"` to distinguish server-emitted events. The DO's `processSandboxEvent` persists tool_call (status="completed"/"error") and tool_result events normally.
- `feature_unavailable` (missing token) is distinct from `feature_disabled` (master switch off) — only the latter emits an event.
- Per the plan's open question §1, `reason` is capped at 500 chars and silently truncated server-side.
- Per §3, `channel` is capped at 80 chars (Slack's max).

author: jflowers
body:
## Summary

Add `--ide` flag to DevPod sandbox commands for IDE selection and fix three sandbox lifecycle bugs (Attach, Destroy, health check).

## User-Facing Changes

### New: `--ide` flag on `uf sandbox create` and `uf sandbox start`

Select which IDE DevPod opens when creating or resuming a workspace:

```bash
uf sandbox create --backend devpod --ide vscode
uf sandbox start --ide vscode
```

Valid values: `none` (default), `vscode`, `openvscode`, `fleet`, `jupyternotebook`, `cursor`. Invalid values produce a clear error listing all options.

### New: `UF_SANDBOX_IDE` environment variable and `sandbox.ide` config field

IDE can be set persistently via env var or `.uf/config.yaml`:

```bash
export UF_SANDBOX_IDE=vscode
```

Or in `.uf/config.yaml`:
```yaml
sandbox:
  ide: vscode
```

Resolution order: `--ide` flag > `UF_SANDBOX_IDE` env var > config file > default `"none"`.

### Fixed: `uf sandbox attach` with DevPod workspaces

Previously, `attach` always fell back to ephemeral container logic. Now it detects persistent DevPod/Podman workspaces and delegates to the correct backend.

### Fixed: `uf sandbox destroy` with no persistent workspace

Previously, `destroy` called `ResolveBackend()` which auto-detected DevPod and failed with "couldn't find workspace" for ephemeral containers. Now it handles ephemeral cleanup directly (stop + rm container).

### New: OpenCode server auto-start in DevPod

DevPod containers now auto-start the OpenCode server via `postStartCommand` in the devcontainer template. `uf sandbox start` waits for the server health check (60s timeout, exponential backoff) before attaching.

## Manual Testing / Demo

```bash
# 1. Create a DevPod workspace with VS Code
uf sandbox create --backend devpod --ide vscode --detach

# 2. Resume with a different IDE
uf sandbox start --ide openvscode

# 3. Verify invalid IDE is rejected
uf sandbox create --backend devpod --ide sublime
# Expected: "unknown IDE: sublime, use one of: ..."

# 4. Verify env var fallback
export UF_SANDBOX_IDE=fleet
uf sandbox create --backend devpod --detach
# Expected: DevPod opens with Fleet

# 5. Verify ephemeral mode ignores --ide
uf sandbox create --ide vscode
# Expected: starts normally without passing --ide to podman

# 6. Test Attach fix (requires existing DevPod workspace)
uf sandbox attach
# Expected: detects persistent workspace, attaches via backend

# 7. Test Destroy fix (no persistent workspace)
uf sandbox destroy
# Expected: "No sandbox to destroy" (not a DevPod error)
```

## Developer Changes

### New functions
- `validateIDE()` in `internal/sandbox/devpod.go` — strict allowlist validation against DevPod's supported IDE values
- `waitForHealth()` in `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go` — exponential backoff health polling (500ms→5s, 60s timeout)

### Modified functions
- `DevPodBackend.Create()` / `Start()` — IDE validation + `--ide` arg passthrough to `devpod up`
- `Attach()` — `isPersistentWorkspace()` check before ephemeral fallback
- `Destroy()` — ephemeral cleanup path when no persistent workspace exists
- `DefaultConfig()` — IDE resolution chain (flag > env > default)
- `merge()`, `Defaults()`, `IsEmpty()`, `applyEnvOverrides()` in `internal/config/config.go` — IDE field support in unified config layer

### Modified files
- `cmd/unbound-force/sandbox.go` — `--ide` flag wiring on create/start commands
- `internal/sandbox/devpod.go` — `validateIDE()`, IDE passthrough, `waitForHealth()` in Start
- `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go` — Attach/Destroy dispatch fixes, `waitForHealth()`
- `internal/sandbox/config.go` — `DefaultIDE` constant, `DefaultConfig()` IDE resolution
- `internal/sandbox/workspace.go` — `IDE` field on `SandboxConfig`
- `internal/config/config.go` — IDE in merge, defaults, env overrides, IsEmpty
- `internal/config/template.go` — `ide` in config template
- `internal/scaffold/assets/devcontainer/devcontainer.json` — `postStartCommand`
- `internal/sandbox/sandbox_test.go` — 16 new tests

### Error wrapping
All `devpod` subprocess errors now use `%w` (wrappable) instead of `%s`, enabling `errors.Is()`/`errors.As()` inspection by callers.

### Tests (16 new)
- IDE validation: `TestValidateIDE_AllValidValues`, `TestValidateIDE_InvalidValue`
- IDE passthrough: `TestDevPodCreate_IDEPassthrough`, `TestDevPodCreate_IDEDefaultNone`, `TestDevPodCreate_InvalidIDEReturnsError`, `TestDevPodStart_IDEPassthrough`, `TestDevPodStart_IDEDefaultNone`, `TestDevPodStart_InvalidIDEReturnsError`
- IDE resolution: `TestDefaultConfig_IDEPrecedence`
- Health check: `TestWaitForHealth_ImmediateSuccess`, `TestWaitForHealth_DelayedSuccess`, `TestWaitForHealth_Timeout`
- Lifecycle fixes: `TestAttach_DetectsPersistentDevPodWorkspace`, `TestAttach_FallsBackToEphemeral`, `TestDestroy_EphemeralCleansUpContainer`, `TestDestroy_EphemeralNoContainer`
- Ephemeral guard: `TestStart_EphemeralIgnoresIDE`

author: sebastionoss
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens `APITool._make_api_call()` (`application/agents/tools/api_tool.py`) against two SSRF gaps (CWE-918) that bypass the existing `validate_url()` allowlist check.

**1. Redirect-based SSRF bypass.** All seven HTTP method branches (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`) call `requests.<method>(...)` without `allow_redirects=False`. `requests` follows 3xx redirects by default. `validate_url()` is only applied to the initial URL; a legitimate, allow-listed external endpoint can return `Location: http://169.254.169.254/...` (or any RFC1918 / loopback target) and the redirected request is sent without re-validation. The fix passes `allow_redirects=False` on every branch.

**2. Path-parameter injection.** When the configured URL template contains `{param}` placeholders, the substitution at line 91-95 inserts the raw `str(query_params[param_name])` into the URL. Path parameter values originate from LLM tool-call arguments and are influenced by retrieved document content / user queries (a realistic prompt-injection surface in an agent system). A value containing `/`, `?`, `#`, or `@` can change the request path, append/override query parameters on the configured host, or alter the URL fragment. The fix wraps the value in `urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")` before substitution so reserved characters are percent-encoded.

## Fix

`application/agents/tools/api_tool.py`:
- Import `quote` alongside `urlencode`.
- Encode path-param values with `quote(str(value), safe="")` before `request_url.replace(...)`.
- Add `allow_redirects=False` to all `requests.{get,post,put,delete,patch,head,options}` calls.

The diff is small and surgical (~30 lines of production code).

## Tests

Added `tests/agents/tools/test_cwe918_api_tool_ssrf.py` (220 lines) covering:
- `allow_redirects=False` is set on each of the 7 HTTP methods.
- A redirect to `169.254.169.254` (AWS metadata) is not followed.
- Path values containing `/`, `?`, `#`, `@` are percent-encoded and do not alter URL structure.
- Normal alphanumeric path params still work end-to-end.

Existing api_tool tests still pass; behaviour for non-malicious inputs is unchanged.

## Adversarial review

Before submitting we tried to disprove this. The pre-existing `validate_url()` checks both the configured URL and the post-substitution URL, which initially looked like sufficient defence. It isn't:
- Redirect bypass: `validate_url()` runs *before* the HTTP call, never on the `Location` header. The default `allow_redirects=True` means the second hop is unchecked. This is exploitable whenever an admin configures an api_tool pointing at any host that an attacker can influence to issue a redirect (their own server, a vulnerable third-party, or an open-redirect endpoint on a trusted host).
- Path-param bypass: the post-substitution `validate_url()` re-check does catch host-changing payloads like `{id}` → `evil.com/x` because `urlparse` would surface a different `netloc`. It does **not** catch payloads that keep the host but mutate the path/query/fragment — for example a value `123?admin=true` that flips a privileged query flag, or `..%2fadmin` that traverses to a different endpoint on the same allow-listed host. Encoding is the correct defence-in-depth.

Preconditions are realistic for DocsGPT's agent architecture (a configured api_tool plus prompt-injection or attacker-controlled redirect endpoint) and do not by themselves grant equivalent SSRF capability.

## Notes for maintainers

- I noticed `SECURITY.md` prefers GitHub's private vulnerability reporting flow. I don't have permission to open an advisory on this repo, so I'm submitting publicly. Happy to redact and move to a private advisory if you'd prefer — just let me know.
- No behavioural change for legitimate API tool usage: redirects are uncommon in REST API integrations, and percent-encoding is what callers normally want for path params.

Sets brightness, color, or color temperature without changing the on/off state.

hass seems not supporting change brightness, color temperature without turning light on. So, I add new service to change that values without turning light on.

I use this to dim real lights at nighttime. It simplifies automations by letting a virtual light remember the desired brightness and color temperature even while real lights are off.

There are two automations:
- Sync real light attributes with the virtual light.
- Invoke `virtual.set_light` on a time-based trigger to update brightness and color temperature.

Changes take effect immediately for lights that are already on. Lights that are off will apply the values when they are turned on.

## Security research probe — non-destructive (Codex AGENTS.md injection)

This PR verifies FINDING-MYCLI-CODEX: Codex reads fork-modified AGENTS.md
and follows injected instructions. PR WILL BE CLOSED without merge.

### What the PoC does

Prepends a canary instruction to the existing `AGENTS.md`. If Codex includes
`CANARY-FINDING-MYCLI-CODEX-INJECTION-CONFIRMED-SC018` in its review comment,
injection is confirmed.

### Why

`codex-review.yml`: `pull_request_target` + non-draft = zero gate + `refs/pull/{N}/merge`
checkout + Codex reads `AGENTS.md` from working directory. Existing `AGENTS.md` (122 lines)
is already in the repo, making mycli a more direct injection target than pgcli.

PR closed within 1 hour.

author: agenta-asaf
body:
## Summary

Virtualize the agent message list (`AgentDocumentView`) using `@tanstack/solid-virtual` so only the visible window + 5-item overscan is mounted in the DOM. Resolves Issue 4 from the agent-pane perf report (DOM virtualization).

**Driving symptom:** in long agent sessions (500-2000+ document nodes), the layout tree alone reaches ~8MB per pane. Tab-switches *into* a pane hosting an active agent stalled for 200ms+ (multiple long-tasks per switch, worst observed 269ms). Switching b↔c (no agent) is fast; switching a↔b (agent in `a`) is slow. Confirmed live in the dev session that drove this work (#769 file).

## What changed

- `frontend/app/view/agent/components/AgentDocumentView.tsx` — replaced `<For each={document()}>` with virtualizer-driven absolute-positioned items.
- `frontend/app/view/agent/styles/_document.scss` — removed `content-visibility: auto` / `contain-intrinsic-size` from `.agent-document-node-wrapper` (no longer needed, items aren't in the DOM at all when off-screen). Added `.agent-document-virtualizer` for the `position: relative` wrapper.
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — added `@tanstack/solid-virtual` ^3.13.

## Three reworked flows

These read DOM directly under the old `<For>` and had to be reauthored:

| Flow | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `scrollToNode` (jump-to-bookmark / search) | `querySelector + getBoundingClientRect`, smooth-scroll to centerOffset | Resolve index first; `virtualizer.scrollToIndex(idx, { align: 'center' })`. Old approach failed if target was outside virtual window. |
| `jumpToBottom` / `scrollToBottom` | `scrollTop = MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (deliberately, to avoid sync layout read on keystroke hot path) | `virtualizer.scrollToIndex(last, { align: 'end' })` — also avoids sync layout reads. |
| `handleScroll` older-history load | Snapshot `scrollHeight + scrollTop`, restore via `new_scrollTop = new_scrollHeight - old_scrollHeight + old_scrollTop` | Anchor by node id. Pre-virt the pixel-delta math was reliable; with measured virtual heights it isn't, until every newly-rendered item settles. Re-anchoring to the same node's index after prepend is exact regardless of measurement timing. |

## Risk surfaces considered

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| **Variable item heights** (tool blocks 32→400px when pinned, code diffs 500+px) | TanStack supports dynamic sizing via `measureElement` + ResizeObserver. estimateSize=80 matches old contain-intrinsic-size hint; real heights settle on first paint. |
| **Collapse/expand state** (`collapsedNodes`, `pinnedNodes` Sets in DocumentState) | Held in **parent** state, not child — already accessed via reactive accessors per existing comment at line 449. Re-mount during scroll preserves state. |
| **Tool-pin overlay portal** (Tool blocks render `<Portal>` to body when pinned, measure via getBoundingClientRect) | Items in the virtual window have valid refs. Pinning a tool that's in the visible region works. Off-screen pin is not a user-reachable action (the pin button is on the row, which means the row is visible). |
| **Truncate-suppression grace window** (5000ms post-SessionStart in reducer) | View-only change — reducer logic untouched. |
| **DOM export / copy via getSelection()** | Native selection unaffected by re-mount of off-screen items. |
| **scrollMargin for loading-older banner / auth-url box** | `scrollMargin` getter reads `virtualContainerRef.offsetTop` so virtualizer scroll math accounts for content rendered above the virtual list. |
| **`<For>` keying of virtualItems** | `getItemKey: (idx) => document()[idx]?.id` provides stable keys across reorder/prepend; SolidJS For's reference identity is stable when the underlying nodes don't change. |

## Untested scenarios I want reviewers to flag

- **Very long pinned tool block with code diff inside.** measureElement should settle to the full expanded height after one frame, but if the inner DiffViewer mounts async (Suspense, dynamic import, or its own virtualization), the measure might shoot up after several frames. Smoke this with a long bash output that's pinned-open.
- **Prepend-while-scrolling** — user scrolls toward top, history loads, then user keeps scrolling before the rAF anchor restore fires. The anchor logic is correct but the brief frame between prepend and anchor-restore could show jump.
- **Search-jump to a node deep in history** — the new `findIndex(node.id)` does an O(n) scan; at 2000 nodes it's fast but worth confirming.

## Local smoke

Type-check passes. Local dev smoke deferred — ran in a `git worktree` so I didn't disrupt the user's running test session for #772. Would appreciate a smoke pass from a reviewer with a long agent session.

## Cross-references

- Agent pane perf report (driving doc): not in repo, summary in PR description.
- Issue 4 (the relevant excerpt): "No DOM virtualization in AgentDocumentView. SolidJS `<For>` is fine-grained but does not remove DOM nodes for off-screen items. With `content-visibility: auto`, the browser skips painting off-screen nodes but still maintains them in the layout tree and retains their JS closures."
- Tab-switch mark coverage (PR #772) — measures the user-perceived switch cost this PR is trying to reduce. After both land, the same long-task instrumentation will show whether the agent-pane reflow on tab-switch drops.

author: anranyus
body:
## Summary

Spec follow-up after **PR #19 / T1.4b part 3d-ii** (merged at f82894a). That PR introduced two things the T1.4 spec didn't yet cover:

1. **`ConnectError.NO_ACTIVE_SERVER`** as a first-class error (runner-emitted when a side-effect intent runs with `ActiveServerHolder.current.value == null`).
2. **`PrimaryAction { RETRY, DISMISS }`** on `ConnectErrorCopy.Lookup`, so each error's button click handler is data-driven instead of hardcoded to `onRetry`.

## §5 changes in this PR

- Enum list now lists 8 values (added `NO_ACTIVE_SERVER`).
- Existing column **Primary CTA** clarified as **Primary CTA (label)**; a new **Action** column carries the `PrimaryAction` enum. All existing rows are `RETRY` (the default).
- New row for `NO_ACTIVE_SERVER`:
  - title: `没有选中的服务器` / `No active server`
  - body: `还没有选好要连的服务器。从历史里挑一个，或在表单里输入 IP。` / `No server is selected. Pick one from history, or enter an IP again.`
  - suggestion: `选服务器或重新输入` / `Pick a server or enter again`
  - CTA label: `去选择` / `Choose`
  - Action: **DISMISS** (button calls `onDismissError`, not `onRetry`)
- Copy is the locked chat-consensus version (msgs `b522a9f3` / `6ca9c818` / `81a4c7cc` in T1.4b thread).
- Added an **Action vs. CTA label invariant** note pointing at the `ConnectErrorCopyTest` ratchet that fails the build if a `DISMISS` row regresses to a `Retry` label (PR #19 round 2 baked this into tests).
- Added a **NO_ACTIVE_SERVER semantic** sub-section describing the runner trigger, reducer wiring (`ConnectAttempt` → `Lost`), zero-IO guarantee, and why the CTA dismisses instead of retrying (a null-server retry would just loop into the same error).

## Why DISMISS, not RETRY

Retrying a null active server would re-enter the same error path with no user-visible change — exactly the loop @Lily caught in PR #19 review (msg 75589ea2). The user's actual recovery is to pick a server from history or re-enter an IP, both of which are already on screen behind the error sheet. `DISMISS` returns control to that screen.

author: delexw
body:
## Summary

Audit and compatibility fix for Codex v0.129.0 (PR #20471), which removed `item/fileChange` and `outputDelta` notification events from the app-server event stream.

## Audit Finding

codex-trace is **unaffected** by this change. The tool reads JSONL session files from disk (`~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`) via filesystem watchers — it never connects to the Codex app-server event stream. Neither `item/fileChange` nor `outputDelta` are referenced anywhere in the codebase.

Even if these event types appeared as `event_msg` entries in older JSONL session files, they would be silently dropped by the existing wildcard arm in `handle_event_msg`. File-change data is already read from `patch_apply_end` events via `patch_changes` — no dependency on the removed notification types exists.

## Changes

- **`src-tauri/src/parser/turn.rs`**: Added regression test `v0129_removed_item_file_change_and_output_delta_events_ignored_gracefully` that:
  - Verifies `item/fileChange` and `outputDelta` `event_msg` entries are silently ignored
  - Confirms turns still complete normally when these events are present in a session JSONL file
  - Documents the architectural boundary (disk-based JSONL reading, not app-server subscription)

## Testing

All existing tests continue to pass (60 Rust unit tests, 122 frontend tests). The new test explicitly exercises the v0.129.0 compat scenario.

Fixes #29

author: wokersilva
body:
### Motivation
- Replace the previous stub DB plumbing with real SQLAlchemy/psycopg factories and a health-check so the app can operate against Postgres.
- Provide idempotent, versioned SQL migrations to create the core schema and enforce deduplication constraints.
- Expose database operations (`check`, `migrate`, `status`) through application services so the CLI does not execute SQL inline.

### Description
- Added a DB factory and session maker in `src/besoccer_scraper/infrastructure/db/connection.py` with URL normalization (`postgresql+psycopg`) and `database_healthcheck` that runs `SELECT 1`.
- Implemented an idempotent `MigrationRunner` in `src/besoccer_scraper/infrastructure/db/migrations.py` that tracks applied versions in `schema_migrations` and executes the SQL files in `sql/postgres/001..006` only once.
- Created concrete Postgres repositories and a `PostgresUnitOfWork` in `src/besoccer_scraper/infrastructure/db/repositories.py` for `sources`, `competitions`, `seasons`, `teams`, `scrape_targets`, `raw_pages`, `matches`, `job_runs`, `job_logs`, and `run_locks`.
- Added SQL migration files to create the base schema and enforce deduplication constraints including `UNIQUE(source_name, target_type, url)` and a unique partial index on `(source_name, source_match_id)` where `source_match_id IS NOT NULL` (`sql/postgres/00*_*.sql`).
- Introduced `DatabaseService` (`src/besoccer_scraper/application/db_services.py`) and updated CLI (`src/besoccer_scraper/cli/db.py` and `src/besoccer_scraper/cli/app.py`) to support `db check`, `db migrate`, and `db status` that call the service APIs.
- Wired the new DB factories and session into the application container in `src/besoccer_scraper/bootstrap.py` so `uow` is constructed with a real SQLAlchemy session.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall src` to verify the codebase compiles successfully; compilation completed without errors.

author: oten91
body:
## Summary

CPU profile from a mainnet gateway pod under ~9.2K rps showed ~30% of CPU spent in `runtime.gcBgMarkWorker` / `scanobject`, driven by ~669 MB/s of heap allocations. This branch addresses the three highest-leverage allocators identified in the profile.

- **Stop per-message logger growth on the WebSocket path.** `websocketRequestContext.hydratedLogger` was reassigning `wrc.logger` on every message and re-adding ~5 fields, so the logger's underlying zerolog buffer grew unboundedly over the connection's lifetime. Profile: ~36% of all heap allocations (~1.9 TB cumulative on a busy pod). Replaced with a one-shot connection-level hydration plus a non-mutating `methodLogger`.
- **Key the reputation cache and session-exhaustion tracker by structs instead of derived strings.** `reputation.service.cache` was `map[string]Score` indexed by `EndpointKey.String()` (~100 GB cumulative). `sessionExhaustionTracker.entries` was `map[string]time.Time` indexed by `serviceID + "|" + sessionID + "|" + supplier` (~90 GB cumulative). Both use struct keys directly now.
- **De-duplicate `BuildKey` calls in `filterByReputation` / `getEndpointScores`.** Both functions iterated the endpoints map twice and called `keyBuilder.BuildKey(...)` once per endpoint per pass. For per-domain granularity this allocates inside `URL.Parse` + hostname extraction. Cached the (addr, ep, key) triples in a single pass; also dropped a redundant `.With(\"method\", ...)` in the per-session loop in `getSessionsUniqueEndpoints` and hoisted the per-iteration `getMinThresholdForService` call out of the filter loop.

### Microbenchmarks (Apple M1, polyzero info-level discard logger)

WebSocket per-message logger:

```
legacy_hydratedLogger_mutating-8       312,775 ns/op  3,554,957 B/op  22 allocs/op
fixed_methodLogger-8                       205.8 ns/op       680 B/op   4 allocs/op

legacy_after_10k_messages-8            746,165 ns/op  8,347,279 B/op  23 allocs/op
fixed_after_10k_messages-8                 202.0 ns/op       680 B/op   4 allocs/op
```

The fixed pattern's per-message cost is constant; the legacy pattern grew linearly because each `.With` cloned the accumulating zerolog context buffer (after 10k messages, every additional `.With` was copying ~8 MB).

`filterByReputation` (per-domain granularity, the case where `BuildKey` allocates):

```
              endpoints=8        endpoints=32
legacy   :    ~48,000 ns/op       ~193,000 ns/op
                5,056 B/68 allocs   24,496 B/265 allocs
fixed    :    ~23,000 ns/op       ~123,000 ns/op
                3,520 B/37 allocs   18,480 B/138 allocs
                (-46% allocs)       (-48% allocs)
```

For per-endpoint granularity (default) wall-clock is comparable; the cached-triple slice is +1 small allocation per call (~1-3 KB) but is offset by the saved second map iteration.

### Expected production impact

The CPU profile on the affected pod attributed:
- ~36% of heap allocations to the WS `hydratedLogger` (commit 1)
- ~4% combined to `EndpointKey.String` + `sessionExhaustionKey` string concat (commit 2)
- A smaller share to duplicate `BuildKey` calls under per-domain granularity (commit 3)

GC CPU on that pod was ~30% of total. With ~40% of the alloc rate gone, expect roughly 10-15% raw CPU back per pod, plus more consistent hedge timing (the hedge rate was suppressed under load because GC pauses were starving the hedge timer).

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test -short ./...` passes (all 30 packages)
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./reputation/storage/...` passes (testcontainer-backed Redis tests)

author: elirap1
body:
## Summary

Audit of the tradingBot Python algorithmic trading system. Five fixes committed — one `AttributeError` that would crash every single trade execution, one misplaced try/except that left all state-load DB errors unhandled, one invalid escape sequence, one always-`None` dead branch, and leftover dead imports/constants. All 376 unit tests pass before and after.

## Fixes

- **fix(coordinator): use correct field name `score` not `composite_score`** — `coordinator.py:1159`
  `watcher.state.composite_score` does not exist on the `WatcherState` dataclass; the field is named `score`. This crashed with `AttributeError` on every position entry. Fixed to `watcher.state.score`.

- **fix(state): move DB operations inside try/except in `load_state()`** — `state.py:load_state()`
  All three DB calls (`get_watermarks`, `get_all_positions`, `get_state`) executed *before* the try block; the try/except only guarded the subsequent `log.info()`. Any SQLite error during state load would propagate unhandled, crashing `RiskManager.__init__` and `PortfolioManager.__init__`. Moved all DB operations inside the try so errors fall back to `dict(_DEFAULTS)`.

- **fix(live_trading): remove invalid escape sequence `\!`** — `live_trading.py:463`
  `"\-- not suitable..."` contained `\!`, generating a `DeprecationWarning` on every import (will become a `SyntaxError` in Python 3.12+). Removed the backslash.

- **fix(calendar): remove always-`None` dead branch** — `edge/market_calendar.py:120–121`
  `next_month = (...) if False else None` always evaluates to `None` and `next_month` is never referenced. Removed both lines.

- **fix(ml_model): remove unused import and dead constant; fix docstring feature count** — `ml_model.py`
  `import json` was unused; `FEATURE_FILE` was defined but never read or written. Both are leftover from a planned feature-logging path. Removed. Also corrected docstring strategy count from "8 features" to "9 features" to match `STRATEGY_NAMES`.

## Noticed but not fixed

| Location | Issue | Reason skipped |
|---|---|---|
| `profit_maximizer.py` | `ProfitMaximizer` class (~250 lines) never imported anywhere — entirely dead code | May be intentionally staged; removing it is a one-file delete but the decision should be deliberate |
| `live_trading.py` docstring/comments | References "Alpaca" throughout; runtime now routes to IB | Documentation inconsistency; no logic bug |
| `ml_model.py` | `STRATEGY_NAMES` (9) is a subset of `ALL_STRATEGIES` (13); 4 strategies silently contribute 0.0 to feature vector | Changing feature space would invalidate any trained model on disk; design decision |
| `walk_forward_optimizer.py:_fetch_all_data()` | Imports legacy Alpaca shim `DataFetcher`/`Broker`; optimizer uses Alpaca data even in IB deployments | Standalone backtest tool; wiring IB data is a larger architectural change |
| `ib_broker.py:387` | Log reads `parent_order.orderId` immediately after `placeOrder()` (async assignment); `parent_id` already in scope | Cosmetic; both reference same object in practice |

## TODOs left in code

None — `grep` for `TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX|BROKEN` returned zero results across the entire codebase.

body:
## Problema

Usuário reportou print de teste com `Erro PIX: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code`. Mensagem genérica esconde o motivo.

## Investigação

Reproduzido via curl direto à edge function: o erro real do PagBank é `whitelist access required. Contact PagSeguro` (HTTP 400). A conta PagBank ainda não tem permissão da Orders API.

O front estava chamando `db.functions.invoke()` que **não retorna o body em respostas 4xx/5xx** — apenas o erro genérico do SDK. Por isso o motivo real não aparecia.

## Fix

No `AdminPaymentTest.tsx`:
- `invokePagBankFn()` helper que usa `fetch` direto e parseia o body mesmo em status != 2xx
- `explainPagBankError()` detecta erro de whitelist e adiciona contato do PagBank (4002-4023)
- Aplicado em `generatePix()` e `chargeCard()`

## Resultado

Depois deste PR, ao tentar testar PIX/cartão sem whitelist:
```
❌ Erro PIX (HTTP 400): whitelist access required. Contact PagSeguro
→ A conta PagBank precisa ser liberada para a Orders API.
  Contato: 4002-4023 (PagBank Empresas) ou painel 'Atendimento'.
```

## Próximo passo (não-código)

Ligar pra **PagBank Empresas (4002-4023)** ou abrir ticket pedindo liberação da **Orders API**. Sem isso, nenhum pagamento real funciona — toda a infra está pronta.

author: brickfrog
body:
## Summary

Fixes the choir MCP startup race (`choir-kqv.12`) where `choir init [--recreate]` would silently fail to connect the choir MCP server in the launched Claude Code TL session. User had to manually run `/mcp` reconnect after every init.

## Root cause

`choir init` spawned `choir serve` and the claude TL tab as siblings (children of the same init parent), at essentially the same instant. The claude TL launcher passed `--mcp-config '{...}'` causing Claude Code to spawn `choir mcp-stdio` shortly after. That mcp-stdio child tried to connect to `.choir/server.sock` while `choir serve` may not have finished binding the UDS yet. With wait budget exhausted, mcp-stdio fell through to an unconfigured TCP fallback and exited 1. Claude Code saw the MCP child die and showed the server as disconnected. No error surfaced because `--stderr-append-log` was never passed.

## Fix (5 layers + audit-fixup)

| Layer | Change | Surface |
|---|---|---|
| A | `choir init` waits for `.choir/server.sock` before spawning the claude TL tab | `src/bin/choir/init.mbt` |
| B | `mcp-stdio` outer-retry the connect-handshake-loop with bounded backoff (3 attempts × ≤30s wait_for_socket + capped exponential sleep) | `src/bin/choir/mcp_mode.mbt` |
| C | Default `wait_tries` 60 (12s) → 150 (30s) | `src/bin/choir/mcp_mode.mbt` |
| D | Init launcher passes `--stderr-append-log` so failures aren't silent — applied to BOTH the init TL path AND every leaf claude path (`claude_mcp_args`), with per-agent log paths | `src/workspace/launch.mbt`, `src/workspace/workspace.mbt` |
| Audit-fixup | Per-agent stderr log path, fixed Exhausted/TCP semantics (no double error, clean exit), capped backoff, documented ~93s worst-case budget, dropped dead Bool return | various |

## Sarcasmotron audit (two rounds)

- **Round 1** found 5 actionable items: Layer D coverage gap on leaf claude agents, Exhausted/TCP semantics divergence between tests and production, unbounded backoff, undocumented worst-case budget, dead Bool return.
- **Audit-fixup leaf** (PR #290, server-automerged) addressed all 5 cleanly.
- **Round 2** verified all 5 closed and no regressions introduced. Sarcasmotron's verdict: "the leaf actually did the work. Approve."

## Test plan

- [x] `moon test --target native` 1144/1144 clean on integrated feature branch (1142 base + 2 new)
- [x] `moon build --target native --release` clean
- [x] Round-2 Sarcasmotron audit: 0 hard gates, 0 regressions, 0 new issues

## Follow-ups filed (not blocking)

Two P3 hygiene items deferred to separate beads under `choir-kqv` (north-star epic):
- Test coverage for `wait_for_socket=true` inner-retry branch + init wait-timeout continue branch
- Reconcile or document the 100/150/300 `wait_tries` triple

## Commits (oldest first)

```
4b740ae fix(init): sequence choir-serve before TL spawn; harden mcp-stdio startup
9daa792 fix(sys): name mcp startup sleep clamp
7a7ca29 fix(audit): extend stderr-log to leaf claude agents; fix Exhausted/TCP semantics
```

body:
## Why

`server/index.ts` started at **9141 lines / 212 routes**. It's the single biggest tech-debt in the repo: every PR risks merge conflicts, every review is a slog, and it's where most silent DE/EN bugs hide because the file is too big to scan visually.

This is the **first PR of an incremental split** — middleware/helpers first, then route groups one at a time.

## What this PR does

Four independently-verified commits, each a pure code-move with **no behavior change**:

### 1. `refactor(server): extract auth middleware to server/middleware/auth.ts`
- `authMiddleware`, `requireCompanyAccess`, `requireResourceAccess` (+ `ResourceType`, `resolveCompanyIdForResource`)
- `agentAuth`, `deriveAgentToken`
- Dropped the orphaned `(global as any).__deriveAgentToken` hack — written but never read
- Module reads `JWT_SECRET` from `process.env` at call time, no init-order coupling

### 2. `refactor(server): extract skills routes to ./routes/skills.ts`
- `mapSkillToDe` helper
- GET `/api/skills`, `/api/skills/categories`
- POST `/api/tasks/match-agent`
- GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE on `/api/companies/:id/skills-library` and `/api/skills-library/:id`
- POST `/api/companies/:id/skills-library/seed`
- GET/PATCH/DELETE on learned-skills
- The 590-line bilingual `SEED_SKILLS` data block moved to its own module `./db/seed-skills-data.ts`
- Dropped duplicated `requireResourceAccess('skillsLibrary'), requireResourceAccess('skillsLibrary')` and `requireCompanyAccess(), requireCompanyAccess()` middleware stacks — the doubles were dead code

### 3. `refactor(server): extract routines routes + activity-log helper`
- All routines + triggers + ausführungen endpoints
- `logAktivitaet` extracted to `./services/activity-log.ts` (multiple future routers will need it; reaches the WS broadcast via the existing appEvents bus)

### 4. `refactor(server): extract projects routes to ./routes/projects.ts`
- GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE on `/api/companies/:id/projects` and `/api/projects/:id`
- POST `/api/projects/:id/fortschritt-aktualisieren`
- Whiteboard endpoints stay in `index.ts` for now — they need `broadcastUpdate`. They'll move once that helper is converted to appEvents.

## Result

```
                                     before    after    delta
server/index.ts                       9141     7835    -1306  (-14.3%)
server/middleware/auth.ts             —        +279
server/routes/skills.ts               —        +296
server/routes/routines.ts             —        +219
server/routes/projects.ts             —        +120
server/db/seed-skills-data.ts         —        +603
server/services/activity-log.ts       —         +41
```

**Net out of the monolith: -1306 LOC**, plus a clear pattern for the rest.

## Verification

After every commit:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- Server boots
- One representative endpoint per group hit via curl, returns the expected payload (or auth-gate response)

## Next PRs (not in this one)

Each as a separate PR for reviewability:
- `routes/companies.ts` (~57 routes, will need its own bigger PR)
- `routes/agents.ts` (~36 routes, second-biggest)
- `routes/tasks.ts` (~18 routes)
- `routes/approvals.ts`, `routes/goals.ts`, `routes/plugins.ts`, `routes/palace.ts`, `routes/meetings.ts`, `routes/system.ts`
- Eventually convert `broadcastUpdate` to appEvents so whiteboard + a few stragglers can move too

**Endgame:** `server/index.ts` from 9141 down to ~150 lines (just app setup + router mounting).

author: barriosnahuel
body:
### Summary
- `kotlin.assert(cond) { msg }` is a no-op without JVM `-ea`. Across the test sources we had 8 call-sites — at least one (`EXTERNAL_LEGAL_ITEMS = 3`) silently masked a stale count after Terms of Service shipped (the constant should have been 4)
- Added an inline CircleCI `test-assertion-guard` job (mirrors `analytics-wrapper-guard`) that fails the build if any `*.kt` under `**/src/test/**` or `**/src/androidTest/**` contains a bare `assert(`
- Migrated the 8 existing offenders to the existing convention in each file: `assertCountEquals(...)` (Compose UI Test, 6 sites), `assertEquals(...)` collapsed into a no-op block (1 site — see review tip), and a same-shape regex-clean rewrite. Bumped `EXTERNAL_LEGAL_ITEMS` 3→4
- Documented the rule in `CLAUDE.md` § Test assertions with the local-grep equivalent of the CI check

### Code review tips
- `AddButtonCreateFlowTest.createModeWithoutUriFinishesImmediately` deserves attention. The original `kotlin.assert(scenario.state == DESTROYED)` was provably a no-op — replacing it with `assertEquals` (which actually evaluates `scenario.state`) crashed the runner, because reading state on a finished-in-onCreate `ActivityScenario` triggers `runOnMainSync` into a process that's already winding down. Rather than fight the API, the test now only verifies that `launch` + `close` complete without throwing — same effective coverage as the no-op assert had been providing all along, just honest about it. Comment in the test explains the why
- `EXTERNAL_LEGAL_ITEMS = 4` matches `LegalAndPrivacySection.kt`'s 4 external rows (Privacy Policy, Data Safety, Terms of Service, Source); the License row is in-app, no `app_about_open_in_browser` hint
- The CircleCI job uses POSIX-portable ERE: `(^|[^[:alnum:]_])assert[[:space:]]*\(`. Word-boundary alternative (`\b`) was avoided for BSD-grep compatibility on contributor machines. Verified zero false positives against `assertThat`, `assertEquals`, `assertCountEquals`, etc. — all of those have non-whitespace between `assert` and `(`
- The job is wired both as a top-level `Pull Requests Workflow` job and as a `requires:` of `bundle`, same as `analytics-wrapper-guard`

### Already tested
- [x] `./gradlew check -x test` — green
- [x] `./gradlew test` — green
- [x] Guard regex on a clean tree returns 0 hits
- [x] Instrumented suite (cold-booted AVD `Android_14_API_34`): 7 of 8 touched tests verified green — `homeDeeplinkLandsOnHomeTab`, `unknownPathDeeplinkFallsBackToHome`, `exploreDeeplinkWithBundledLandsOnExploreTab`, `tapCreditsRowExpandsSectionWithAiAttributionCards`, `externalLegalItemsExposeOpensInBrowserHint` (count fix verified), `createModeWithoutUriFinishesImmediately` (post-fix), `swipeLeftOnBundledCardDoesNotPinOrRemove` reproduces a "Process crashed" on plain develop too — pre-existing AVD-only flake, not introduced here. `exploreDeeplinkWithoutBundledFallsBackToHome` skipped via `assumeFalse` (depends on bundled audio dir being empty)

## Summary

### 1. BSVibe public demo stack automation

Previously only removed compose containers (and prompted for volumes), letting images/networks/dangling volumes accumulate — caused 350GB+ of bloat in `~/.colima` over time.

author: himanshu4141
body:
## Summary
- Global `QueryCache` + `MutationCache` onError handler that signs the user out when any query / mutation rejects with an auth-dead error (revoked Google token, expired JWT, 401 from PostgREST, etc.). The existing `AuthGate` then redirects them to `/auth`. Without this, a session that goes invalid mid-use leaves the user staring at error toasts on every screen until they manually sign out.
- New `src/lib/authError.ts::isAuthSessionInvalidError` covers the four shapes Supabase clients can throw: AuthError/AuthApiError with HTTP 401 or 403, PostgREST `code: PGRST301` (JWT expired) / `PGRST302` (anonymous-role disallowed), generic `{ status: 401 }` objects (edge-function invoke errors), and `Error` messages containing "JWT expired" / "invalid_grant" as a string fallback.
- Single-flight signOut: when 50 in-flight queries all 401 simultaneously (the realistic scenario when refresh fails), only one `supabase.auth.signOut()` runs. The guard clears 5 seconds later so a fresh re-login can still trigger a future invalidation.
- Auth-dead errors skip retry so the handler fires immediately instead of after two failed retries (existing default).
- Emits a single `auth_session_invalidated` PostHog event so we can see how often this fires in production — useful signal if Google revocations spike.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx jest src/lib/__tests__/authError.test.ts` — 15 tests pass — **Validated by Claude**
- [x] `npx jest src/lib/__tests__/queryClient.test.ts` — 6 integration tests pass (single-flight, 401, JWT-expired, mutation, no-retry, no-op for unrelated errors) — **Validated by Claude**
- [x] `npx jest --coverage --collectCoverageFrom='src/lib/authError.ts' --collectCoverageFrom='src/lib/queryClient.ts'` — 100% on authError, 95% on queryClient — **Validated by Claude**
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — zero errors — **Validated by Claude**
- [x] `npm run lint` — zero warnings — **Validated by Claude**
- [ ] Reproduce on DEV: revoke Google access from accounts.google.com, return to the app, observe redirect to /auth within one query cycle — **Requires manual verification**
- [ ] Confirm normal sign-out still works (the handler shouldn't loop on the signOut-induced session-null state) — **Requires manual verification**

author: eccentric-jamaican
body:
## Summary

- Add an Android Storage setting for image preview history with three modes: Storage saver, Small previews, and Larger previews.
- Apply the selected retention policy to newly sent image attachments before they enter the visible timeline, while keeping the original prepared payload for the turn request.
- Show a clear "Image received by Codex!" fallback for elided history images instead of a broken-image-only state.
- Keep persisted history storage-bounded by stripping full image payloads unless a compressed larger preview is selected.

## Root cause

Bridge history can replace inline image data with an elided reference to avoid storing and relaying large image payloads. Android treated that reference like a renderable image source, so old sent images could appear as broken previews. The first live-timeline approach also only enforced retention during persistence, so newly sent images could still open the larger in-memory payload even when Small previews was selected.

## Validation

- Ran `cd android; .\gradlew.bat :app:compileDebugKotlin` successfully.
- Manually tested on a Samsung Galaxy Note 10 with Storage saver, Small previews, and Larger previews.
- Confirmed Small previews opens a lower-detail retained preview, Larger previews opens a clearer compressed preview, and storage-saver/elided images show the fallback message.

body:
## Summary

Three operator-explicit asks landed in one PR — all root-cause fixes, no workarounds:

1. **Audit-r8 brief #07 — model leak root cause.** `BrainState.init` now registers `self.provider_catalog` as the process-wide `providers.catalog._SHARED` singleton BEFORE `LLMProvider()` is constructed. Without this, `_default_model_for` consulted a lazily-built empty catalog whose `default_model_for(provider)` returned \`\"\"`, and the failover quietly fell back to the persisted/env model id — which is how the dated-transcribe id kept leaking into chat completions despite a clean settings.json + boot self-heal + classifier fix. Wire-level guard removed (it was a workaround for this). `await` added to the `switch_provider` call in `/api/config/update` (was fire-and-forget, leaving in-memory state drifted from settings.json until next boot).
2. **Audit-r8 brief #08 HIGH — pre-release readiness.** `_build_morning_briefing` now applies the same `_FRESH_WINDOW_S = 120s` gate the `_evaluate` path got in 2026.5.18 — stale Apple HealthKit reads are no longer verbalised. `realtime_proxy._handle_transcript` node-path now uses `is_partial: not is_final` (was hardcoded `False`, contradicting the web path, causing iOS to render partial deltas as committed text).
3. **Audit-r8 brief #02 — CI gating.** `ci.yml` and `version-coherence.yml` no longer gate `pull_request:` on `branches: [main]`. Stacked PRs (PR into a phase-N branch) used to skip the full suite — only `lint` ran (no `if:` guard). Operator caught this on PR #81 / PR #84.

body:
## Summary

- **Arrivals row** restructured to mirror the PWA: `[28px route badge] [headsign / status] .... [wall time / countdown]`. Route icon bumped 24→28px. Status labels shortened to transit-board glyphs (`ON TIME`, `+N MIN`, `SCHED.`, `CANCELED`).
- **Live countdown** — new `format.c/h` helpers derive both wall-clock (`5:42p` / `17:42`) and countdown (`3 MIN`, `NOW`, `GONE`, `1h 12m`) from raw backend fields. A `MINUTE_UNIT` tick handler re-renders countdowns independently of the 30-300s data poll.
- **Protocol change (v1.1, breaking)** — pkjs forwards raw `mins` (u16 BE) + `st` (s8) instead of pre-formatted strings. `ArrivalEntry` drops `time[10]`/`label[20]`, gains `uint16_t mins` + `int8_t st`. Saves ~24 bytes per entry. Watch and pkjs must be updated together.
- **Editorial departures board aesthetic** across all screens — 2px solid black header rule, 1px black row dividers, all `GColorDarkGray` replaced with black. Styled headers added to station picker, route picker, edit-favorites, and settings.
- **Home subtitle** now shows `"Next: 5:42p · 3 MIN"` with live tick, replacing `"Next: H:MM AM/PM (Route)"`.

body:
## Summary
- Start YouTube extraction and voice join concurrently for direct URL playback, matching the faster Bilibili path.
- Add YouTube direct playback timing logs for extraction, voice join, queue add, playback start, and total time.
- Keep the YouTube rate limiter intact, while switching yt-dlp to an audio-first low-bandwidth fallback selector so it does not fall back to heavy 1080p combined streams when audio-only formats are missing.

## Root Cause
YouTube direct URL playback was still serialized: yt-dlp extraction completed before the bot attempted to join voice and queue/start playback. The old `bestaudio/best` selector could also fall back to a large combined video stream, making FFmpeg startup feel slower even after extraction finished.

**Bug:** `_run_agent_task` line 517 called `working_memory.append(step_summary)` with one arg, but `append()` requires `(step, result)` — two positional args.

**Root cause:** `compress_step_result()` returns a single summary string. The call site didn't unpack it into the step ID + result that `append()` expects.

**Fix:** `working_memory.append(outcome.step.id, step_summary)`

**Impact:** Crashed every agent task (`/plan`) on real hardware. 147/147 tests still pass.

**Discovered during:** First smoke test on USB shard hardware (2026-05-10).

author: halsk
body:
## Summary

Redesigns the AST chunk extraction logic from text-node level (0.2.x) to paragraph level (0.3.0).

### Root Cause

The 0.2.4 L2 chunk used raw AST text node extraction, splitting inline_code/emphasis boundaries. This caused LLM context loss → EN/JA mix / duplicate phrases / semantic inversion (17 issues found in cmd_443 PR#210).

**Example** — `"When \`AUTH_ENABLED=true\`, a token is required."` was split into:
- chunk1: `"When "`
- chunk2: `", a token is required."`
→ LLM had no context for each fragment → mixing

### Changes

- **`extractTextNodes()` removed** → replaced by `extractBlockNodes()`: paragraph-level extraction preserving inline markup (inline code, bold, italic, links) as whole units
- **`DEFAULT_MAX_NODES_PER_BATCH` removed** → `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_BATCH = 4000`: token-count-based batching (`chars / 4` approximation)
- **`maxNodesPerBatch` option renamed** → `maxTokensPerBatch` in `TranslateOptions`, `BatchTranslateOptions`, CLI (`--max-tokens-per-batch`)
- **System prompts updated**: explicit instructions to preserve inline markdown formatting and treat each block as an independent paragraph-level unit
- **LLM output re-parsed**: translated markdown re-processed through remark (`applyTranslation` closure per block, updates `node.children` in-place)

### Test Coverage

- 262 tests pass, 0 skip
- New test: paragraph-level inline code preservation (whole sentence as one segment)
- Batch splitting tests updated for token-based logic

Part of cmd_453 (yuuhitsu 0.3.0). Part B (Local QC dogfood) depends on this PR being merged first.

body: ## Summary - Closes the wildcard-cert gap flagged in #179. Self-serve workspace claims now register `.narraterx.ai` on the shared `narraterx` Vercel project via the Vercel REST API, so per-domain certs issue automatically (no more manual "add the domain in the Vercel UI when an email comes in"). - Hard-fail with full rollback when Vercel rejects: workspace row deleted, Clerk org deleted. A workspace whose subdomain doesn't resolve is worse than none. - The wizard's "Setting up your workspace…" loader now actively probes the new subdomain (no-CORS favicon `` request) and only redirects once SSL handshake succeeds — up to 30s, with a manual-continue link after 25s. > **Stacked on #179.** Base is `claude/eager-bell-1c1ac5`. Merge #179 first, or rebase onto main after #179 lands. ## Required env vars (paste before merge) Set these on the `narraterx` Vercel project. Per memory `feedback_env_var_division_of_labor.md`, sensitive values go via the Vercel dashboard. | Variable | Tier | Notes | |---|---|---| | `VERCEL_TOKEN` | **Sensitive** | Vercel personal/integration token with `project:write` scope | | `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` | Mildly sensitive | The `narraterx` Vercel project's ID | | `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` | Mildly sensitive | Only if the project lives inside a Vercel Team | If any of these are missing, `claim.js` logs a warning and skips the registration step (dev-friendly fallback) — production will need them set. ### 1Password entry for `VERCEL_TOKEN` | Field | Value | |---|---| | **Item type** | API Credential | | **Title** | `NarrateRx — VERCEL_TOKEN` | | **Vault** | The vault holding your other narraterx production keys | | **Password / Value** | (paste the token after generating in Vercel → Account Settings → Tokens) | | **Website** | https://vercel.com/account/tokens | | **Notes** | Vercel personal access token used by `api/onboarding/claim.js` to register `.narraterx.ai` on the shared narraterx project at workspace-claim time. Scope: `project:write`. Lose this and self-serve onboarding's domain-registration step will start returning 502 / `domain-registration-failed`. To rotate: create a new token in Vercel, paste here + into Vercel env vars, then revoke the old one. Generated YYYY-MM-DD. | ## DNS assumption Adding a domain in Vercel is independent of DNS resolution. This PR assumes Cloudflare has either a wildcard CNAME `*.narraterx.ai → cname.vercel-dns.com` or per-subdomain CNAMEs already in place. If DNS isn't resolving the new subdomain, Vercel still accepts the domain registration (200) but cert issuance hangs until DNS is fixed; the wizard's SSL probe will time out at 30s and surface a manual-continue link. If you don't have a wildcard CNAME today, the cleanest fix is to add one in Cloudflare: - **Type:** CNAME - **Name:** `*` - **Target:** `cname.vercel-dns.com` - **Proxy:** DNS only (gray cloud) — Vercel needs the bare CNAME for cert challenges That's a one-time setup; per-tenant DNS becomes zero work. ## Files | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `api/_lib/vercelDomains.js` | `addProjectDomain` / `removeProjectDomain` REST helpers; idempotent on already-attached | | `api/onboarding/claim.js` | Calls `addProjectDomain` after the workspace row is inserted; rolls back DB + Clerk on failure | | `src/pages/Onboarding.jsx` | Active SSL probe in the launching screen + new error copy for `domain-registration-failed` | ## Test plan - [ ] Set `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` (and optionally `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`) on the `narraterx` Vercel project - [ ] Verify Cloudflare wildcard CNAME `*.narraterx.ai → cname.vercel-dns.com` (or that per-subdomain CNAMEs are in place) - [ ] After #179 + this PR are merged + deployed, run a self-serve onboarding from `narraterx.ai/onboard` end to end - [ ] Confirm `.narraterx.ai` appears in the Vercel project's Domains tab within ~10s of submit - [ ] Confirm the launching screen's SSL probe waits for cert and redirects automatically once ready - [ ] (Negative) temporarily unset `VERCEL_TOKEN` on a preview deployment, run onboarding, confirm warning is logged and claim still succeeds (dev fallback) - [ ] (Negative) submit a slug with a `VERCEL_TOKEN` that has insufficient scope, confirm rollback: no workspace row, no Clerk org left behind, error surfaced in Review step 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: cbeaulieu-gt
body:
## Summary

Adds `push: branches: [main]` to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers so the CI status badge added in #334 has `head_branch=main` runs to report on.

## Why the badge was empty

shields.io filters workflow runs by `?branch=main`, which under the hood matches `head_branch`. PR-triggered runs have `head_branch = <source-branch>`, never `main`. With `ci.yml` triggering only on `pull_request`, there were zero matching runs — confirmed via:

```
$ gh api 'repos/glitchwerks/siege-web/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main'
{ "total_count": 0, "workflow_runs": [] }
```

## Why a push trigger is the right fix

- **Accurate badge**: one run per merge into main, so the badge always reflects the current state of `main`.
- **PR-pair race-condition net**: catches the case where two PRs each pass individually but break together after both merge — a real failure mode the PR-only trigger misses.
- **Concurrency safe**: existing `concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}` already handles `push` events correctly (`head_ref` is empty → falls back to `run_id`, so each push gets its own group with no cancellation).

## Cost

~1 extra CI run per merged PR. Single-digit minutes of runner time per merge.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this PR (the workflow itself parses cleanly)
- [ ] After merge, `gh api 'repos/.../runs?branch=main'` returns at least one run
- [ ] Badge in README renders with passing/failing status, not "no status"

Closes #336

author: espadonne
body:
## Summary
Two follow-ups to PR #12 found while mirroring AIDE onto the live shithub-app droplet:

1. **`shithub-aide-check`**: AIDE 0.18 (Ubuntu 24's package) requires `--config` explicitly — the binary refuses to pick up `/etc/aide/aide.conf` implicitly. Without it, every nightly run errors out with `ERROR: missing configuration` and exits 17. Patched the wrapper to pass `--config=/etc/aide/aide.conf`, the same path `aideinit` and the upstream `dailyaidecheck` use.
2. **`aide.yml`** task: `creates: /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz` is wrong on Ubuntu 24 — the shipped `/etc/aide/aide.conf` writes the DB uncompressed at `/var/lib/aide/aide.db`. The bug was idempotency-only (the next ansible run would re-invoke `aideinit -y -f`, which is harmless because of `-f`, but causes a 7-minute reinit on every play). Fixed to `creates: /var/lib/aide/aide.db`.

Verified against the live droplet:
- Original wrapper: `rc=17` and "ERROR: missing configuration"
- Patched wrapper: `aide --check` runs against the just-built baseline.

## Test plan
- [x] Wrapper rc=17 reproduced before fix
- [ ] Wrapper rc=0 after fix on a clean baseline (verifying live as this PR is up)
- [ ] `creates:` path matches the actual artifact (already true on live droplet)
