author: ness001
body:
## Summary `ToolCallBlock` is a disclosure widget — a button that toggles a region of input/output JSON open and closed. The button declared `aria-expanded` (so screen readers announce \"collapsed\" / \"expanded\"), but had **no `aria-controls`**, so the user got no signal about *which region* the toggle controls. With several tool-call blocks rendered on a single conversation page, that ambiguity is the whole point of `aria-controls` — it disambiguates which collapsed region just appeared on the page. ## The bug `src/components/conversation/ToolCallBlock.tsx` (pre-fix): ```tsx {open && (
…
// no id, so couldn't be referenced anyway )} ``` WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/): \"The element that shows and hides the content has role button. … When the controlled content is visible, the element with role button has `aria-expanded` set to true. … `aria-controls` referencing the controlled region is recommended.\" WCAG mappings: **1.3.1 Info and Relationships** (the programmatic relationship between the toggle and its panel must be exposed) and **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (the toggle's value/state must be exposed including its target). ## The fix ```tsx const bodyId = useId(); … {open &&
…
} ``` `React.useId()` was chosen specifically so two ToolCallBlocks rendered on the same page get distinct ids (a hard-coded string would collide). The id is generated even when the body is not rendered — this is fine and standard, since `aria-controls` may legitimately reference a not-yet-mounted region per ARIA. ## Tests `tests/components/conversation/messages.test.tsx` — 2 new cases (now 6 in the `ToolCallBlock` suite, file total 21): 1. **id ↔ aria-controls match** — render one block, click to expand, assert `body.id === toggle.getAttribute('aria-controls')`. 2. **collision-free across instances** — render two blocks side by side, assert their `aria-controls` values are both truthy and distinct. ## Verification - `npx vitest run tests/components/conversation/messages.test.tsx` — **21/21 pass** (was 19; +2 new) - `npx vitest run` — **405/405 pass** across the full suite, no failures, no skips - `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean ## Scope - Surgical: 4 lines added in component (`useId` import, `useId()` call, `aria-controls` attr, `id` attr) plus the two tests. - No behavior change for sighted users. - No existing test broken. - No new deps; `useId` ships with React 18+. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body: Fecha dois achados da auditoria de segurança ([SECURITY_AUDIT.md](SECURITY_AUDIT.md)) e remove os dois do relatório. ## 1. Defesa em profundidade nos drops Liquid \`ContactDrop\` e \`UserDrop\` agora passam os campos controlados pelo cliente (\`name\`, \`email\`, \`phone_number\`, valores string em \`custom_attributes\`) por um pipeline Loofah \`:prune\` + \`:strip\` antes de expor ao Liquid: - Tags perigosas (\`\` vira string vazia, não \`alert(1)\`. - Tags benignas (\`\`, \`\`) têm o wrapper retirado e o texto preservado. - Caracteres legítimos como \`&\`, \`<3\` e unicode passam intactos, evitando que o destinatário do WhatsApp receba \`Mary & John\` no lugar de \`Mary & John\`. Mesmo que o sanitizer do front (\`MessageFormatter\` no agent UI) tenha uma regressão, um nome de contato como \`Maria \` deixa de carregar payload executável. ## 2. Bloqueio de etiquetas protegidas para todos os perfis \`prevent_protected_label_modification\` antes só barrava \`manager?\` — administradores conseguiam editar/apagar \`agente-off\` e \`kb-*\` pela API. Isso quebrava o contrato de IA on/off que essas etiquetas representam, e expunha um vetor de quebra silenciosa de invariante operacional. Agora o filtro vale pra **todos os perfis**, incluindo administrator. ## How to test 1. Rails console: \`ContactDrop.new(Contact.new(name: 'Maria Silva')).name\` → \`'Maria Silva'\` (sem o tag). 2. Rails console: \`ContactDrop.new(Contact.new(name: 'Mary & John')).name\` → \`'Mary & John'\` (preserva \`&\`). 3. Como administrator, \`PATCH /api/v1/accounts/:id/labels/:agente_off_label_id\` retorna \`401\`. Mesmo \`DELETE\` também. 4. Como administrator, \`PATCH /api/v1/accounts/:id/labels/:cliente_label_id\` continua \`200\` (etiquetas comuns intactas). ## What changed - \`app/drops/contact_drop.rb\`: \`sanitize_text\` privado usando Loofah; \`name\`, \`email\`, \`phone\`, \`phone_number\`, \`custom_attribute\` valores de string passam pelo sanitize. \`first_name\`/\`last_name\` derivam do nome já saneado. - \`app/drops/user_drop.rb\`: mesma lógica em \`name\`, \`email\`, \`available_name\`. - \`app/controllers/api/v1/accounts/labels_controller.rb\`: removida a checagem \`return unless Current.account_user&.manager?\` em \`prevent_protected_label_modification\`. Comentário documentando o porquê. - \`spec/drops/contact_drop_spec.rb\` + \`spec/drops/user_drop_spec.rb\`: novos testes pra script tag (conteúdo interno também removido), tags inline (wrapper removido, texto preservado), \`&\` e unicode preservados, \`first_name\`/\`last_name\` derivam de valor saneado, custom_attribute também. - \`spec/controllers/api/v1/accounts/labels_controller_spec.rb\`: novos testes garantindo que admin não modifica/deleta \`agente-off\` nem \`kb-*\` mas mantém poder sobre etiquetas regulares. - \`SECURITY_AUDIT.md\`: dois findings removidos, contagem atualizada (MÉDIO 5→4, BAIXO 3→2).

author: n-ichimura
body:
## Summary

- Phase 8b of [`docs/plans/annot-html-document.md`](https://github.com/ingcreators/annot/blob/main/docs/plans/annot-html-document.md) — second row of the templates-mechanism phase. Pairs with Phase 8a's `cloneTemplate` (the READ side); this lands the WRITE side: a modal that collects template metadata + a doc-mode header button that stamps the current document and persists it under `Templates/<name>.annot.html`.
- New `showSaveAsTemplateDialog(opts?)` helper in `@ingcreators/annot-host-ui/ui/save-as-template-dialog`. Three field inputs (name / description / tags) on `<annot-dialog>` chrome.
- New "Save as template…" button in the doc-mode header (alongside back / save-status). On OK it stamps `meta.template = {name, description?, tags}` on a clone of the live doc, serialises (the marker-aware serializer auto-emits the three template markers), and calls `storage.saveDocument({folderPath: "Templates", …}, {filename: ${name}.annot.html})`.

## Editor session unaffected

The live document + its debounced save lifecycle are not mutated by this action. Only a new file is written under `Templates/`. The user can keep editing immediately afterwards without losing context.

## Validation

- `name` is required (trimmed); empty submit shows an inline error.
- `name` cannot contain `/`, `\`, or `..` — the save path is `Templates/${name}.annot.html`, and any of those would let the user escape `Templates/`. Explicit reject (rather than silent sanitise) so the failure mode is visible.
- Tags are comma-split, whitespace-trimmed, empty entries dropped.
- Description is omitted from the resolved value when blank after `.trim()` (so the eventual `meta.template.description` field is genuinely absent rather than an empty string).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r typecheck` — clean across all 11 packages.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 2083 tests pass (145 files), including 10 new `showSaveAsTemplateDialog` cases:
  - OK resolves with all three fields populated
  - Cancel resolves null
  - trim-and-drop tag handling (consecutive commas, trailing comma)
  - blank-description omission from result
  - empty-name reject + retry happy path
  - path-separator reject (`/`, `\`, `..`)
  - error clearing on `input` event
  - Enter-to-submit on the name input
  - DOM removal on resolve
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (27 pre-existing warnings, unchanged).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-web build` — clean.

## Manual smoke checklist

- [ ] Open a `.annot.html` doc → header shows "Save as template…" button.
- [ ] Click → dialog opens prefilled with the current title.
- [ ] OK → file appears under `Templates/<name>.annot.html`; live editor unchanged; status bar still says "saved" (no `pending` flash).
- [ ] Re-save with the same name → backend uniquifies (`<name> (2).annot.html`).

## Next phases (8c / 8d)

- **Phase 8c** — `<annot-template-picker>` host-ui component (user-templates section + recently-used chips; built-in section stubbed for Phase 9).
- **Phase 8d** — File-manager "New" split button (default "New blank document"; flyout "From template…").

Greptile Summary

author: torsday
body:
## Summary

- Adds `scripts/board-mutate.sh <verb> <ITEM_ID> <value>` — single-item Project v2 field mutator with mandatory round-trip verification per `~/.claude/skills/shared/status-transition.md`.
- Verbs: `flip-status`, `set-priority`, `set-size`, `set-phase`, `set-risk`, `set-model-queue` (case-insensitive values, canonical lower-case-with-hyphens).
- Distinct exit codes (`0/2/3/4/5/6/7`) so callers can distinguish usage error, missing constants, unknown verb/value, mutation failure, and verification failure.
- Smoke tests in `tests/scripts/board-mutate.test.ts` mock `gh` via a PATH shim — exercise every verb's success path plus each failure-mode exit code (32 cases, all green).

## Design link

Implements [#847 — feat(scripts): generalize set-ready-status.sh into scripts/board-mutate.sh](https://github.com/torsday/omnifocus-mcp/issues/847). Sub-issue of #804.

Closes #847

## Breaking change?

- [x] No

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests cover happy + edge + error (32 cases — verb resolution, arg validation, missing constants, mutation/verify failures)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` are green locally (3572 passed, 59 skipped, 0 failed)
- [x] Self-reviewed via /review-pr
- [x] No new dependencies

## Scope notes — partial AC; follow-ups intended

The issue's AC has 8 items. This PR delivers the core script + tests. Three items are intentionally out of scope; none block the value of the wrapper itself, but follow-ups should be filed to cover them:

1. **`set-ready-status.sh` → thin wrapper conversion (AC item 5).** The current `set-ready-status.sh` is a *bulk-bootstrap* script — it iterates every project item and flips each to Up Next or Backlog based on a hardcoded `UNBLOCKED_NUMBERS` array. It does not accept a single item ID. Converting it to ``board-mutate.sh flip-status \$1 up-next`` would silently break its bulk semantics. Recommend a follow-up to either retire the bulk script (it appears to be a one-off) or rename it to ``bootstrap-status.sh`` for clarity, then optionally add a separate thin alias if a single-item ``set-ready-status`` entry point is wanted.

2. **Skill call-site updates (AC item 6).** Skills live at `~/.claude/skills/` and are not tracked in this repo (per CLAUDE.md). Updating call-sites in `/ship-next`, `/groom`, `/ship-debug`, `/ship-refactor`, `/hunt-bugs` is a separate, local-only edit pass — orthogonal to landing the script itself.

3. **`scripts/README.md` listing (AC item 8).** That file does not exist on `main` yet; #829 is the in-flight PR that creates it. Once #829 lands, a one-liner can be appended either as part of #829 or as a follow-up.

## Tension worth flagging

`~/.claude/skills/shared/status-transition.md` explicitly argues *against* abstracting board flips behind a helper — the prior helper-comment pattern caused silent drift when the LLM didn't translate the comment into actual code. The wrapper here is a different failure mode (an actual subprocess invocation, not a comment placeholder), but the trade-off is real and deserves a `/groom` pass before mass-converting skills. Recommend trying the wrapper at one or two call-sites first, observing for one cycle, then expanding if no drift surfaces.

## Conventions checklist

- [x] Follows project conventions in `AGENTS.md`
- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] No new dependency
- [x] Docs are inline in the script's `--help` and the test file's header docstring (no public-surface docs change)

author: xarmian
body:
## Summary Adds an **authoring-honesty** feature for HTML blocks (PLAN-1322): when the user pastes / types raw HTML containing content that's invisible (or near-invisible) to humans but readable by LLMs / agents, surface a non-blocking warning pill above the block. Click to expand an inspector listing each hidden segment with the rule that flagged it plus a snippet for context. \"Dismiss for this block\" button persists acknowledgement via a sentinel HTML comment marker. **Not a security control.** Render-time sanitization (`sanitizeHtmlBlock`, TASK-1323) protects browsers from XSS. This protects authors from unconsciously shipping content that looks one way to humans and reads another to agents — common with copy-pasted HTML blobs containing steganography channels (`display:none` divs, white-on-white text, `font-size:0`, hidden HTML comments, off-screen positioning, suspiciously long `aria-label` / `alt` / `title` values). ## Detector heuristics | Rule | Trigger | |---|---| | `display:none` | inline style | | `visibility:hidden` | inline style | | `opacity:0` / `0%` / `0.0` | inline style | | `font-size:<6px` | inline style with px value | | `color === background-color` | inline style; normalised match | | `position:absolute/fixed + left/right/top/bottom <= -9000px` | inline style | | `transform translate` to off-screen | regex heuristic on translate values | | `width:0 AND height:0` | inline style | | `clip:rect(0,0,0,0)` | inline style | | HTML comments | except the Pad-internal `` marker | | Suspicious `aria-label` / `alt` / `title` | length > 200 chars OR contains newlines | Class-based hiding (e.g. `.sr-only`) is **not** flagged — resolving it requires stylesheet context we don't have, and false-positives would be high. The detector stays conservative. ## Files - **NEW** `web/src/lib/utils/hiddenContentDetector.ts` — pure function `detectHiddenContent(html): HiddenSegment[]` plus `isHiddenContentAcknowledged` / `setHiddenContentAcknowledged` helpers + the marker constant. Uses `DOMParser` to walk the tree. - **MODIFIED** `web/src/lib/components/editor/extensions/htmlBlock.ts` — NodeView gets a warning pill (above preview) and an inspector panel (below source). `updateWarning()` runs on every `renderPreview` call so the warning tracks `attrs.html` changes live. - **MODIFIED** `web/src/lib/components/editor/Editor.svelte` — CSS for the warning pill (orange-tinted) and inspector panel (segments list + dismiss button), placed after the existing `.html-block-done-btn:hover` rule using the same `:global` pattern. ## Test plan - [x] `cd web && npm run check` — 0 errors - [x] `cd web && npm run build` — clean - [x] No regression to existing htmlBlock UX: preview / source / insertion / sanitization paths unchanged - [ ] Manual smoke: paste `
secret
` into a block → warning appears; click pill → inspector lists segment; click dismiss → warning disappears; reload page → warning still dismissed (marker persists in storage) ## Out of scope - Class-based hiding detection - Auto-stripping hidden content - Detection in non-HTML-block content - TASK-1328 (diff view collapse) — separate PR

author: mrandhawa14
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs left **anime downloads stuck at 0%** with **no error visible to the user**. The download row spawned, an empty episode-named folder appeared on disk, and the spinner ran forever. Manga downloads from sources with clean MP4/JPG URLs (Asura Scans, MangaDex, etc.) were unaffected, which is why this slipped through.

Fixed by two surgical changes in two files. Both bugs reproduce end-to-end on AnimeGG; both are general (not source-specific).

## The two bugs

### 1. `isMediaVideo()` rejects URLs with query strings

`lib/utils/extensions/string_extensions.dart` — `isMediaVideo()` did a plain `endsWith` against the **full URL string**:

```dart
return [...].any((extension) => toLowerCase().endsWith(extension));
```

Many sources return stream URLs shaped like:

```
https://www.animegg.org/play/75460/video.mp4?for=101778365476299
```

The trailing `?for=…` query string defeats the suffix match — `isMediaVideo()` returns `false` for a URL that genuinely is an MP4. In `downloadChapter` (`lib/modules/manga/download/providers/download_provider.dart`), this means **both** filters return empty:

```dart
final m3u8Urls = value.$1.where(... .endsWith(".m3u8") ...).toList();
final nonM3u8Urls = value.$1.where((e) => e.originalUrl.isMediaVideo()).toList();
...
if (videosUrls.isNotEmpty) { ... isOk = true; }
```

`isOk` stays `false`, and the surrounding loop:

```dart
await Future.doWhile(() async {
  await Future.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 1));
  if (isOk == true) return false;
  return true;
});
```

waits forever. `MDownloader` is **never constructed**. No error is raised because there's no error path for "extension returned 0 playable URLs" — the function just polls. The outer `} catch (_) { keepAlive.close(); }` would have hidden it anyway.

**Fix** (this PR):

```dart
final lower = (Uri.tryParse(this)?.path ?? this).toLowerCase();
return const [...].any((ext) => lower.endsWith(".$ext"));
```

Two adjustments:
- Match against the URL **path only** (`Uri.tryParse(this)?.path`), so `?…` and `#…` cannot defeat the check.
- Require a leading dot in the suffix (`.mp4` not `mp4`), so a URL ending in e.g. `flashmp4` cannot accidentally pass — a latent bug in the original code.

### 2. `_downloadFile` rejects HTTP 206 Partial Content

`lib/services/download_manager/download_isolate_pool.dart` — once a URL passes the filter, the anime branch of `_downloadFile` opens a streaming request:

```dart
StreamedResponse response = await client.send(request);
if (response.statusCode != 200) {
  throw DownloadPoolException('Failed to download file: …');
}
```

When the source extension sets `Range: bytes=0-` on the request (AnimeGG's extension does this; many others do too), the server **correctly** responds with **HTTP 206 Partial Content** — that's the literal definition of an honored range request. The check rejects it as non-200, throws, retries 3×, and ultimately surfaces the throw — but the throw is masked by the outer `} catch (_) { keepAlive.close(); }` in `downloadChapter` (`lib/modules/manga/download/providers/download_provider.dart`), so the user only sees a forever-spinner.

**Fix** (this PR):

```dart
if (response.statusCode < 200 || response.statusCode >= 300) {
  throw DownloadPoolException(
    'Failed to download file: ${pageUrl.fileName!} '
    '(status ${response.statusCode})',
  );
}
```

Same fix applied to `_downloadSegment` for HLS segment fetches (HLS hosts also commonly return 206 to a ranged segment GET).

## Files

```
lib/utils/extensions/string_extensions.dart             |  8 ++++++--
lib/services/download_manager/download_isolate_pool.dart| 17 +++++++++++++----
2 files changed, 19 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
```

No platform-specific code. No new dependencies. No behavior change for any URL that already passed both predicates.

## Reproduction

- **Source:** AnimeGG (en) — install via Mangayomi extensions
- **Episode:** any. Examples used in testing:
  - Toriko Episode 147 — 65,026,283 bytes
  - Gintama Episode 39 — 40,499,317 bytes
  - Grand Blue Episode 12 — 180,478,812 bytes
  - One Piece, etc.
- **Action:** tap the download icon

**Before this PR:** an empty `…/AnimeGG (EN)/<series>/<episode>.mp4`-named folder is created (this is the per-episode subdir from earlier in `downloadChapter`). The download icon stays in the spinner state. No error toast, no log entry, the queue row sits at 0% indefinitely.

**After this PR:** the `.mp4` file is written to disk at exactly the size declared in `Content-Length`, plays in QuickTime/VLC.

## Trial-and-error trail (chain of evidence)

We instrumented the download path with `print` statements to find the bug. Each step ruled out a hypothesis or revealed the next layer.

| # | Test | Observation | Conclusion |
|---|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | `curl -L -o "<download path>" "<animegg URL>"` | 241 MB written in 25 s | URL + filesystem fine, not a network issue |
| 2 | Trigger manga download (Asura Scans) on the same build | `.cbz` written end-to-end, "MDownloader completed" log | Downloader pipeline works for manga |
| 3 | Trigger anime download on the same build | Empty episode folder created, **zero** logs from `_downloadFile` | `MDownloader` is never reached for anime |
| 4 | Add log inside the anime branch of `downloadChapter` | `got 1 videos` → `originalUrl=…video.mp4?for=… isMedia=`**`false`** → `m3u8=0 nonM3u8=0` | `isMediaVideo()` rejects URLs with `?…` query strings |
| 5 | Patch `isMediaVideo()` (this PR) | `isMedia=true` → `nonM3u8=1` → "picked video url=…" → `_downloadFile` reached | First bug confirmed and fixed; second bug now visible |
| 6 | `_downloadFile` finally fires | `response status=206 contentLength=65026283` followed by `Failed to download file: … (status 206)` thrown 3× | Status check rejects 206 Partial Content |
| 7 | Patch the status check to accept any 2xx (this PR) | `first chunk received (7571 bytes)` → `stream done, received=65026283 bytes` → `MDownloader completed` | File written, plays |

### Sample log output

**Before any fix** — empty filter result, infinite poll:

```
[DL] anime: got 1 videos for Episode 147 - Toriko and Komatsu Embark on a New Voyage!
[DL]   video quality=360p - Sub url=https://www.animegg.org/play/75460/video.mp4?for=… originalUrl=…?for=… isMedia=false
[DL] anime: m3u8=0 nonM3u8=0
[DL] anime: NO playable URLs after filtering — download will hang in doWhile loop
```

**With `isMediaVideo()` fixed but status check still 200-only** — second bug visible:

```
[DL] anime: m3u8=0 nonM3u8=1
[DL] anime: picked video url=https://www.animegg.org/play/75460/video.mp4?for=…
[DL] anime fetch: https://www.animegg.org/play/75460/video.mp4?for=…
[DL] anime response status=206 contentLength=65026283
[DL] downloadChapter: MDownloader threw: MDownloaderException: Download failed (… status 206)
```

**With both fixes** — file completes:

```
[DL] anime first chunk received (7571 bytes) for https://www.animegg.org/play/75460/video.mp4?for=…
[DL] anime stream done, received=65026283 bytes
[DL] downloadChapter: MDownloader completed for Episode 147 …
```

Concurrent downloads (Toriko 147, Toriko 146, Gintama 39, Grand Blue 12) all reached "first chunk received" together; the Toriko 147 one completed end-to-end before we stopped watching.

The instrumentation `print`s are **not** included in this PR — they were dev-only. The PR carries only the two minimal source changes that proved load-bearing.

## Notes

- **Manga path unchanged.** The non-anime branch of `_downloadFile` still uses `if (statusCode != 200)`. Manga image servers don't honor `Range` requests (the manga branch doesn't send one), so 206 is irrelevant there. Left as-is to keep the diff minimal and avoid touching code the bug doesn't reach.
- **No source-specific code.** The fix isn't "make AnimeGG work"; it's "stop

author: prasadxa
body:
### 💡 What
Added a "Skip to main content" link to the application layout.

### 🎯 Why
To improve accessibility for keyboard users, allowing them to bypass repetitive navigation links and jump directly to the primary content of the page.

### 📸 Before/After
*Before*: Keyboard users had to tab through all navigation items on every page load to reach the main content.
*After*: A hidden link becomes visible when focused, allowing users to immediately jump to the main content area.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added a `href="#main-content"` anchor link that is visually hidden (`sr-only`) but becomes visible on focus (`focus:not-sr-only`).
- Set `id="main-content"` on the `<main>` element.
- Added `tabIndex={-1}` to the `<main>` element so it can receive programmatic focus without interfering with regular tab flow.
- Added `outline-none` to the `<main>` element to prevent a browser default focus ring when it receives programmatic focus.

body:
## Summary

- Replace shipped two-stage `muller_brown.yaml` and `lj13.yaml` recipes with **single-stage `pvre` on a small MLP** (`n_embed=4, depth=2`) at `lr=1e-3` with `patience=1` and a deterministic round-decade `threshold` trigger.
- MB: `(rtol, atol, threshold) = (1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-1)`, mean wall ~38s across 3 seeds, max F_2 ≈ 0.62 (target F_2<1).
- LJ13: `(rtol, atol, threshold) = (1e-1, 1e-4, 1e-3)`, mean wall ~76s across 3 seeds, max F_2 ≈ 0.0073 (target F_2<0.05). Bounded fmax ≤ 0.0064 (chemistry-standard fmax<0.05 met with ~7.8× headroom).
- Both yamls share `atol/threshold = 0.1` to enforce the strict /10 noise-floor rule for the trigger to fire reliably.
- Includes the empirical sweep + diagnostic harnesses (`tests_ongoing/sweep_*.py`) and the LJ13 single-loss baseline yamls referenced from the new `lj13.yaml` comment block.
- Docs (`convergence.md`, `advanced.md`, `loss-functions.md`, `paths.md`) updated to reflect the new single-stage shipped recipes; the `pvre² → pvre` schedule is reframed as a "pattern" with `lj13_pvre_two_stage.yaml` as the worked example.

Smoke tests on both yamls pass (cold-cache wall close to sweep-mean predictions). Memory entries `project_popcornn_{mb_two_stage_caveats,lj13_recipes,atol_threshold_rule,ts_force_targets}.md` updated alongside.

## Test plan

- [x] MB sweep: 3 seeds × `(rtol, atol, threshold)` grid; option B (atol=1e-2, thr=1e-1) selected for atol/threshold=0.1 consistency with LJ13.
- [x] LJ13 sweep: 3 seeds × (atol=1e-3, atol=1e-4) configs; ship recipe (atol=1e-4, thr=1e-3) selected for 6.8× F_2 headroom and pre-rebound stop on seed 0.
- [x] LJ13 rtol diagnostic: rtol=1e-2 + atol=1e-3 → empirical |g|_∞ floor unchanged from rtol=1e-1; confirms rtol-only tightening is useless when atol dominates.
- [x] End-to-end smoke runs of both yamls via `python examples/run.py --config <yaml>` on an interactive A100 node.

## Problem

`tooltip-neutral` was never defined in `tooltip.css`, making it a silent no-op. Every other semantic color variant exists (`tooltip-primary`, `tooltip-secondary`, `tooltip-accent`, `tooltip-info`, `tooltip-success`, `tooltip-warning`, `tooltip-error`) but `neutral` was skipped.

This means:
- `tooltip-neutral` has no effect on styling
- It does not appear in autocomplete (Tailwind Play, IDE plugins)
- Users expecting consistent API across all color variants are left with a broken class

## Fix

Added `.tooltip-neutral` following the exact same pattern as the other color variants — sets `--tt-bg` to `var(--color-neutral)` and applies `text-neutral-content` to the tooltip content.

The placement in the file follows alphabetical ordering relative to the other variants.

Closes #4492

author: ran-taig
body:
## Summary

Three small follow-ups to PR #104 (CAURA-222 write/query embedding-surface alignment), bundled into one PR. None change production logic — they close the loop on cleanup, regression coverage, and operational tooling that was intentionally deferred to keep #104 minimal.

1. **Delete `compose_embedding_text` and unwire re-exports.** Zero production call sites since #104.
2. **Add `tests/test_embed_stability.py` regression suite.** Pins write/query surface symmetry so the asymmetry can't return silently.
3. **Extend the embedding-backfill CLI with `--rewrite-hint-prefixed`.** One-shot recall-recovery mode for tenants whose existing rows were embedded under the old hint-prefixed write path.

## 1. Drop `compose_embedding_text`

After #104 removed every production call site, the helper, its re-exports, and the `TestComposeEmbeddingText` class were dead weight. Removed:

- `common/enrichment/service.py` — function definition.
- `common/enrichment/__init__.py` — import + `__all__` entry.
- `core-api/src/core_api/services/memory_enrichment.py` — re-export.
- `tests/test_retrieval_hint.py::TestComposeEmbeddingText` — the class.
- `tests/test_embed_off_hot_path.py` — leftover mock that was a no-op since #104.

Kept on purpose:

- The `retrieval_hint` LLM field, prompt validator (\`tests/test_retrieval_hint.py::TestValidatorRetrievalHint\` and \`TestPromptContainsHintRule\` stay).
- `metadata.retrieval_hint` persistence — auditability and the selector for the backfill mode below.
- The historical-context comments in \`parallel_embed_enrich.py\` and \`memory_enriched.py\`.

If the symmetric reintroduction work (the future PR I drafted as part of #104) goes with Option A (two-vector store), it'll add a new helper rather than reviving this one — the old prefix shape is documented as the failure mode in the test suite below, not as a building block.

## 2. Regression test — `tests/test_embed_stability.py`

Three tests, deterministic spies on the embedding providers — no network, no DB, no CI infra dependencies:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `test_hot_path_embeds_raw_content_when_enrichment_yields_hint` | `ParallelEmbedEnrich` calls embedder exactly once with raw content even when enrichment yields a `retrieval_hint`. Catches re-introduced hint prefixes on the write hot path. |
| `test_atomic_fact_children_embed_raw_fact_content` | Atomic-fact fan-out children pass `fact.content` (not `compose_embedding_text(fact_content, fact_hint)`) to the embedder. |
| `test_write_and_query_embed_identical_input_for_identical_text` | **Load-bearing**: write and search paths feed the embedder byte-identical strings for byte-identical content/query. Any future divergence — re-introduced prefix, document-side instruction without a query-side counterpart, normalization on one side — trips this test. |

The third test is the one I'd want to see in any future PR that touches embedding text construction. It mocks `get_embedding` (write side) and `get_query_embedding` (search side) with recording spies, exercises both paths with the same input string, and asserts the recorded inputs are equal.

## 3. Backfill CLI — `--rewrite-hint-prefixed`

New mode in \`core-storage-api/src/core_storage_api/scripts/backfill_embeddings.py\` for one-off recall recovery on tenants that already have rows embedded under the old surface.

**Selector:**
```sql
WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL
  AND metadata_ ? 'retrieval_hint'
  AND COALESCE(metadata_->>'retrieval_hint', '') <> ''
  AND deleted_at IS NULL
```

Default IS-NULL scan path unchanged — the new flag branches inside `_iter_rows`. Entities are skipped silently in this mode (no hint metadata exists there). Per-tenant phasing via `--tenant-id` and `--dry-run` still apply.

**Usage:**
```
# Dry-run scope estimate per tenant:
docker compose run --rm core-storage-api \
  python -m core_storage_api.scripts.backfill_embeddings \
    --rewrite-hint-prefixed --tenant-id tenant-abc --dry-run

# Actual rewrite:
docker compose run --rm core-storage-api \
  python -m core_storage_api.scripts.backfill_embeddings \
    --rewrite-hint-prefixed --tenant-id tenant-abc
```

Three new tests cover this:
- `test_rewrite_hint_prefixed_targets_memories_with_hint_metadata` — asserts the SQL filter shape.
- `test_rewrite_hint_prefixed_skips_entities` — entities table is not even queried.
- `test_default_mode_uses_null_embedding_filter` — pins the default mode's WHERE shape so the new branching can't silently break the original CLI.

**Caveats called out in the existing module docstring still apply:**
- Standalone CLI runs against the process-level embedding provider; it does NOT honour per-tenant overrides. Multi-tenant prod with per-tenant overrides should still use the event-driven `core-worker backfill-embeddings` task. `--tenant-id` here scopes the SQL scan, not the provider resolution.
- A re-run of `--rewrite-hint-prefixed` will re-match the same rows because `metadata.retrieval_hint` is intentionally preserved (auditability). Operational pattern is one forward pass per tenant, then the embed-stability probe to verify, then move on.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_embed_stability.py tests/test_embed_off_hot_path.py tests/test_retrieval_hint.py tests/test_backfill_embeddings.py` — 43 passed locally.
- [x] `ruff format --check` clean on all touched paths.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all touched paths.
- [ ] CI green.
- [ ] After merge: dry-run the new backfill mode against staging \`memclaw.dev\` tenant \`ran-507cb7\` to validate the SQL selector against real metadata shape; expected scope = paragraph-or-longer memories that were enriched on a deploy where the hint re-embed fired.

## Rollout

Independent of any production deploy — this PR is purely additive (regression test + cleanup + new opt-in CLI flag). Default backfill behavior, write path, and search path are all byte-identical to post-#104 main.

The recall recovery itself (running `--rewrite-hint-prefixed` against existing data) is a separate operational decision, owner-driven per-tenant, with the dry-run cost gate built into the existing CLI.

author: samoht
body:
Trailing "rest of buffer" payloads previously had no good shape in a `Codec` field. Add `Wire.rest_bytes total` to express the trailing field as `Expr.(Param.expr total - sizeof_this)`, projecting to `UINT8 Rest[:byte-size (total - sizeof(this))]` in 3D.

A `Codec` field can also use plain `all_bytes` / `all_zeros` directly: the size is derived from the buffer length minus the running offset, so `field "Rest" all_bytes` round-trips without an explicit length parameter. Demo schemas in [examples/demo/demo.ml](examples/demo/demo.ml) (`TrailingData`, `PaddedMsg`) use the new combinator.

author: aaronjmars
body:
## Summary

Four endpoints in `backend/src/routes/tabular.ts` accept user-supplied `document_id` (or read it out of `tabular_cells` rows the same user planted) without verifying the caller can read those documents. The downstream pipeline then downloads the bytes from R2, runs an LLM extraction with an attacker-controlled column prompt, and stores the result back in `tabular_cells.content` — which the attacker reads via the standard review GET.

By contrast the chat path (`backend/src/lib/chatTools.ts:buildDocContext`) does the right thing — it filters `documents.user_id = userId`, which is why regular chat is unaffected. The tabular path is the regression.

## Impact

A signed-in user with **knowledge of a document UUID** they don't own can extract the full text of that document by running it through their own tabular review. Three requests: create a review with `document_ids: [<victim_uuid>]` and a column prompt asking for verbatim text → `POST /:reviewId/generate` → `GET /:reviewId` returns the leaked content in `cells[0].content`. No project membership or sharing relationship required.

UUIDv4 is unguessable, but UUIDs leak in practice — a removed project collaborator retains every UUID they saw (browser cache, exported chats, screenshots). After they're dropped from `projects.shared_with` they legitimately lose access to project routes but can still extract via this path. It's a "former-insider keeps reading" class of bug, not a stranger-guesses-UUIDs class.

On a legal-document platform the data at risk is exactly the data the product is built to keep confidential.

## Location

- `backend/src/routes/tabular.ts:172-222` — `POST /tabular-review`
- `backend/src/routes/tabular.ts:484-567` — `PATCH /:reviewId`
- `backend/src/routes/tabular.ts:619-727` — `POST /:reviewId/regenerate-cell`
- `backend/src/routes/tabular.ts:730-…` — `POST /:reviewId/generate`

## Fix

Adds `filterAccessibleDocumentIds(documentIds, userId, userEmail, db)` in `backend/src/lib/access.ts`, alongside the existing `ensureDocAccess` / `ensureReviewAccess` / `listAccessibleProjectIds` helpers. The helper resolves each id to its `user_id` + `project_id` row and admits it only if the caller is owner-of-doc OR a member (own or `shared_with`) of the doc's project.

Applied at all four entry points:
- **POST /tabular-review** — filter `document_ids` before inserting `tabular_cells` (drop unauthorised silently).
- **PATCH /:reviewId** — drop newly-added unauthorised ids; preserve already-attached cells so a non-owner project collaborator's PATCH doesn't accidentally orphan rows they can't directly re-add.
- **POST /:reviewId/regenerate-cell** — refuse byte fetch when the caller can't read the underlying doc, even for stale `tabular_cells` rows that pre-date this fix.
- **POST /:reviewId/generate** — filter `docIds` before the parallel LLM fetch loop (same defense-in-depth as above).

Fails closed silently rather than 403'ing so legacy clients passing stale ids don't error out the whole review.

## Note on legacy data

This PR closes the **new** exfil path. Cells that were extracted before the fix already live in `tabular_cells.content` for the attacker's own review and remain readable via the standard GET (since they planted the row). Wiping or filtering those legacy rows is a separate data-migration concern — happy to do a follow-up if you want one.

## Detected by

Aeon + manual review of the cross-route document-access pattern (chat path filters by `user_id`, tabular path doesn't).
- Severity: **HIGH**
- CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key)

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p backend/tsconfig.json` clean against the patched tree.
- No test suite in the backend (`scripts: build/dev/start` only) — no regression suite to run.
- Diff is +97 / -6 across two files, scoped to the access-control fix only.

---

body:
## Summary
Third mode for the per-project \`secrets:\` block — when \`operator_secret_values[<name>] = { vault_path = "secret/tenants/<t>/<n>" }\`, engine emits a \`VaultStaticSecret\` CR (consumed by VSO from PR #121) instead of a literal \`kubernetes_secret_v1\`. VSO syncs the Vault KV-v2 path → k8s Secret with the same name in the project namespace.

After this lands, an operator-supplied secret can move from \`.env\` literal-mode into Vault by:
1. Putting the values into Vault under a \`secret/tenants/<tenant>/<name>\` path (UI or CLI via OIDC SSO with the tenant's role).
2. Setting \`TF_VAR_operator_secret_values\` for that entry to \`{ vault_path = "secret/tenants/<tenant>/<name>" }\`.
3. \`./tf apply\` — engine swaps emit shape; VSO materialises the same Secret name with whatever's at the Vault path.

Rotation = update the Vault entry; VSO re-syncs within \`refreshAfter\` (30s); pod restart on consumer side stays a separate concern (checksum-annotation pattern from PR #116).

## Plan
\`\`\`
Plan: 0 to add (mode-related), 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
\`\`\`
Mode is opt-in per entry; no consumer declares \`vault_path\` yet, so this PR is dormant code until an operator config update flips an entry over.

## What's not in scope (separate)
- Engine-side Vault writes (operator generates → engine writes → VSO reads back loop). Decided against today: blocked by the standing "no \`hashicorp/vault\` TF provider" rule (cascade trap), would need a Job-per-secret with \`vault\` CLI + RBAC, and operator's manual UI path is acceptable for current use cases. Can land later if visibility/rotation demand grows.

## Test plan
- [x] terraform fmt + validate clean
- [x] Plan: 0 destroy, 0 replace, no behavioural change to existing literal/random entries
- [ ] After merge + apply: declare a \`vault_path\` entry in operator config + put the corresponding Vault path → engine emits VaultStaticSecret → VSO materialises matching k8s Secret with the right keys

author: xpoes123
body:
The final piece: failed phases retry up to 3 times against current main before being terminally marked failed. Independent siblings keep going; dependents are skipped only when retries are exhausted; terminal failures escalate to Discord with an owner ping.

## What changed

### Schema (migration 030)
\`build_phases.attempt_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0\`

### Loop changes
- Each iteration computes \`phase_attempt = (row.attempt_count or 0) + 1\`
- Branch names disambiguate retries: \`phase-{N}-retry-{attempt-1}\` so each retry starts on a fresh branch from main with no leftover commits poisoning the worktree
- The phase prompt on attempt > 1 includes:
  - "RETRY ATTEMPT N of M" header
  - last \`failure_reason\` from the prior row
  - prior PR number + \`gh pr diff <N>\` instruction so the agent can read what was tried
  - explicit "do NOT reuse the previous attempt's branch"

### New helper \`_handle_phase_failure\`
Consolidates both PR-creation and review-failure paths. Either:
- keeps \`status='pending'\` + increments \`attempt_count\` → next \`next_runnable_phase\` call re-picks the phase
- or, when retries exhausted: \`status='failed'\`, skip dependents, escalate to Discord with \`<@owner>\` ping, last failure reason, and PR number for inspection

## Per the design questions answered upthread
- \`MAX_PHASE_ATTEMPTS=3\`
- Retry context = failure reason + last PR diff (via \`gh pr diff\` instruction); fresh worktree from main
- Terminal failure = skip dependents + escalate to Discord

## Tests (5 new in \`test_phase_level_retry.py\`)
- First failure keeps phase pending + bumps attempt_count
- MAX_PHASE_ATTEMPTS marks failed + skips dependents (independent siblings keep going)
- Two consecutive failures progress 1 → 2 (still pending)
- Terminal failure includes PR number in escalation message
- Retry message uses "Retrying" language; not "failed permanently"

87 reliability tests pass total. Only the 2 pre-existing \`test_task_queue_fixes\` failures remain on main.

## Closing the loop
With #407 + #408 + #409 + #410 + this PR, the multi-phase build pipeline now has:
1. Structured failure observability (\`failure_reason\`, \`exit_code\`)
2. Time budgets that protect review from outer timeouts
3. Phase state in DB (no more in-memory loss on restart)
4. Boot-time orphan reconciliation with session_id resume
5. Phase-level retry with escalation

\`Closing: orphaned PR from interrupted task pipeline\` shouldn't happen anymore — the reconciler picks them up automatically; phase-level retry handles transient failures; only genuinely-stuck phases escalate to you.

body:
### Motivation
- Evitar a exceção `ArgumentException: The 'ClientId' option must be provided.` ao iniciar quando o Google OAuth está declarado mas sem `ClientId`/`ClientSecret` configurados.
- Permitir que a aplicação inicie normalmente sem OAuth do Google e manter o fluxo de login normal funcionando.
- Ocultar a opção de login via Google na UI quando as credenciais não estiverem preenchidas para não confundir o usuário.

### Description
- Em `Program.cs` foi lido `Authentication:Google:ClientId` e `ClientSecret` e introduzida a flag `googleAuthConfigured` para detectar se o Google está configurado corretamente.
- O `DefaultChallengeScheme` agora usa `GoogleDefaults.AuthenticationScheme` apenas quando `googleAuthConfigured` for `true`, caso contrário usa o esquema de cookie para evitar falha na inicialização.

author: nathanjohnpayne
body:
Authoring-Agent: claude

Closes #210 (sub-C of #154). Doc-only follow-up to [#208](https://github.com/nathanjohnpayne/mergepath/issues/208) (PR #226), which landed the canonical precedence section but deliberately scoped out the rotation procedure and the deeper reconciliation pass. This PR finishes that work.

## Files changed

- **`DEPLOYMENT.md`** (+71/-2)
  - New `### Rotating a Firebase deploy SA key` section under `## Secrets Management`, after `### Provisioning the Firebase-vault SA key`. Replaces the prior one-line "Rotation:" sentence with a full procedure: triggers (calendar 90d / compromise / personnel change), 7-step procedure (mint → capture old key id → replace 1Password item with same canonical title → wipe local → verify with non-prod deploy → revoke old key → optional CHANGELOG entry), failure-mode diagnosis, and rollback path. Documents the human-only nature explicitly — the bootstrap wizard (#156) does NOT automate rotation.
  - `## CI/CD Integration` paragraph rewritten so the SA-key path is the recommended one (matching the canonical precedence — same source-credential shape interactive and headless), with WIF / `external_account` positioned as also-supported rather than preferred. Closes the contradiction the issue called out between the canonical-precedence section's \"standard day-to-day credential, both interactive and CI\" and the prior CI/CD paragraph's \"prefer WIF\" framing.

- **`.ai_context.md`** (+8/-3)
  - `op-firebase-deploy` script-table description rewritten: \"Uses the project Firebase-vault SA key directly when present; falls back to short-lived impersonation when only the shared 1Password ADC is available,\" with a pointer to the canonical precedence section.
  - `op-firebase-setup` description rewritten: \"configures impersonation as the fallback path for when the project SA key isn't yet provisioned\" (vs the prior \"configures impersonation\" framing that read as if impersonation were the primary mode).
  - Usage section's `# Set up per-project impersonation` comment broken into two: the setup step + a pointer to the provisioning procedure as the natural next step.

- **`docs/agents/deployment-process.md`** (+17/-0)
  - New `## Credential source debugging` section. Documents the source-credential log line format and a 4-case diagnosis tree for unexpected sources (local-adc when project-sa-key expected, human-override unexpectedly, preflight-adc when project-sa-key expected, ADC-quota-warning false positive). Cross-links to the rotation procedure in DEPLOYMENT.md.

## Verification

- `scripts/ci/check_duplicate_docs` passes (4 pre-existing warnings about `Code Review` / `Pull Request` mentions in `.claude/` / `.cursor/` config files; none introduced by this PR).
- **Audit grep** per #210 step 5 (`git grep -lE 'firebase login|impersonat|GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS|op-firebase-deploy' | grep -vE '^scripts/|^.github/'`) was reviewed file-by-file. Remaining mentions are:
  - **Descriptive** (script-step walkthroughs in `op-firebase-deploy`, IAM permission prerequisites, gcloud-config scaffolding, the trade-off paragraph that explicitly compares to the prior model) — accurate as written.
  - **Historical incident references** (#137 reauth friction, #181 closure) — accurate as written.
  - No remaining prescriptive content contradicts the new precedence.

Net diff: 93 insertions, 5 deletions across three doc files. Under the issue's ≤200-line target.

## Out of scope (per #154's sub-issue split)

- **Policy decision** — landed via #208 (PR #226).
- **op-firebase-deploy code changes** — already shipped in [#181](https://github.com/nathanjohnpayne/mergepath/pull/181); this PR documents what's there.
- **End-to-end verification on a real consumer repo** — see [#211 (#154 sub-D)](https://github.com/nathanjohnpayne/mergepath/issues/211); requires manual attended deploy.

## Self-Review

**Correctness.** The 7-step rotation procedure was cross-checked against the existing provisioning procedure at line ~654, and against `scripts/firebase/op-firebase-deploy`'s `materialize_firebase_vault_sa_key` lookup logic — the same `op://Firebase/{project-id} — Firebase Deployer SA Key` item title is reused so rotation doesn't require any per-project script edit. The 4-case debugging diagnosis tree maps each unexpected source to its concrete cause (item missing / env-var override / ADC fallback chain / cosmetic warning) with a one-step fix per case. The CI/CD rewrite preserves the WIF / external_account support as a documented option — this PR only re-orders the recommendation.

**Regression risk.** Pure docs change. `scripts/ci/check_duplicate_docs` passes. The new rotation section is independent of the existing provisioning procedure; existing consumers running rotation via the prior one-liner can pick up the fuller procedure without breaking anything. The CI/CD paragraph rewrite kept all existing options as supported — just re-ordered.

**Style.** Followed the existing tone (active voice, concrete commands, fenced bash blocks, cross-references via section anchors). The rotation procedure's failure-mode diagnosis matches the same shape as the credential-source debugging diagnosis added to deployment-process.md, so a reader hitting one finds the other.

**Test coverage.** Doc-only PR; the implicit test is `scripts/ci/check_duplicate_docs` plus the audit-grep above. Both clean. No automated test for prose accuracy exists in the repo (would be out-of-scope here).

**Security / dependency hygiene.** No code changes. Rotation procedure documents a sensitive operation (key rotation) with explicit ordering: mint new → save old key id → replace 1Password item → verify deploy → revoke old. The order ensures we never have a window where the project lacks a valid deploy credential. Failure-mode diagnosis includes a rollback path. No new dependencies.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/ci/check_duplicate_docs` passes.
- [x] Audit grep reviewed — no remaining prescriptive contradictions.
- [ ] An operator following the rotation procedure on a real project (e.g., matchline) successfully rotates the SA key without surprises — this is the operational test, naturally happens at the next quarterly rotation cycle. Failure to converge would surface as the same kind of feedback that produced this PR.

## Summary

Adds comprehensive YAML language support to srgn, enabling syntax-aware manipulation of `.yaml` and `.yml` configuration files.

## Changes

- **Package**: Added `tree-sitter-yaml v0.7.2` (1,813,985 downloads, official tree-sitter grammar)
- **8 Working PreparedQuery variants**:
  - Scalar values: `string-scalar`, `integer-scalar`, `float-scalar`, `boolean-scalar`
  - Structure: `block-sequence`, `block-mapping`, `flow-sequence`, `flow-mapping`
- **CLI Integration**: `--yaml`, `--yaml-query`, `--yaml-query-file`
- **Test Coverage**: 8 snapshot-based tests for all prepared queries
- **All tests passing**: 501 unit + 195 module + 59 CLI + 2 regression

## Why This Matters

YAML is the most popular configuration format across:
- DevOps & CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI)
- Kubernetes configs and Helm charts
- Application configuration files
- Data serialization and API specs

This enables srgn to work effectively with the most widely-used configuration format in the ecosystem.

## Example Usage

```bash
# Extract string values from YAML config
cat config.yaml | srgn --yaml string-scalar -- your-replacement

# Find all integer values
cat config.yaml | srgn --yaml integer-scalar -- resize

# Target block mappings
cat config.yaml | srgn --yaml block-mapping update-all

# Interactive replacement with scope awareness
cat config.yaml | srgn --yaml boolean-scalar toggle-features
```

## Implementation Quality

- **100% coverage** - All 8 defined variants work correctly 
- **Compatible** - Native tree-sitter 0.25.10 compatibility (no version conflicts)
- **Production ready** - Fully tested and integrated

## Scope (Claude, Opus 4.7) — EvidenceLog hash-chain (re-enable P1.5)

Picks up the next bounded slice from `AGENTS_LOG.md`'s roadmap, chosen because it doesn't conflict with **PR #2** (UI/SSR/page-wiring) or **PR #3** (fetch timeouts + sync hardening), and stays out of the lead coordinator's queued Float → Decimal scope.

## What this PR will do

1. New `src/lib/evidence-log.service.ts`:
   - `record({ eventType, tenantId, makerIdentity, description, payload })`
   - Computes `sha256(previousHash || canonical(payload) || eventType || tenantId || makerIdentity || createdAt)`.
   - Looks up the latest evidence row for the tenant, links via `previousHash`.
   - Writes inside the caller's transaction so the evidence cannot exist without the operation that produced it (and vice versa).
2. Hook into `src/lib/ledger.service.ts`:
   - `postEntry` records a `JOURNAL_POSTED` evidence row.
   - `reverseEntry` records a `JOURNAL_REVERSED` evidence row.
3. Re-enable **P1.5** in `.github/workflows/p1-governance.yml` (the `evidenceLog.create` + `sha256` greps).

## Out of scope (deferred)

- **SoD** (P1.4 `makerIdentity !== checkerIdentity`) — needs auth/session first.
- **Per-tenant serialisation** of concurrent evidence writes — flagged in `AGENTS_LOG.md` as a known limitation; current implementation relies on Postgres transactions and could theoretically fork the chain under concurrent writers. Mitigation (advisory lock or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) tracked as a followup.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx prisma validate` still passes.
- [ ] P1.5 grep gates pass (file is referenced by name and contains `sha256`).
- [ ] Manual: posting two journal entries produces two evidence rows; second's `previousHash` equals the first's `hash`.

## Coordination

- Branch claim recorded in `AGENTS_LOG.md` on first commit.
- PR #2 (lead coordinator) and PR #3 are independent; both have been pinged with rebase instructions against the new `main`.

Timer and Countdown

 (vacío — todo el JavaScript lo añades tú) (no existe todavía — debes crearlo) Adjunto a este prompt va una imagen de referencia (stopwatch.png) que define el lenguaje visual de la app. La imagen muestra UN componente; nuestra app tendrá DOS componentes con ese mismo estilo, apilados verticalmente. Construye una página de una sola pantalla con DOS componentes funcionalmente independientes, apilados verticalmente: 1. Un CRONÓMETRO (stopwatch) que cuenta hacia arriba desde cero, arriba. 2. Una CUENTA ATRÁS (countdown timer) que cuenta hacia abajo hasta cero desde una duración configurable por el usuario, abajo. Los dos componentes tienen estado separado, DOM separado y lógica separada. No comparten temporizador ni botones. Sí comparten el mismo lenguaje visual (el de la imagen). Estado inicial: - Display muestra "00:00:00" (HH:MM:SS) con "000" (milisegundos) en pequeño, alineado abajo a la derecha del display, con menor jerarquía visual. - Botón 1: "Start" (fondo verde). - Botón 2: "Clear" (fondo rojo). Transiciones: - Pulsar "Start" → el cronómetro arranca y cuenta hacia arriba. Botón 1 cambia a "Pause" (fondo rojo). - Pulsar "Pause" → el cronómetro se detiene conservando el valor actual. Botón 1 cambia a "Continue" (fondo verde). - Pulsar "Continue" → el cronómetro reanuda desde el valor actual. Botón 1 vuelve a "Pause" (fondo rojo). - Pulsar "Clear" en cualquier estado → el cronómetro se detiene si estaba corriendo, el display vuelve a "00:00:00" "000", y el botón 1 vuelve a "Start" (fondo verde). Estado inicial: - Tres inputs `` con sus labels visibles: "Hours" (0-99), "Minutes" (0-59), "Seconds" (0-59). Valores iniciales 0/0/0. - Display muestra "00:00:00" "000" con el mismo estilo que el cronómetro. - Botón 1: "Start" (fondo verde, deshabilitado mientras la duración total sea 0). - Botón 2: "Clear" (fondo rojo). Transiciones: - Pulsar "Start" → arranca la cuenta atrás con el valor de los inputs. Los inputs se deshabilitan. Botón 1 cambia a "Pause" (fondo rojo). - Pulsar "Pause" → la cuenta atrás se detiene conservando el valor actual. Botón 1 cambia a "Continue" (fondo verde). Los inputs siguen deshabilitados. - Pulsar "Continue" → la cuenta atrás reanuda. Botón 1 vuelve a "Pause" (fondo rojo). - Cuando el display llega a "00:00:00" "000": el color del texto del display cambia a rojo, el loop de animación se detiene, el botón 1 vuelve a "Start" (verde, deshabilitado de nuevo hasta que el usuario cambie la duración), y los inputs se vuelven a habilitar. - Pulsar "Clear" en cualquier estado → la cuenta atrás se detiene si estaba corriendo, el display vuelve a "00:00:00" "000" en su color normal (no rojo), los inputs se habilitan, el botón 1 vuelve a "Start" (deshabilitado si la duración es 0). La imagen adjunta es la fuente de verdad. Replícala con fidelidad para los DOS componentes. Puntos clave: Display: - Fondo lavanda/azul muy claro (≈ #E8E8F5). - Borde negro grueso (~6-8px). - Esquinas muy redondeadas. - Tipografía fina, condensada, color negro, sans-serif. - Tamaño grande: el display ocupa la mayor parte del ancho disponible del componente. - Separadores entre HH/MM/SS: dos puntos cuadrados verticales (no ":" clásicos). - Milisegundos: tres dígitos, alineados abajo a la derecha del display, mucho más pequeños que los dígitos principales. Botones: - Mismo estilo de borde y esquinas que el display (negro grueso, muy redondeado). - Tamaño grande, texto en negro. - Verde brillante para Start/Continue. - Rojo brillante para Pause/Clear. - Posicionamiento horizontal con buena separación, uno a cada lado. Layout: - Cronómetro arriba, cuenta atrás abajo, con clara separación entre ambos. - Cada componente ocupa la mayor parte del ancho del viewport con márgenes generosos. - Responsive: en mobile (≤480px), los tamaños se reducen pero la jerarquía y proporciones visuales se preservan. Stack: - Solo HTML, CSS y JavaScript vanilla. Cero frameworks, cero librerías, cero CDNs. Arquitectura del JS: - Código modular. Encapsula la lógica del cronómetro y de la cuenta atrás en sus propias funciones/módulos. No uses variables globales sueltas; encapsula el estado. author: zetimente
body:
## Why

Yesterday's real turnkey test found two silent failure modes the README wasn't honest about. A fresh operator following the old Quickstart could do everything right and still end up at `backend_ok: false` with no idea why.

Both are well-known Linux+docker+Ollama interactions. Neither is a Nursery code bug. Both are Nursery's **problem** because our docs didn't mention either.

## The two cliffs

**1. Ollama defaults to `127.0.0.1:11434`** after the standard `curl|sh` install. Containers on the docker bridge (172.17.0.0/16) cannot reach loopback on the host. The agent will start, report healthy, and then silently fail every chat() call.

**2. If the host runs `ufw`** (Raspberry Pi OS default is ufw active), traffic from the docker bridge to host ports is blocked. Even with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` set, you'll still hit connection timeouts.

Both were reproduced and fixed during a cold-clone turnkey test earlier tonight.

## What this PR changes

Pure docs. No code.

### Quickstart rewritten

The old Quickstart was aspirational — it referenced `nursery fork` (not implemented) and an `examples/agents/layla.yaml` that doesn't exist. The new one is a **working sequence you can copy-paste** and get a real reply at the end. Numbered steps, realistic expectations, ends with cleanup.

### New '## Host Prerequisites' section

Lives between Quickstart and Example Agent Spec. Covers the three real requirements:

1. **Docker** — install + docker-group note (our CLI already falls back to sudo with a notice).
2. **uv** — one-liner install.
3. **Ollama, reachable from the container** — this is where the work lives:
   - 3a. `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` via systemd drop-in, with verification command.
   - 3b. `ufw allow from 172.17.0.0/16 to any port 11434 proto tcp`.
   - 3c. `ollama pull batiai/gemma4-e2b:q4` + `ollama pull nomic-embed-text`.

### 'Quick sanity check' one-liner

At the end of Host Prerequisites, a single command that tests the container-to-Ollama path **without Nursery in the loop**:

```bash
docker run --rm --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway alpine/curl:latest \\
  -s --max-time 5 http://host.docker.internal:11434/api/version
```

If that returns a version, `nursery spawn` will work. If not, you know exactly which step above to fix. This is the test we should have shipped with the first Ollama-using PR.

## What's still aspirational

The current doc makes it easy for a human to follow the checklist. It doesn't **preflight** anything on behalf of the user. That's a separate improvement — flagged earlier as 'Option B' in the turnkey findings, on the list as a follow-up PR. Scope of this one stays small: explain what's needed, explain how to verify it.

author: austinnchristensen
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for the dashboard discoverability problem:

> Getting error not found trying to get to the dashboard page

The most common cause is a **stale Hive process** that started before #53 merged. \`hive.sh\` updates the source on disk but doesn't restart the running process. This PR makes that obvious and also auto-opens the browser so the operator gets to the dashboard the moment they start the Hive.

## Discoverability

- **Startup banner** with version + clickable URLs:
  \`\`\`
  HivePlane Hive v0.0.1 listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787
  Dashboard:   http://localhost:8787/
  Health:      http://localhost:8787/healthz
  API root:    http://localhost:8787/api/bees
  \`\`\`
- \`/version\` route + \`version\` field on \`/healthz\` so \`curl /version\` confirms which build is running. If it's older than expected, the operator knows to restart the Hive process.
- \`/dashboard\`, \`/dashboard/\`, and \`/index.html\` are aliases for \`/\`. Defensive against operators typing the obvious URLs.
- 404 message on missing \`index.html\` now hints that the running process may be older than the source on disk.
- \`0.0.0.0\` / \`::\` in the bound host get rewritten to \`localhost\` in the displayed URL (since \`0.0.0.0\` isn't browsable).

## Auto-open browser

\`apps/web/src/cli.ts\` shells out to the native opener after \`server.emit('listening')\`:

| Platform | Command |
|---|---|
| darwin | \`open <url>\` |
| linux | \`xdg-open <url>\` |
| win32 | \`cmd /c start "" <url>\` |

Defaults: **on** when \`process.stdout.isTTY\` (interactive runs via \`hive.sh\` / \`pnpm start\`), **off** when stdout is redirected (launchd/systemd service unit, CI, pipes). This means the future Hive service unit (#46) won't accidentally try to spawn a browser at boot.

Overrides:
- \`HIVEPLANE_OPEN_BROWSER=true|false\` (env)
- \`--open\` / \`--no-open\` (CLI flag, takes precedence over env)

Failure (e.g. headless container, no display) is best-effort: warn and proceed. The URL is in the log either way.

## What's new

- \`apps/web/src/cli.ts\` — startup banner, \`open\` flag, \`openInBrowser()\` helper
- \`apps/web/src/server.ts\` — \`/dashboard\`, \`/dashboard/\`, \`/index.html\` aliases, \`/version\` route, \`version\` on \`/healthz\`, sharper 404 hint
- \`apps/web/src/server.test.ts\` — extended dashboard test to assert all four aliases work; new test for \`/version\` and \`version\` on \`/healthz\`
- \`README.md\` — note the auto-open + opt-out + aliases + \`/version\` curl

## Validation

- \`pnpm format\` ✅
- \`pnpm check\` ✅ — 21 web tests (+1 from previous)
- Manual on this Mac: startup printed the 4-line banner, \`curl /version\` returned \`{"version":"0.0.1","service":"hiveplane-hive"}\`, all four aliases returned 200 + \`text/html\`, binding to \`0.0.0.0\` displayed \`localhost\` in the user-facing URL.

## Stack

- Targets \`main\` directly. Compatible with #52 (install guide) — both touch the README in different sections; whichever lands first the other rebases trivially.

## Note on the original 404

If you're hitting "not found" on a Hive started before #53, it's not a bug in the route — your running process predates the dashboard. After this PR you'll see the version on startup and on \`/version\`, so you can tell whether to restart. Concretely:

\`\`\`bash
curl http://your-hive:8787/version  # → {"version":"0.0.1",...}
\`\`\`

If \`/version\` 404s, the Hive process is from before this PR landed; if it returns the version but \`/\` 404s with \`dashboard_not_built\`, the source on disk is missing the file (re-run \`hive.sh\` to refresh the clone).

author: iacob-alexandru-andrei
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the F-class hyperagents edits that have been sitting in the local working tree but were never committed to any branch of this fork. Without these, fresh checkouts of recursive-scientist + hyperagents cannot run Nemotron experiments end-to-end (the meta-agent gets a one-line stub instruction; the writer crashes mid-draft on the 4096-cap; no retry on transient NVIDIA Inference 5xx; reasoning_effort isn't plumbed to gpt-5/o-series; container can't auth to upstream because OPENAI_API_KEY isn't propagated).

Stacks on PR #11 (cost-proxy-per-turn-visibility / F2h+F2i+query_model). Base: \`cost-proxy-per-turn-visibility\`. After #11 merges to \`rqgm\`, this PR's base auto-retargets to \`rqgm\`.

## Edits (one commit covering all)

### \`agent/llm.py\` (F2c+)
- \`@backoff.on_exception\` now catches \`litellm.exceptions.{RateLimitError, APIError, Timeout, APIConnectionError, InternalServerError, ServiceUnavailableError}\` in addition to the previous \`requests.RequestException + json.JSONDecodeError + KeyError\`. Was missing every transient NVIDIA 5xx.
- \`reasoning_effort\` threaded through \`get_response_from_llm\` via litellm \`extra_body\`. Only injected when model name matches \`gpt-5\` / \`o1\` / \`o3\` / \`o4\` prefixes (\`_supports_reasoning_effort\`).
- \`response_text\` falls back to \`msg['reasoning_content']\` when \`'content'\` is missing or empty (Nemotron 3 Super populates the former).
- Raise on \`finish_reason='length'\` — loud truncation rather than silent malformed output downstream.
- Relax the 4096-token cap that was applied to all non-gpt-5 models down to only Claude Haiku. Nemotron 3 Super accepts 16K, the cap was crashing the paper-writer mid-draft.

### \`Dockerfile\` (F2f)
- \`git config --global --add safe.directory '*'\` so in-container git operations don't trip 'dubious ownership' against host-uid bind mounts.

### \`meta_agent.py\` (F-class long instruction)
- Replaces the one-line stub instruction with the full briefing: catalog read, \`iterations_left\` mention, \`query_model\` usage hint, prior-generation artifact documentation, val-leakage warning, malformed_qids self-correction guidance.

### \`agent/llm_withtools.py\`
- \`load_tools\` accepts a \`catalog\` kwarg bound via \`functools.partial\` into the \`query_model\` tool surface.

### \`task_agent.py\` (F2h)
- Per-domain output-format dispatch.

### \`utils/docker_utils.py\` (F2c)
- Propagate \`OPENAI_API_KEY\` from host into container env so litellm in-container can authenticate.

### \`agent/_cost_tracker.py\` (NEW)
- Container-side cost tracker: hooks \`litellm.success_callback\` to append to \`/eval_path/llm_calls.jsonl\` so the host's \`rebuild_cost_md\` sees in-container spend.

### \`run_meta_agent.py\` / \`run_task_agent.py\`
- Pass \`reasoning_effort\` through.

### \`generation_step.py\` / \`utils/common.py\` / \`utils/gl_utils.py\` / \`domains/harness.py\`
- Helper plumbing supporting the above.

- Content has been used in real Nemotron canary runs in the recursive-scientist parent (\`runs/paper_writer_review/exp1_v2_nemotron/seed0/generate_20260509_230407_771561\`), producing 240 evals across 5 nodes before hitting the parser-crash bug fixed separately in parent PR #193.
- The longer prompt is the same content the user emphasized was missing in their Telegram-time conversation 2026-05-10.

This PR does NOT yet replace the os.environ-based F2g/F2h plumbing. That's a follow-up: read \`RS_COST_PROXY_HEALTH_URL\` / \`RS_EXPANSION_DEADLINE_TS\` / \`RS_COST_PROXY_HOST_IP\` from the catalog file or container args instead of \`os.environ\`, per the user's "no os.environ" directive. author: acmeproducts
body:
### Motivation
- Replace the prior incremental lineage logic with a fresh, deterministic two-pass pipeline that extracts factual git metadata/diffs first and then derives analysis fields from adjacent diffs. 
- Produce a minimal, stable timeline model for all `bridge*` files starting at commit `ec23f33` and provide a small, focused explorer UI that consumes only that model. 

### Description
- Rewrote `scripts/build-lineage-model.mjs` to implement a factual-first pass (git metadata, name-status, raw patches) and a deterministic second pass that derives `description_delta_from_previous`, `functional_impacts`, `diff_evidence`, and `patch_hash`, while emitting the required fields including `seq`, `timestamp`, `timestamp_pt`, `commit_hash`, `commit_short`, `commit_message`, `code_fingerprint`, `primary_filename`, `changed_paths`, `blob_refs`, `launch_ref`, `note`, and `previous_commit_hash` for each entry.  
- Script is scoped to `bridge*` changes from `ec23f33`..`HEAD`, formats Pacific display via `America/Los_Angeles` DST-aware formatter, normalizes patches for deterministic hashing with `sha256`, and writes valid JSON to `bridge-lineage-timeline-model.json`. 
- Rebuilt `repo.html` to consume only `bridge-lineage-timeline-model.json` and present the required explorer behavior: left-pane omni search + descending timeline list, right-pane with only `Details` and `Side-by-Side` tabs, two selectable side-by-side entries with searchable selectors, filename display, iframe preview, and working `view blob` / `launch actual version` links; `Details` shows filename and the same links plus `description_delta_from_previous`, `functional_impacts`, and note. 
- Kept `package.json` script `build:lineage` and regenerated `bridge-lineage-timeline-model.json` from the updated script. 

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build:lineage` which executed the new script and produced `bridge-lineage-timeline-model.json` successfully (script logged the written entry count). 
- Verified the generated JSON loads in `repo.html` via the page fetch path and that the UI renders timeline entries (fetch succeeded during local run). 
- Performed a local commit including `repo.html`, `scripts/build-lineage-model.mjs`, and `bridge-lineage-timeline-model.json` to validate file changes could be produced (`git commit` succeeded).

author: alfanumrikos
body:
## Summary

User-reported bug: Grade 7 student Hridaan Kaushik asked Foxy "Provide me 5 questions from this chapter to practice." (Science → Sour, Sweet, Bitter, and Salty). Foxy responded with a 1-sentence intro and **zero actual questions**. Trace shows 3 successive student attempts at the same task, all routed to `foxy_tutor_v1` (explain template) with answer_length 139-566 chars.

## Root cause

`QUIZ_PATTERNS` regex in `src/lib/ai/workflows/foxy-router.ts` was too narrow:

```js
/\b(quiz|test\s+me|give\s+me\s+questions?|mcq|practice\s+questions?|mock\s+test)\b/i
```

It required `give\s+me\s+questions` (specific verb) or `practice\s+questions` (specific word order). Common natural phrasings — "Provide me 5 questions", "questions to practice", "ask me MCQs" — all fell through, defaulted to `explain` intent → routed to `foxy_tutor_v1` template → no quiz workflow ever ran.

The LLM-fallback classifier (called when keyword confidence < 0.8) also misclassified these messages as `explain` because its prompt had no examples for these phrasings.

## Fix (option C — both regex + LLM prompt)

**1. Broaden `QUIZ_PATTERNS` regex** to cover:
- More request verbs: `provide|share|send|show|generate|create|make|prepare|set|ask`
- More qualifiers: `practice|tricky|hard|difficult|easy|sample|board-level`
- More nouns: `questions|problems|mcqs|tests|quizzes`
- Standalone forms: `practice questions`, `questions from this chapter`, `questions to solve`
- Want/need/would-like phrasings: `I want to solve`, `I need a few problems`, `I would like some MCQs`

**2. Strengthen the LLM classifier prompt** in `classifyWithLLM()` with 12 few-shot examples (7 quiz, 5 negative) so word-order variants get correctly routed even when regex misses.

## Tests

- 19 new positive cases (regression guard for the incident phrasings)
- 5 new negative cases (does-NOT-misclassify checks)
- All 69 `ai-layer` tests pass
- `npm run type-check` 0 errors

## Risk

- **False positives** in the broader regex are the main risk. Mitigated by:
  - Negative test cases for "Can you explain X?", "What is the difference?", "Summarize chapter 3", "Tell me about Y", "I am confused about Z" — all confirmed NOT to fire as quiz.
  - Word stem `questions?|problems?|mcqs?` is required in every alternation — bare verbs like "give me X" or "I want X" don't trigger.
- **No backward incompatibility** — broader patterns are a strict superset of the prior regex.
- **Cost neutral** — keyword path returns 0.85 confidence which short-circuits the LLM call; pure win.

## Verification

After merge + deploy, the same student query "Provide me 5 questions from this chapter to practice" should:
1. Match `QUIZ_PATTERNS` → keyword classifier returns `intent='quiz'` with confidence 0.85
2. Short-circuit before LLM classifier
3. Route to `runQuizGenerateWorkflow` (which has its own RAG retrieval + Claude call + P11 validation)
4. Return a `WorkflowResult.metadata.questions: QuizQuestion[]` with 5 valid MCQs

Will validate post-deploy with the trace lookup pattern from this incident.

- Vocabulary 통합 필터 조회 API(`/api/vocabulary`)의 N+1 문제 개선

author: thekk1
body:
fixes thekk1#15:
 
Swap the order of strip_break_spaces_re and break_between_alnum_re in filter_blocks(). Previously, strip_break_spaces_re removed whitespace around all [break] tags first, making them indistinguishable from spurious inline breaks, which break_between_alnum_re then deleted.

With the new order, break_between_alnum_re runs first and only matches [break] tags that have no surrounding whitespace (i.e. genuine inline breaks from span/inline tags). Legitimate paragraph breaks, which always carry surrounding whitespace from the clean_list join, are left intact for strip_break_spaces_re to normalize.

Fixes chapter titles running into body text without pause, e.g.: before: 'Kapitel eins Ich glaube nicht...' after:  'Kapitel eins[pause] Ich glaube nicht...'

author: yjn279
body:
## 概要

X (Twitter) の「ブックマーク長押し → 共有 → Links」経路で発生している `No script URL provided. Make sure the packager is running or you have embedded a JS bundle in your application bundle.` (`unsanitizedScriptURLString = (null)`) を解消する。

このエラーは React Native (`RCTBundleURLProvider` / `RCTBridge.bundleURL`) が JS バンドル URL を解決できなかったときに投げられるネイティブ例外で、本リポジトリの使い方では「Share Extension 内ではなく、Share Extension 経由で起動された **メインアプリ** 側」で発生していると判断した。`expo-share-intent` v5.1.1 の iOS 実装は純粋な `UIViewController + Storyboard` で JS バンドルを一切ロードしないため、Extension 自体は原因になり得ない。Extension は App Group の `UserDefaults` に URL を書き込んで `links://dataUrl=...` でメインアプリを起動するだけで、その先のメインアプリで `main.jsbundle` が解決できない／Metro が到達不能、というのが本症状の本質である。

実機検証を本パイプライン内では行えないため、本 PR は次の二点に絞っている。

1. **原因の文書化と切り分け手順整備** — `docs/share-extension.md` のトラブルシューティング節に「No script URL provided」を追加し、Development / Preview / Release ビルドごとに対処を提示。
2. **本番デバッグ補強** — `app/+native-intent.tsx` の `getShareExtensionKey()` を握りつぶしていた `try/catch` を `console.warn` 出力付きに変更し、再発時にログから切り分け可能にする。

`app.json` の設定（`scheme` 単一文字列、`ios.bundleIdentifier`、`plugins`、`newArchEnabled`）は `expo-share-intent` v5 README と整合済みで、変更は不要と判断した。

## 受け入れ基準

- [x] **原因解析の文書化**: `${RUN_DIR}/notes.md` に React Native の API、Share Extension が JS を持たない根拠（上流 `ShareExtensionViewController.swift` 引用）、ビルドタイプ別仮説、上流リポジトリ外部リンクを記載
- [x] **app.json の設定健全性**: `app.json:8` の `expo.scheme`、`app.json:13` の `bundleIdentifier`、`app.json:32` の `plugins`、`app.json:10` の `newArchEnabled: true` が `expo-share-intent` v5 想定と整合（変更不要）
- [x] **`docs/share-extension.md` のトラブルシューティング追記**: Development / Preview / Release の 3 パターン + X 特有仮説を追記（`docs/share-extension.md:69-139`）
- [x] **既存テスト全 PASS**: 5 スイート / 34 テスト全 PASS（`tests/share-intent.test.ts`、`tests/shareintent.screen.test.tsx`、`tests/native-intent.test.ts` 含む）
- [x] **lint PASS**: `npm run lint` エラー 0、警告 0
- [x] **型検査 PASS**: `npx tsc --noEmit` エラー 0
- [x] **既存 Share Intent 受け取り経路を破壊していない**: `app/+native-intent.tsx:22-25` の `redirectSystemPath` のフォールバック挙動は不変、テスト 7 ケース全 PASS
- [x] **prebuild 整合性（任意）**: 環境制約により未実行、`notes.md` に明記

## Trinity 実行サマリ

- Run: `.trinity/20260510T083042Z-fix-share-ext-script-url`
- Iterations: 1/15
- Final verdict: PASS
- Final commit: c643f9f

## 判定根拠（最終 Evaluator レポートからの抜粋）

本コミットは実機での直接修正ではなく、「原因を正確に文書化し、ユーザーと将来の開発者が自己解決できるようにする」という計画の方針を忠実に実行した。`expo-share-intent` v5 の iOS 実装（`ShareExtensionViewController.swift`）が React Native ブリッジを持たないことを上流ソースから確認し、エラーの発生箇所をメインアプリの `AppDelegate`（`RCTBundleURLProvider`）と特定した根拠が `notes.md` に記録されている。`docs/share-extension.md` には Development / Preview / Release の 3 ビルドタイプ別の対処が追記され、ユーザーが再発時に切り分けを行える。`app.json` の静的チェックで設定不整合がないことを確認済み。テスト 34 件・lint・型検査をすべて独立再実行して PASS を確認した。変更ファイルは計画スコープ内の 2 ファイルのみで、スコープ外への影響はない。

Closes #20

## Summary

- Adds `_scan_personal_signal()` to `events/stop.py` — rules-based JSONL scan on every stop event
- Scans last user turn for 7 category patterns: family, health, creative, emotion, finance, job, date_ref
- Stages matched turns to `personal/candidates` SOIL collection (status: pending)
- Loki review gate reads candidates and decides what writes to sean.db

## Design

Split ownership:
- **Hanuman (this PR):** JSONL → personal/candidates (rules-based, fast, no LLM)
- **Loki:** candidates → sean.db (review gate, human-tier write authorization)

Read-only on sean.db enforced separately in hanuman_cli.py (b0ec0eb, URI ?mode=ro).

## What each candidate record contains

```python
{
    "id": f"candidate-{session_id[:8]}-{timestamp}",
    "session_id": session_id,
    "categories": ["family", "health", ...],   # which patterns fired
    "text_excerpt": text[:300],                 # first 300 chars of user turn
    "status": "pending",
    "created_at": ISO timestamp,
    "reviewed_by": None,
}
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Stop hook fires and writes to personal/candidates when user turn matches a pattern
- [ ] No candidate written when turn < 20 chars or no pattern match
- [ ] Fails silently if JSONL not found (session_id not matched)
- [ ] `personal/candidates` collection readable by Loki review gate

body:
## Why

The project currently has no automated test suite. The Markdown-to-HTML rendering logic in `scripts/render_course.py` is regex-heavy and handles multilingual quiz/glossary parsing. Without tests, regressions are easy to introduce when adding new languages or refactoring parsers.

## What

- Add `tests/test_render_course.py` with 25 unit tests covering:
  - `read_text` (existente, missing, BOM stripping)
  - `parse_first_h1`
  - `parse_glossary` (letters, terms, non-letter section skipping)
  - `_split_numbered` and `_detect_kind`
  - `parse_quiz` (MC, short answer, plain-letter fallback, empty inputs)
  - `derive_flashcards` (from glossary, from quizzes, first-paragraph truncation)
  - `slugify`
- Add `pyproject.toml` with pytest configuration (stdlib-only, no new dependencies).

## How to verify

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_render_course.py -v
```

All 25 tests should pass. No production code was changed.
