body:
…ar sistema" duplicado

Cliente reportó: "Hay una pantalla que sale siempre en Roles cuando refresco que es inicializar el sistema de roles con un boton de inicializar sistema que desaparece no dura ni unos milisegundos. Verifica si ese boton tiene alguna funcionalidad en estos momentos. y por que solo demora unos milisegundos si no funciona eliminalo".

Análisis:
- El botón "Inicializar sistema" SÍ tenía funcionalidad técnica (invocaba seed-system-roles → Cloud Function seedSystemRoles que siembra el catálogo + CEO).
- PERO era duplicado redundante del botón "Resembrar sistema" del header (siempre visible, hace exactamente lo mismo).
- El flicker pasaba porque el primer render usaba defaults (_state.ceoExists=false) → entraba al Caso A "Inicializar sistema" → al llegar el snapshot ~50-200ms después, _state.ceoExists=true → re-render Caso B "Creá tu primer rol personalizado".

Solución: 2 fixes coordinados.

Fix A — Loading state inicial:
- Nuevo flag _state.firstSnapshotReceived (default false)
- Se setea a true en el primer snap callback del listener Firestore
- render() chequea flag: si false, muestra solo header (sin empty state)
- Cuando llega el snapshot real, render con empty state correcto
- Cero flicker entre defaults y data real

Fix B — Caso A eliminado, empty state unificado:
- Antes: 2 casos en empty state Caso A (ceoExists=false): "Inicializar el sistema de roles" + botón Caso B (ceoExists=true):  "Creá tu primer rol personalizado" + botón
- Ahora: 1 solo empty state con texto condicional Si ceoExists=true → "Creá tu primer rol personalizado" + Crear rol Si ceoExists=false (edge) → "Sistema sin inicializar" + texto que dirige al botón "Resembrar sistema" del header (UNA sola fuente de verdad, cero duplicación)
- Botón "Inicializar sistema" eliminado completamente

Cero impacto en funcionalidad:
- Cloud Function seedSystemRoles sigue funcionando (invocable por "Resembrar sistema" del header)
- Caso edge "sistema sin sembrar" sigue cubierto (texto dirige al header)

Tests E2E:
- Cliente con CEO sembrado entra a sec-roles → solo header visible durante loading → empty state "Creá tu primer rol" inmediato
- NO aparece pantalla "Inicializar sistema" parpadeante
- NO aparece botón "Inicializar sistema"
- Botón "Resembrar sistema" del header sigue OK
- Caso edge (borrar CEO manual): empty state "Sistema sin inicializar"
  + texto que dirige al header (sin botón duplicado)

Anti-patterns evitados:
- §17.4: cero IDs renombrados, solo lógica del render
- §17.12: cero MutationObserver
- §35: cero pointermove
- §17 perf: loading state evita render con defaults — UN solo render real cuando llega el snapshot
- Big Bang: cero deploy backend, Cloud Function seedSystemRoles preservada (utility legítima)
- §61: R8.3 hotfix UX puntual

### Motivation

- Prepare the project to run in a VPS production environment using Docker Compose with a containerized PostgreSQL and a standalone Next.js production image. 
- Ensure the web service is production-ready with a non-root runtime, healthcheck, environment-driven secrets, and a documented deployment workflow. 
- Provide operational tooling and guidance for migrations, backups, admin bootstrap, and optional Nginx reverse proxy with HTTPS-ready configuration.

### Description

- Add a production-ready web `Dockerfile` that builds the Next.js standalone output, includes a `tools` target for DB tasks, runs as a non-root user, exposes internal port `3000`, and includes a container `HEALTHCHECK` that calls `GET /api/health` (`apps/web/Dockerfile`).
- Add `docker-compose.prod.yml` with services `postgres`, `web`, a one-off `migrate` tools service, and an optional `nginx` profile, including a persistent `postgres` volume, env-file support, healthchecks, and localhost-only web port binding for reverse proxying.
- Implement `GET /api/health` at `apps/web/app/api/health/route.ts` which checks DB connectivity using `prisma.$queryRaw` and returns `{ ok, database, timestamp }`, responding `503` if the DB is unreachable.
- Add `docs/deployment.md` with VPS-focused step-by-step guidance covering server requirements, Docker installation, cloning, `.env` setup, migrations, creating the first admin, running containers, Nginx/HTTPS guidance, updating, and backup/restore and security notes.
- Add operational helpers: `Makefile` with `dev`, `prod-up`, `prod-down`, `logs`, `migrate`, `seed`, `backup`, and `restore` targets, plus a `.dockerignore` to keep secrets and local artifacts out of builds.
- Add an example host Nginx config at `deploy/nginx/parcel-society.conf.example` that reverse-proxies `https://your-domain.com` to `http://127.0.0.1:3000` and an updated `.env.example` showing production env variables.
- Add `db:deploy` script to `packages/db/package.json` which uses `prisma db push` for schema deployment in the current repo state.

### Testing

- `git diff --check` was run and reported no whitespace/errors in diffs (success). 
- Basic JSON validation of `package.json` and `packages/db/package.json` was performed with `python3` and succeeded (success). 
- `pnpm install` was attempted but failed due to a `403 Forbidden` when fetching `@tailwindcss/postcss` from the configured registry, preventing installation of `node_modules` (failed). 
- Typechecks and build-related checks (`pnpm --filter @parcel-society/web typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @parcel-society/db typecheck`) could not complete because dependencies were not installed after the registry failure (blocked). 
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml config` could not be run in this environment because Docker is not available (not executed).

author: jbbqqf
body:
Fixes #7990.

## Summary

`Dataset.map` crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'` when the user's map function returned `None` for the first few examples and a `dict` (or `pa.Table` / DataFrame) for later ones.

The writer was initialized only when `i == 0` (or `i[0] == 0` in batched mode). If `update_data` flipped to `True` only on a later call, `i != 0`, so the writer was never initialized, and the next `writer.write(...)` raised.

This PR:

1. **Initializes the writer lazily** on the first non-`None` result (`if writer is None`), regardless of the example/batch index.
2. **Latches `update_data`** so it stays `True` once any non-`None` result has been seen. The previous walrus assignment (`update_data := (processed_inputs is not None)`) silently flipped the flag back to `False` on subsequent `None` returns, which caused the post-loop `if update_data: writer.finalize() ...` to no-op and silently dropped the writer's accumulated rows (the inverse `dict-then-None` pattern).
3. **Skips writes for `None` results** now that `update_data` no longer flips back.

## Reproduce BEFORE/AFTER yourself (copy-paste)

The only thing that changes between the two blocks is the checked-out git ref.

```bash
# --- BEFORE: origin/main, expect AttributeError ---
git fetch origin main
git checkout origin/main
python - <<'PY'
from datasets import Dataset
ds = Dataset.from_dict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
def fn(example, idx):
    return None if idx < 2 else {"x": example["x"] * 10}
try:
    ds.map(fn, with_indices=True)
    print("NO CRASH")  # Expected: not reached
except AttributeError as e:
    print(f"REPRO: {e}")  # Expected: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'
PY

# --- AFTER: this branch, expect no crash and correct output ---
git fetch origin pull/<PR>/head:fix
git checkout fix
python - <<'PY'
from datasets import Dataset
ds = Dataset.from_dict({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
def fn(example, idx):
    return None if idx < 2 else {"x": example["x"] * 10}
out = ds.map(fn, with_indices=True)
print(out["x"])  # Expected: [30]
PY
```

## What I ran locally

```
pytest tests/test_arrow_dataset.py -k "test_map or test_filter or test_class_encode_column"
# 63 passed, 10 skipped (Beam-related, pre-existing)
```

The new regression test `test_map_mixed_none_and_dict_returns` fails on `origin/main` with the exact `AttributeError` from the issue, and passes on this branch.

## Edge cases covered by the new test

| Pattern | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `None, None, dict` (the issue) | crash: `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'` | `[30]` |
| `dict, dict, None` | silently returns the **original** shard (writer never finalized because `update_data` flipped back to False) | `[10, 20]` |
| `dict, None, dict` (alternating) | crash on the second `dict` write because `update_data` was False at that point | `[10, 30]` |
| All `None` | unchanged | unchanged |
| All `dict` | unchanged | unchanged |
| Batched variants of the same | same crashes / silent drops | correct |

## Notes

- The lazy `if writer is None` init makes the location of the first dict-return irrelevant.
- The latch on `update_data` is necessary because the post-loop `if update_data: writer.finalize() ...` previously read whatever the **last** call set it to. A `dict, dict, None` sequence currently leaves `update_data == False` and silently drops the writer's accumulated rows. This is fixed here.
- No public API change.

---

🤖 Disclosure: This PR was authored with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), reviewed and tested by me. The reproducer was run end-to-end on this branch (`pytest tests/test_arrow_dataset.py -k test_map`), and the regression test was verified to fail on `origin/main` and pass on this branch.

body:
## Summary

Migrates opencatalogi's local `src/store/modules/object.js` (~2.5k lines) onto the canonical `@conduction/nextcloud-vue` `useObjectStore` via a thin-wrap pattern. **No Vue file is touched** — all 697 callsites + 60 distinct call patterns continue to work because the outer Pinia store named `'object'` preserves the entire public API surface.

The wrapper delegates CRUD to `createObjectStore('opencatalogi-objects-inner', { plugins: [...] })` while keeping 10 categories of opencatalogi-specific behaviour locally (active-object map, related-data fan-out, settings + dynamic type registration, columnFilters, mass operations, attachment publish/depublish, per-object errors, search debounce, lifecycle signature shims, cross-schema `createObject` override).

Net win: `fetchObject` (the missing method that bit decidesk #162) is now backed by the lib, plus `liveUpdatesPlugin` / `auditTrailsPlugin` / `filesPlugin` / `relationsPlugin` / `lifecyclePlugin` / `selectionPlugin` are mounted.

## Migration pattern

**Thin-wrap** — outer store (id `'object'`) preserves API; inner store (id `'opencatalogi-objects-inner'`) provides canonical CRUD + plugins. See `openspec/changes/opencatalogi-store-migration/design.md` for full per-module disposition + gap analysis.

| Module | Disposition |
|---|---|
| src/store/modules/object.js | Thin-wrap lib useObjectStore + 6 plugins |
| src/store/modules/catalog.js | Kept local (calls /api/{catalogSlug}) |
| src/store/modules/navigation.ts | Kept local (pure UI state) |
| src/store/modules/search.ts | Kept local (federation API) |
| src/store/store.js | Unchanged barrel |

## Plugin availability

All 6 plugins requested in the plan importable from @conduction/nextcloud-vue@1.0.0-beta.14:

author: nightbaker
body:
Closes #497

## Summary

- Wraps three `PerformEffects` switch cases (`StartChildWorkflowCommand`, `AddConditionsCommand`, `EvaluateActivationConditionCommand`) in try/catch — matching the pattern established for `RegisterMessageCommand` in #425
- Catch handler uses `_state.FindEntry(activityInstanceId)?.ActivityId` (nullable, safe in catch) to call `FailActivity`; if the entry is already gone, the exception is swallowed without failing (the activity is no longer active)
- Removes the now-resolved `#497` TODO comment from the `RegisterMessageCommand` case

## Key decisions

- **`FindEntry` over `GetActiveEntry` in catch**: `GetActiveEntry` throws on missing entry — using it in a catch block would mask the original exception. `FindEntry` is the nullable variant.
- **`activityId is not null` guard**: In the (unlikely) case the entry has been removed from state before the catch runs, FailActivity is safely skipped.
- **`BuildChildInputVariables` does NOT throw on missing variables**: It uses `TryGetValue`, silently skipping unmapped variables. The realistic throw trigger for all three cases is `GetActiveEntry` on a non-existent instance (state/programming error). Defensive wrapping is still correct for future changes.
- **`StartChildWorkflowCommand` phantom `ChildWorkflowLinked`**: If `GetActiveEntry` succeeds but a later line throws, `ChildWorkflowLinked` would already be emitted. This pre-existing concern is out of scope for this fix (the child grain never receives `StartWorkflow` in this case).

## Tests

Three new tests in `WorkflowExecutionProcessCommandsTests`:
- `ProcessCommands_StartChildWorkflowCommand_UnknownActivityInstanceId_DoesNotThrow`
- `ProcessCommands_AddConditionsCommand_UnknownActivityInstanceId_DoesNotThrow`
- `ProcessCommands_EvaluateActivationConditionCommand_UnknownActivityInstanceId_DoesNotThrow`

Each passes a non-existent `activityInstanceId` which triggers `GetActiveEntry` to throw inside the Process* method. Verifies: no exception propagates, effects are empty (FailActivity skipped because FindEntry returns null).

Full domain test suite: 414/414 passing.

author: walenhill
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition in `bookSlot` and `cancelBooking`. Concurrent requests could potentially double-book the same slot if they passed the PHP-level check simultaneously before the UPDATE query executed.
🎯 Impact: Data integrity issue causing multiple clients to successfully book the exact same timeslot, leading to overlapping appointments and business confusion.
🔧 Fix: Moved the state requirement (`status = 'available'` or `status = 'booked'`) into the `UPDATE` query's `WHERE` clause to make the state transition atomic at the database level. Added check for `$stmt->affected_rows === 0` to return an appropriate error if the slot was concurrently modified.
✅ Verification: Review the SQL queries in `backend/includes/slots_crud.php` to verify atomic updates. Ensure `php backend/tests/HelpersTest.php` and `php backend/tests/AuthTest.php` pass successfully.

author: joestump
body:
## Summary

Layers full SHA-256 pin enforcement on top of the foundation override hatch introduced in #139. Adds the `npm run docs:refresh-overrides -- <skill-name>` helper that rewrites the pin in place after the author re-reviews the override against the new SKILL.md.

**Stacked on #139** — review #139 first.

## Pin contract

- Pin format: `{/* Governing-SKILL: skills/{name}/SKILL.md@<sha256> */}` as the first non-blank line of `skills/{name}/page.override.mdx`.
- Hash scope: full bytes of `SKILL.md`, no normalization, no trimming (per SPEC-0021 design.md OQ #5).
- Match → copy override verbatim, skip auto-generation, skip `mdx-escape.js` (author owns override).
- Mismatch / missing pin / orphan → fail build with a named error + refresh-overrides remediation pointer.

## Files

- `docs-site/scripts/transform-skills.js` — `loadOverride(skillDir, skillName)` now enforces the pin; the no-op pass-through from #139 is replaced. Adds an upfront orphan-override scan so overrides for un-registered or removed skills fail the build (the manifest loop alone wouldn't visit them).
- `docs-site/scripts/refresh-overrides.js` — new. Single-skill scope (rejects multi-arg invocations per design.md OQ #2). Rewrites only the pin line; if the override lacks a pin, inserts one as a new first line. All other bytes preserved.
- `docs-site/package.json` — adds the `docs:refresh-overrides` script.
- `docs-site/scripts/__tests__/override-pin.test.js` — Node-built-in test (`node:test`) for: pin parsing, hash computation, every `loadOverride` failure mode, byte-identical preservation in the refresh helper.

## Failure mode coverage

| Condition | Error |
|---|---|
| Override exists, SKILL.md missing | `…page.override.mdx: orphan override — skills/X/SKILL.md does not exist…` |
| Override missing the pin header | `…missing or malformed Governing-SKILL pin header…npm run docs:refresh-overrides -- X…` |
| Override pin doesn't match disk | `…stale Governing-SKILL pin. expected (pinned): …, current (on disk): …. Re-review…npm run docs:refresh-overrides -- X…` |

## Test plan

- [ ] `node --test docs-site/scripts/__tests__/override-pin.test.js` (framework-free; only requires Node 20+)
- [ ] Stack on #139 and run `npm run build` once with no overrides — should still produce the same auto-generated pages
- [ ] Drop a fixture `skills/list/page.override.mdx` with a stale pin → confirm build fails with the spec-mandated error message
- [ ] Run `npm run docs:refresh-overrides -- list` → confirm the override file's pin line is updated and every other byte is unchanged
- [ ] Run `npm run build` again → confirm the override is now used verbatim
- [ ] Remove the `Governing-SKILL` line entirely → confirm build fails with the missing-pin error
- [ ] Move `skills/list/SKILL.md` aside → confirm orphan-override error fires before the manifest check

## Build verification limitation

Same as #139 — agent sandbox blocked `npm install` and node script execution. The Node built-in test runner (`node:test`) is used instead of Jest so the tests run on a clean checkout without an extra dependency install.

Closes #141
Part of #137 (SPEC-0021)

# 二、核心区别总表

| 维度 | util | plugin |
|---|---|---|
| 定位 | 工具库、纯能力 | Vue 插件、全局能力扩展 |
| 目标 | 解决某个小问题 | 扩展整个应用的能力 |

| 使用方式 | 直接 import 调用 | `app.use(...)` 安装后全局使用 |
| 是否有副作用 | 通常尽量无副作用 | 常带副作用，如挂全局属性 |
| 适合内容 | 函数、常量、格式化、校验 | 缓存、弹窗、标签页、下载、登录态集成 |
| 复用粒度 | 细粒度 | 中/粗粒度 |
| 测试难度 | 低 | 中高 |
| 维护成本 | 低 | 较高 |
| 典型例子 | `validate.js`, `request.js` | `modal.js`, `tab.js` |

---

# 三、能力对比

## 1) util 的能力
`util` 的能力特点是：

### 更偏“函数化”
比如：
- 日期格式化
- 表单重置
- 树形数据处理
- 权限判断
- 校验规则
- 请求封装
- 滚动到指定位置

这些通常是**一次调用、立即返回结果**。

### 更偏“局部复用”
比如：
- 某个页面要做手机号校验
- 某个列表要把扁平数组转树
- 某个请求要统一封装
- 某个组件要根据权限显示按钮

### 更偏“无状态”
大多数 util：
- 不持有 UI 状态
- 不依赖组件实例
- 不需要安装
- 更适合纯逻辑

---

## 2) plugin 的能力
`plugin` 的能力特点是：

### 更偏“系统级”
比如：
- 弹窗统一调用
- 下载统一封装
- 标签页控制
- 认证上下文注入
- 缓存能力暴露

### 更偏“全局可访问”
安装后，页面里的组件可能直接：
- `this.$modal`
- `this.$download`
- `this.$tab`
- `this.$cache`

### 更偏“有上下文”
plugin 往往和：
- Vue app
- 全局配置
- Pinia store
- 路由
- DOM 行为
耦合更强。

---

# 四、实现方式对比

## 1) util 怎么实现
你这个项目里的 util 通常是下面几种形式：

### a. 导出函数
```js
export function parseTime() {}
export function resetForm() {}
```

### b. 导出对象
```js
export default {
  ...,
}
```

### c. 导出常量/规则
```js
export const validRules = {}
```

### d. 组合导出
`index.js` 统一导出，方便引用。

---

## util 的实现特征
- 尽量不依赖 Vue 生命周期
- 尽量不操作全局 DOM
- 尽量不挂全局变量
- 只关注输入输出

---

## 2) plugin 怎么实现
plugin 通常是 Vue 插件标准写法：

### a. 提供 `install`
```js
export default {
  install(app) {
    app.config.globalProperties.$modal = ...
  }
}
```

### b. 或导出一个插件对象/函数
```js
const plugin = {
  install(app) {}
}
```

然后在 `main.js`：

```js
app.use(plugins)
```

---

## 你这个项目中的 plugin 特征
从 `src/main.js` 看：

```js
app.use(plugins)
```

说明 `plugins/index.js` 会把多个插件统一安装进 app。

并且 `main.js` 还做了：

```js
app.config.globalProperties.useDict = useDict
app.config.globalProperties.download = download
app.config.globalProperties.getConfigKey = getConfigKey
...
```

这说明有些“工具能力”也被提升成了全局可访问能力。

---

# 五、开发方式对比

## 1) 开发 util 的方式
写 util 时，重点是：

### 要求
- 接口简单
- 入参明确
- 输出稳定
- 不要隐藏副作用
- 单个函数职责单一

### 开发风格
- 更像写通用函数库
- 更注重可测试性
- 更容易独立单测

### 典型问题
- 功能过多导致一个 util 变成“杂物箱”
- 命名不统一
- 过度依赖全局状态

---

## 2) 开发 plugin 的方式
写 plugin 时，重点是：

### 要求
- 统一安装入口
- 全局注入清晰
- 命名规范
- 避免和 Vue 原生属性冲突
- 注意副作用和初始化顺序

### 开发风格
- 更像写框架扩展层
- 通常要考虑安装时机
- 常与 store、router、modal、cache 配合

### 典型问题
- plugin 之间耦合太重
- 初始化顺序错误
- 全局属性命名污染
- 依赖 `app.use()` 后才生效

---

# 六、使用方式对比

## 1) util 的使用
直接 import：

```js
import { parseTime } from '@/utils'
```

或者：

```js
import { download } from '@/utils/request'
```

### 特点
- 用多少引多少
- 局部引用
- tree-shaking 友好
- 逻辑清晰

---

## 2) plugin 的使用
先安装：

```js
app.use(plugins)
```

然后在组件里使用：

```js
this.$modal.msgSuccess(...)
this.$download(...)
```

或者通过全局属性间接访问。

### 特点
- 一次安装，全局可用
- 适合项目级通用能力
- 组件里调用方便
- 但隐藏依赖更强

---

# 七、结合你这个项目的具体分析

---

## `utils` 更像“业务基础设施”
比如：

### `auth.js`
处理认证相关辅助逻辑

### `permission.js`
处理权限判断

### `request.js`
封装 axios 请求，统一拦截器、错误处理

### `dict.js`
处理字典数据获取和展示

### `validate.js`
处理各种校验函数

### `boot.js`
更像项目工具集合，承载多个通用方法

这些都属于“一个个拿来就能用的函数”。

---

author: loonghao
body:
## Summary

Fourth migration in the **#852 chain**. Moves the two smallest self-contained sub-configs of `McpHttpConfig` — `JobConfig` (#328 + #567) and `WorkflowConfig` (#348 + #352) — into `dcc-mcp-http-types::config`.

Both depend only on `PathBuf` + `JobRecoveryPolicy` (already in `http-types` since #899), so the dependency direction stays strictly inward.

## What moves

| Symbol | Now at | Old path (re-exported) |
|---|---|---|
| `JobConfig` { `job_storage_path`, `job_recovery` } | `dcc_mcp_http_types::config::JobConfig` | `dcc_mcp_http::config::JobConfig` |
| `WorkflowConfig` { `enable_workflows`, `enable_scheduler`, `schedules_dir` } | `dcc_mcp_http_types::config::WorkflowConfig` | same |

`crates/dcc-mcp-http/src/config.rs` widens its existing `pub use dcc_mcp_http_types::config::{...}` line to include the two structs. The `McpHttpConfig` aggregate keeps composing them via `cfg.job: JobConfig` / `cfg.workflow: WorkflowConfig`, so every existing consumer path (`cfg.job.job_recovery`, `cfg.workflow.enable_workflows`, `with_job_recovery`, `with_workflows_enabled`, …) keeps compiling.

## Design choices

- **`Serialize` + `Deserialize` derives added** on both structs — the gateway / http server historically didn't round-trip them through serde, but external config validators and the future per-section CLI plumbing will. Adding the derives now is cheap (just attribute additions) and keeps every config-shape round-trip cohesive across the four enums + two structs already migrated.
- **`skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` on optional paths** so pristine-boot configs serialise compactly without explicit `null`s in the wire form.
- **Pristine-boot defaults pinned by tests.** `WorkflowConfig` defaults both opt-in switches to `false` so the minimal MCP surface is what boots; `JobConfig` defaults to in-memory storage + `Drop` recovery (today's behaviour). New tests `workflow_config_default_disables_both_subsystems` and `job_config_default_is_in_memory_with_drop_policy` pin those contracts.

## New wire-contract tests in `http-types`

- `job_config_default_is_in_memory_with_drop_policy`
- `job_config_serialises_skip_none_storage` — pins the compact wire form
- `job_config_round_trips_with_storage_path`
- `job_config_accepts_minimal_body` — `{}` must deserialise to defaults (env-var plumbing relies on this)
- `workflow_config_default_disables_both_subsystems`
- `workflow_config_round_trips`
- `workflow_config_skip_none_schedules_dir`
- `workflow_config_accepts_minimal_body`

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace` ✅
- `cargo test -p dcc-mcp-http-types` ✅ (33 total: 24 prior + 9 new)
- `cargo test -p dcc-mcp-http --lib config::` ✅ (11 tests — builder + env-var plumbing still green)
- `cargo clippy -p dcc-mcp-http-types --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo clippy -p dcc-mcp-http --no-deps --tests -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✅

## Follow-up

Next in the #852 chain: `TelemetryConfig` (Prometheus metrics — pure value type, easy seed) and `FeatureFlags` (8 self-contained bools), then the harder `ServerConfig` / `InstanceConfig` / `SessionConfig` / `GatewayConfig` / `QueueConfig` (these need careful read because they touch `IpAddr`, `std::time::Duration`, and other typed fields that may need `humantime` for clean wire shapes).

Builds on #895, #897, #899, #900. Part of #848 epic.

author: milesburton
body:
## Summary

Curated subset of changes from a parallel security/quality review session. Keeps the genuine security wins and dead-code cleanup; drops the over-applied prototype-pollution defenses (see "What was deliberately left out" below).

### Real fixes
- **`gateway/routes/logs.ts`** — escape backslashes *before* quotes when building Loki LogQL from user-supplied search input. Prior code escaped only quotes, so a `\"`-prefixed payload could inject regex metacharacters.
- **`gatewayMiddleware`** — `sanitizeLogEntry()` strips CR/LF from `console.warn`/`console.error` arguments, defending against log-injection from gateway-error/order-rejected payloads.
- **`useSessionRecording`** — replace `Math.random()` with `crypto.getRandomValues()` for session-ID entropy. Session IDs benefit from CSPRNG output.
- **`capture-grafana-screenshots.mjs`** — validate PNG magic bytes (`89 50 4E 47`) before writing to disk, so a misconfigured Grafana returning HTML/JSON doesn't produce silently-broken screenshot files.
- **`user-service.ts parseOAuthClients`** — drop default-then-overwrite for `redirectPart`; every branch already assigns it. Slight definite-assignment narrowing.
- **`risk-bypass.test.ts findProducers`** — generalize regex escape so the helper still works if topic names ever include metacharacters beyond `.`.

### Dead-code cleanup
- `electron-dev.mjs`: remove a `req` declaration that was always `null`.
- `playwright.electron.config.ts`: drop unused `path` import.
- `AlgoMonitor.tsx`: simplify trade-at-last title — the `marketPrice ? formatPrice(marketPrice) : "—"` ternary was unreachable behind an early-return that guarantees `marketPrice` is truthy.
- `frontend/tests/{fixtures,observability,panels,screenshots}`: drop unused imports.

## What was deliberately left out

The parallel session also added a `keyValidation.ts` utility and `isValidKey` guards on every `state.bySymbol[symbol]` write across `advisorySlice`, `intelligenceSlice`, `newsSlice`, `windowSlice`, and parts of `gatewayMiddleware`. After review, those were dropped because:

1. **Wrong threat model.** `obj["__proto__"] = x` is treated as an accessor write by modern V8/SpiderMonkey, not a prototype-pollution vector.
2. **Wrong layer.** Input validation belongs at the WebSocket message boundary, not duplicated across every reducer.
3. **Silent-failure mode.** Each guard turned a write into a no-op on validation failure with no log/warning, hiding real upstream bugs (e.g. an empty-string symbol from a parsing issue would silently disappear).
4. **Over-broad denylist.** `hasOwnProperty`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `toLocaleString` are not pollution vectors — they're just inherited methods that are harmless to shadow on per-object Records.
5. **Misleading framing.** A client-side ID regex on `useWorkspaceSync.ts` was labelled "prevent request forgery" — that's not what it does (CSRF is a different problem; server-side validation is the security boundary).

If a real prototype-pollution risk surfaces from a specific upstream input, the fix should be at the WebSocket message validator, not sprayed across every reducer.

## Test plan
- [x] Backend: lint + type-check + 464 unit tests pass
- [x] Frontend: Biome clean (formatter auto-wrapped one long line in `gatewayMiddleware.ts`), tsc clean, 1736 vitest tests pass
- [x] Pre-commit hook (8 checks) passes
- [ ] Visual smoke after merge to confirm session recording, log panel, and Grafana screenshot capture still work

author: jrakibi
body:
Currently we loop over blocks and call `process_block()` for each 64-byte chunk, which loads/saves state into SIMD registers on each call. Instead we can move the loop inside the intrinsic function so that state stays in registers across blocks.

This shows around ~8% improvement for x86 SHA-NI (EC2 c7i-flex.large instance)
For ARM I didn't see much improvement but the code is updated to stay consistent with x86.

body:
## Summary

- Add drone restriction zone providers for **France** and the **United Kingdom** alongside the existing Spain (ENAIRE) provider
- Each country can be toggled independently via checkboxes in the Visualization settings under **Extra layers**

## Details

### France (DGAC)
- Queries the **Géoplateforme WFS** (`data.geopf.fr`) for the `carte_restriction_drones_lf` layer
- Returns UAS restriction zones for open category / aeromodelling across metropolitan France and overseas territories
- Maps `"Vol interdit"` → prohibited (red), height restrictions → restricted (orange)
- No authentication required, returns GeoJSON natively via WFS `GetFeature` with bbox filtering

### United Kingdom (NATS)
- Downloads the **NATS KMZ** flight restriction dataset (published every 28-day AIRAC cycle)
- Lazy-fetches on first request overlapping UK bounds, caches in memory with 24h TTL
- Parses KML → GeoJSON (using `fast-xml-parser` + `jszip`)

author: stefanobaghino
body:
Closes the parse-throughput gap with syntect on realistic JS workloads. On a per-process highlight of jquery.js (247 KB, 9 210 lines) wall time goes from 2.04 s on `main` to 359 ms — a 5.7× speedup that puts us at ~1.47× syntect 5.3.0's `syncat` baseline on the same hardware. Before this PR we were at ~8× syntect's wall time on this workload.

## What changed

Three independent levers in `src/pegvm/vm.rs` and `src/walk.rs`, summarised by where the time was actually going:

`OpenCapture` is now `Copy`. All its fields are already `Copy`; the missing derive on the struct was the only thing keeping `Vec`'s memcpy specialisation off the slice clones inside `protect_max_captures`'s `to_vec()` and the related capture-replay paths. ~24 % wall-clock win on its own.

`protect_max_captures` saves only the *suffix* being dropped from the watermark prefix instead of cloning the whole prefix. The previous strategy cloned `captures[..max_captures_len]` on every endangered backtrack — on a successful jquery.js parse that was ~80 k clones × ~750 KB each ≈ 60 GB of `to_vec()` memcpy under the ~50 GB/s memory-bandwidth ceiling, ~1.2 s of pure copying. The new scheme displaces only `captures[new_len..saved_lower]` into a back-to-front buffer; over an `max_sp` epoch each capture is saved at most once, so the cumulative copy traffic drops to ≤ `max_captures_len × sizeof(OpenCapture)` ≈ 40 MB on jquery.js. This is the headline change; ~4.2× on top of the `Copy` win. See the field doc on `VM::saved_lower` / `VM::saved_above`.

`walk` is now a single linear sweep over the captures slice instead of materialising sorted Begin/End events. Captures arrive from the VM in pre-order forest traversal — `start`-ascending, parent before child, see the doc comment on `pegvm::Capture` — so an active-capture stack with the same end-pop semantics gives the same output without the `O(N log N)` sort or the auxiliary event vector. Behaviour-identical (md5 match on the full jquery.js render). Flat on the wall clock here but cleaner code, and fewer moving pieces if anyone investigates the post-VM cost in the future.

## Benchmark results

`hyperfine -N --warmup 3` on M1 Pro, our `target/release/demo`:

| fixture | main | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `medium.js` (1.8 KB) | 8.3 ms | 8.4 ms | flat — input too small for the prefix bloat to bite |
| `xlarge.js` (138 KB) | 1117 ms | 216 ms | 5.16× |
| `jquery.js` (247 KB) | 2043 ms | 359 ms | 5.69× |

`benches/memo.rs` `xlarge` cells (median-of-11 µs at default threshold 128), captured with `.claude/skills/memo-bench/compare.sh main pegvm-parse-throughput memo`:

| grammar | main | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rust/xlarge` | 1 337 942 µs | 189 903 µs | 7.04× |
| `sql/xlarge` | 482 930 µs | 161 973 µs | 2.98× |
| `toml/xlarge` | 13 816 µs | 4 537 µs | 3.05× |
| `json/xlarge` | 13 355 µs | 12 752 µs | 1.05× (flat) |

Speedup scales with how much the grammar backtracks and how large the watermark prefix grows. Rust's operator-precedence cascades are the worst offender on `main`; JSON's roughly-LL grammar barely backtracks, so `protect_max_captures` was barely firing and there was nothing to fix. `large` cells track the same shape at smaller magnitudes; `medium` and `small` are within ±5 % noise.

## Syntect comparison

Trajectory only — workloads aren't apples-to-apples (different grammar maturity, different tokenisation granularity, syntect's regex backend is oniguruma, ours is pure PEG) but the methodology matches and both numbers include per-process startup + asset/grammar load + parse + ANSI render + write to a hyperfine-captured stdout sink:

| | jquery.js wall time | source |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 359 ± 11 ms | `hyperfine 1.20.0 -N --warmup 3`, 10 runs, M1 Pro |
| `main` | 2043 ± 11 ms | same |
| syntect 5.3.0 `syncat` | 245 ± 3.4 ms | upstream baseline summary, same hardware/flags |

The motivating workload, samply attribution side-quests, the negative-result `vm-chunked-arena` rewrite that came before this much smaller fix turned out to be the right lever, and the suffix-save analysis are written up in `~/.claude/plans/a-combination-of-if-piped-wave.md` for posterity.

author: haakonsvane
body:
## Context

The group detail page was framed as a database record — three tabs labeled Games / Members / Trophies — which buried the things members actually want when they open it: who's winning, what just happened, and the quickest path to handing out a new reward. This PR redesigns the page around those three jobs and tightens a few cross-cutting design rules along the way.

## What's changed

- **Added** `Group.recentActivity(first: Int)` on the API — returns a typed union of `TrophyAwardedActivity` and `MemberJoinedActivity`, derived from existing tables (no new schema). Bounded to `[1, 50]` server-side.
- **Added** `Trophy.awardedBy: User` so the activity feed can attribute "Alice awarded X to Bob".
- **Added** an integration test covering the happy path: trophy + member-join events surface newest-first with the right `__typename`s.
- **Redesigned** `groups/$id` as a single scrolling story: hero header (group name, tagline, primary "Award trophy" CTA) → top-performer card + members card row → activity feed (main column) + games sidebar (right). Tab structure removed.
- **Added** new components: `GroupHero`, `GroupTopPerformer`, `GroupMembersCard` (with a "see all" drawer), `GroupActivityFeed`, `GroupAside`, plus a zero-dep `formatRelativeTime` helper using `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`.
- **Added** a shared `Breadcrumb` component built on shadcn primitives, replacing five hand-rolled breadcrumb instances across dashboard, groups, group detail, game detail, and auth pages. Container paddings aligned to `py-10 sm:py-14` so chrome sits at the same vertical offset everywhere.
- **Refactored** the games card layout (buttons moved to a footer row separated by a 1px border) so it stops squeezing in the 320px sidebar.
- **Reserved** the 3D `MedalBadge` for awarded trophies only — games now render with a plain emoji per the design language. `MedalBadge` is still used in `TrophyAvatar` and the activity feed (both for actual awards).
- **Tightened** icon-only button proportions: encoded chunkier icon sizes into the `icon`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg` button variants so they read as substantial affordances without per-call overrides.
- **Removed** `GroupSocialCard` and `GroupPodium` — content absorbed into the new hero and replaced by the cleaner top-performer card respectively.

author: thiagotigaz
body:
## Summary

\`Changeset.riskChip\` was always null. The schema field, the digest chip styling, and the changeset detail page all already render \`cs.riskChip ?? 'low'\`, so the column existed only to be set.

Computes a heuristic risk level right after the PR opens, persisting it alongside \`prNumber\` / \`prUrl\`. Signals (in order of weight):

1. **Sensitive paths touched** — auth / billing / migrations / IaC / GitHub workflows / \`mergecrew.yaml\` / role-guard → \`high\`. A reviewer almost always wants to look at these.
2. **Test failures** upgrade severity by one bucket when paired with a non-trivial diff; small diffs with red tests stay \`medium\` since one-line changes are plausibly flakes, not structural risk.
3. **Diff size** — total additions+deletions and file count.

Best-effort: a failure to fetch PR files (transient API blip) leaves the chip null and the UI defaults to \`low\` rather than failing the changeset.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @mergecrew/runner test\` — 11 tests pass covering each branch:
  - small clean diff → low
  - moderate diff → medium
  - 6+ files touched → medium
  - very large diff → high
  - sensitive path override (auth, billing, migrations, GitHub workflows) → high
  - test failure + small diff → medium (probably flake)
  - test failure + non-trivial diff → high
- [x] Inaugural test suite for the \`@mergecrew/runner\` package.
- [x] \`pnpm typecheck\` + \`pnpm test\` clean across the workspace.

Closes #193.

body: Two related improvements to the recording configuration UX: ### 1. `/recordings` page - **Per-model edit panel** in the model detail view: change recording **resolution** (`best / 1080p / 720p / 480p / 360p`), **retention (days)**, and **auto-record** state, then save. - **Effective resolution hint** beneath the dropdown — shows the height the model will actually be recorded at, after combining the per-model value with the global cap. Goes amber when the global cap is the binding constraint (e.g. per-model `best` with `max_resolution: 480` shows `Effective: 480p (capped by global max 480p — Settings)`). - **7-day activity timeline**: one bar per day for the last 7 days (oldest → newest). Each recording is a green segment positioned by its `createdAt` and sized by `duration`. Recordings spanning midnight are clipped across rows. Hovering shows filename / start / end / duration; clicking opens the player. - **Blinking "now" line**: red, animated vertical marker on today's row at the current local time, refreshes every 30 s. - Hour ticks (`0h`, `3h`, … `24h`) under the grid for orientation. ### 2. Default vs. Max resolution `max_resolution` was being conflated with "default for new models". Split into two distinct settings, both surfaced in **Settings → Recording**: - **Default Recording Resolution** (`default_resolution`) — applied to a model's `record_quality` when auto-record is **turned on**: - `POST /api/models` with no `recordQuality` and `autoRecord: true`. - `PATCH /api/models/{username}/auto-record` on an off → on transition. Per-model values can still be edited afterward and will not be overwritten on subsequent edits. - **Max Recording Resolution** (`max_resolution`) — unchanged hard cap. No model can exceed it even if its per-model value is higher. ## Test plan Backend: - [ ] `GET /api/settings/recording` returns `default_resolution` (0 when unset). - [ ] `PUT /api/settings/recording {"default_resolution": 720}` persists and is reflected in subsequent GETs. - [ ] `PUT /api/settings/recording {"default_resolution": 999}` returns 400. - [ ] With `default_resolution=720`, toggling a model's auto-record from off to on sets `record_quality` to `"720p"`. The reverse toggle does not change the quality. Verified end-to-end with `aslhyn_gomez` during development. - [ ] `POST /api/models {"username": "x", "autoRecord": true}` (no `recordQuality`) creates the model with `record_quality` equal to the configured default. - [ ] `POST /api/models {"username": "y", "autoRecord": true, "recordQuality": "1080p"}` honours the explicit value. Frontend: - [ ] `/settings` shows two distinct rows: "Default" and "Max" recording resolution with the right defaults loaded from the API. - [ ] Changing either select issues a `PUT` and shows a "Setting updated" toast. - [ ] `/recordings` → click a model: edit panel pre-fills with the model's current values; "Effective" hint matches `min(global_cap, per_model)` and goes amber when capped. - [ ] Saving updates the API and the dropdown survives reload. - [ ] Untracked-model detail pre-selects the global default in the dropdown; "Add & Save" enrols the model with that quality. - [ ] Timeline shows 7 day rows, today highlighted, recordings rendered at correct hour-of-day, midnight-spanning recordings clipped across rows, hover tooltip + click-to-play work, blinking red "now" line drifts forward over a few minutes. - [ ] Going back to the model grid stops the now-line interval. ## Notes - Static asset uses `?v=4` cache-busting. Bump again on future edits or switch to a build hash. - All changes preserve existing fields on the existing endpoints, so older clients continue to work — the `default_resolution` field on `GET /api/settings/recording` is purely additive. - `record_quality` is only auto-assigned on enrolment / off → on. Once a model is tracked, it is the source of truth and is only modified through explicit edits.

author: chicoxyzzy
body:
## Summary

Vite has been warning about a >500 KB chunk for a while. The fix is the textbook one Vite itself suggests in the warning: each of the six workspace views (Chats, Providers, Tasks, Observability, Costs, Settings) becomes its own lazy chunk, plus a build-time `<link rel="modulepreload">` for the most-likely-first workspace so the parallel-load benefit isn't lost on the default landing surface.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Initial JS | 561.84 KB | **259.02 KB** |
| Initial gzipped | 149.43 KB | **80.19 KB** |
| Largest chunk after | — | ChatView 91.71 KB / 23.44 KB gz |
| Vite `>500KB` warning | yes | gone |

**Reduction: -54% raw / -46% gzipped on the initial bundle.** Workspace chunks fetch on first visit (sub-100 ms on localhost, invisible in practice).

Vite also auto-extracted three shared chunks because multiple lazy components consume them: `AddProviderModal-*.js` (15 KB), `TranscriptActivityTimeline-*.js` (11 KB), `ui-*.js` (22 KB). Those load alongside whichever workspace needs them first, then are cached for the others.

## Implementation

- The 6 `import { XView } from "..."` lines in `AppShell.tsx` become `const XView = lazy(() => import("..."))`.
- The conditional render block in `AuthenticatedShell` is wrapped in a single `<Suspense>` with a muted `<WorkspaceFallback />` ("Loading…" in the same monospaced style as the boot splash, so a workspace switch reads as "still booting that surface" rather than as a jarring spinner).
- One AppShell test that asserted on lazy ChatView content via synchronous `getByText` switches to `await findByText` — the standard pattern for components inside Suspense. Shell chrome (workspace nav buttons, statusbar) stays sync because it's not lazy.

## Modulepreload for ChatView

Inline Vite plugin `preloadLikelyFirstWorkspace` runs at build-time, finds the hashed `assets/ChatView-*.js` filename in the bundle map, and injects a single `<link rel="modulepreload" href="...">` into the built `index.html`. The browser fetches + parses ChatView in parallel with the entry chunk so first-paint of Chats happens with the chunk already warm.

Why ChatView specifically:
- Default landing surface for new operators (no localStorage workspace preference yet).
- Most-used surface for repeat operators.
- Incidentally the largest workspace chunk; the parallel-load win scales with chunk size.

Modern browsers follow the import graph for modulepreloaded chunks, so the shared dependencies (AddProviderModal, TranscriptActivityTimeline, ui) get pulled along without explicit tags.

Cost when the operator's last-active workspace is something else: ~23 KB gzipped of wasted bandwidth, fetched once. On localhost / LAN — Hecate's deployment shape — invisible.

## Gitkeep preservation

Side fix: `//go:embed all:ui/dist` (in the module root's `embed.go`) requires `ui/dist/` to be a non-empty directory at compile time, otherwise Go fails with "pattern all:ui/dist: no matching files found". The placeholder is a tracked `.gitkeep`. Vite's `emptyOutDir: true` wipes it on every build, leaving a phantom deletion in `git status` until something restores it. The Justfile used to do this restore as a post-step, which only worked when callers went through `just ui-build` — bare `bun run build`, IDE-triggered builds, or CI invoking bun directly all left the worktree dirty.

New `preserve-dist-gitkeep` plugin emits `.gitkeep` as a build asset via Rollup's `emitFile` API. Empty-out-dir runs before `generateBundle`, so the emitted asset always lands in the output regardless of who invoked the build. The Justfile's post-step is gone, replaced with a comment pointing at the plugin.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --build`: clean.
- [x] Production build: clean, no `>500KB` warning.
- [x] Built `index.html` contains `<link rel="modulepreload" href="/assets/ChatView-*.js">` in `<head>`.
- [x] `.gitkeep` survives 3 consecutive `rm -f ui/dist/.gitkeep && just ui-build` cycles, worktree stays clean.
- [x] Full UI suite: 5 consecutive runs all green (29 files, 654 tests).
- [x] Bundle inspection: 11 chunks total, all under 260 KB; per-workspace sizes match expectations.

## Risk

- **First-visit-per-workspace latency** adds a fetch+parse for the chunk. On localhost (and the desktop app's embedded webview, which is also localhost-equivalent), this is sub-100 ms. The fallback prevents layout flash.
- **Service worker / cache invalidation** behavior unchanged — Vite handles chunk hashing automatically.
- **Tauri bundle** picks up the multi-file dist transparently via `//go:embed all:ui/dist`. No goreleaser or release-pipeline changes needed.

## Summary

- Add new **Task** resource exposing the Linkup `/v1/tasks` async batch API
- Three operations: **Create** (POST), **Get** by ID (GET), **Get Many** with filters (GET)
- Create operation supports all three task types (search, fetch, research) with dynamic UI fields

- Get Many supports filtering by status and type, plus pagination and sorting

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` passes

- [x] Create a search task → verify request body is `[{ type: "search", input: { q, depth, outputType, ... } }]`
- [x] Create a fetch task → verify URL field appears, depth/outputType hidden
- [x] Create a research task → verify mode/reasoningDepth fields appear

author: irnb
body:
## Summary

- Drop `claim_index` from the nullifier preimage so one SSH key can take at most one reward per `(rootId, period)`, instead of being able to drain `maxClaims` from a single key.
- The contract ABI is unchanged. `claim_index` stays as a slot tag in the public values and the SSH claim signature.
- Updates docs, contract comments, and tests to match.

## Why

Before this change, the nullifier preimage included `claim_index`, so the same key with `claim_index = 0, 1, 2, …` produced distinct nullifiers. Combined with `maxClaims` being a period-wide cap, this meant one contributor could submit `maxClaims` claims and walk away with the entire period's pool. The README sells "patronage for OSS contributors" — distributive — and the nullifier should match that intent.

## Test plan
- [ ] `SP1_SKIP_BUILD=1 cargo test --workspace`
- [ ] `cd contracts && forge test -vv`
- [ ] Verified nullifier no longer changes when only `claim_index` differs (new test in `lib/src/nullifier.rs`)
- [ ] Existing period-cap tests still pass (the contract-level cap is unchanged and is still a useful second line of defense)

## Breaking change

This changes the nullifier value for the same `(key_id, repo_id_hash, period_id, contract, chain_id)` tuple — old proof artifacts cannot be replayed against an upgraded vault and would need to be re-proven. Coordinate with vault operators before rolling out.

author: m-bonanno
body:
## What

Address Copilot review on the v2.4.0 release PR (#551). Same shape as #543 was for #542 — a small chore PR into `develop` that fixes the comment, then the release PR can land cleanly.

## Why

Copilot flagged a SSR safety issue in `VersionCheckService.start()` that would `ReferenceError` at boot if the service runs without a DOM `defaultView` (SSR pass, non-browser test bootstrap). The previous shape did `fromEvent(this.document.defaultView ?? window, 'focus')` — but if `defaultView` is null, the global `window` is also undefined in those environments, so the fallback would throw before the service could even early-return.

## How

- `version-check.service.ts` — derive `const win = this.document.defaultView` at the top of `start()`, return early if it's null. Pipe consumes `win` directly (no `?? window` fallback). The dev-sentinel guard above already had a similar shape via `consumeForceUpdateFlag()`; this brings the rest of `start()` in line.
- `version-check.service.spec.ts` — new spec `is a no-op when document.defaultView is null (SSR / non-browser bootstrap)` configures DOCUMENT with `defaultView: null` and asserts `start()` doesn't throw and no HTTP request fires. 722 specs total now (was 721).

## Out of scope

- Any other Copilot comments on the release PR (none — this was the only one).

## References

- #551 — v2.4.0 release PR (target of the fix)
- #549 — original SPA cache-bust feature where `VersionCheckService` shipped

- [x] `npm test` — 722 specs green (new SSR test included)

author: may-keepur
body:
## Summary

Phase A #3 under [KPR-210](https://linear.app/keepur/issue/KPR-210). Flattens the skills layout in this repo (engine + seeds) to SDK-exact convention. [KPR-215](https://linear.app/keepur/issue/KPR-215) does the same for dodi + keepur operator-skills repos.

```
Today:    <root>/skills/<workflow>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
Phase A:  <root>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
```

## Architectural surprise + resolution

The plan assumed a straightforward path-flatten + loader-update. During implementation, an SDK constraint surfaced: the SDK's plugin format requires `<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`. With flat layout (`<root>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`), one option was register `<root>` as one plugin (loses `agents:` per-skill scoping). To preserve the per-skill scoping that's hive's value-add, the loader builds a **synthetic symlink projection** at `<hiveHome>/.skill-projections/<key>/skills/<skillName>/` rebuilt each load.

This deserves careful review — it's a design choice that the plan didn't fully anticipate. Trade-offs:
- ✅ Preserves `agents:` per-skill scoping (hive's value-add)
- ✅ Each skill becomes its own SDK plugin config — directly maps to the existing SDK contract
- ✅ Idempotent (rebuilt each load; tolerant to parallel-test races)
- ⚠️ Adds a new on-disk artifact (`.skill-projections/`) — not visible to operators normally
- ⚠️ Symlinks aren't portable (Windows) — fine for hive's macOS-only deployment

## Dual-layout transition

Per plan §R4: engine reads BOTH old (double-`skills/`) and new (flat) layouts during the transition. Old layout fires a deprecation warning. [KPR-215](https://linear.app/keepur/issue/KPR-215) migrates dodi + keepur operator-skills repos; once that lands, a future ticket can drop dual-layout support.

## What's in the PR

5 commits, 11 files modified (+1314/-183 lines), 27 new tests (1322 → 1349 passing), 0 errors:

| `e51d1d2` | migration script + 14 unit tests |

- [x] Existing 21 legacy-layout tests unchanged — keeps deprecation path exercised until KPR-215

## Out of scope

author: copilot
body:
In command-line mode, in-progress SKK composition (e.g. `:▽ああ`) could not be aborted mid-entry: `<Esc>` and `<C-g>` ended up leaving composed text on the command line and triggering invalid command execution. This change adjusts command-line cancellation flow so active composition is discarded before exiting cmdline editing state.

- **Command-line `<Esc>` now follows cancel semantics during active composition**
  - In `s:asym_filter()`, `<Esc>` is routed to `s:do_cancel()` (not `s:do_escape()`) when mode is `c` and preedit is non-empty.
  - This avoids the confirm-style path that previously committed composed text.

- **Cancel path now clears preedit state before cmdline escape**
  - In `s:do_cancel()`, cmdline-mode handling now:
    - resets phase to normal
    - clears all preedit buffers
    - emits `\<Esc>` as a post-rewrite key
  - This ensures cancellation removes `ああ` / `▽ああ` from the cmdline rather than confirming it.

- **Scope control**
  - Changes are isolated to command-line cancel behavior; insert-mode and candidate-selection behavior are not otherwise altered.

```vim
" before
elseif char ==# "\<Esc>"
  call s:do_escape(a:stash)

" after
elseif char ==# "\<Esc>"
  if mode() ==# 'c' && !preedit.empty()
    call s:do_cancel(a:stash)
  else
    call s:do_escape(a:stash)
  endif
endif
```

This PR is intentionally tiny and inert: it lays down the package skeleton, types, env wiring, and the rule definitions without yet performing any emulation. Subsequent PRs add the request builder (PR-B), scanner integration (PR-C), and graceful-degradation paths (PR-D).

Spec section: `docs/research/ton-shield-bot-implementation-spec.md` §9.3 and §20.7 (local-only — that file is gitignored, but I updated it locally for design provenance).

## What this PR adds

### `packages/ton-emulator/`

A new workspace package wrapping `@ton-api/client`. Currently exposes only:

- `loadTonEmulatorConfig(env)` — reads `TONAPI_KEY` (optional) and `TONAPI_BASE_URL` (default `https://tonapi.io`) via zod. Missing key is **not an error** — the scanner runs in static-only mode and surfaces `EMULATION_NOT_CONFIGURED` so the absence is visible.
- `isEmulationEnabled(config)` — boolean predicate for the static-only branch.
- `createTonEmulatorClient(config)` — thin wrapper around `TonApiClient`. Returns `{ enabled, raw, baseUrl }`. The `raw` SDK client is exposed only for use *inside this package*; the rest of the codebase imports our own typed surface.
- `EmulationResult` discriminated union (`status: "ok" | "skipped" | "failed"`) with concrete `EmulatedAction[]`, `EmulatedRisk`, and skip/fail reason variants. Mirrors the slice of `MessageConsequences` we'll consume in PR-C.
- `EmulatedActionKind` enum aligned with TONAPI v2 `Action.type` (TonTransfer, JettonTransfer, NftItemTransfer, ContractDeploy, AddExtension, etc).

### `packages/risk-engine/src/rules.ts` — 12 new rules under `category: emulation`

| Rule | Severity | Score | Triggered when |
|------|----------|-------|----------------|
| `EMULATION_SENDS_NEAR_FULL_BALANCE` | critical | +80 | `risk.transfer_all_remaining_balance === true` |
| `EMULATION_WALLET_V5_AUTH_CHANGE` | critical | +80 | Any `AddExtension` / `RemoveExtension` / `SetSignatureAllowedAction` |
| `EMULATION_DEPLOYS_UNKNOWN_CONTRACT` | high | +45 | Emulated `ContractDeploy` not in static decode |
| `EMULATION_SCAM_PATTERN_DETECTED` | high | +45 | `event.is_scam === true` |
| `EMULATION_MISMATCH` | high | +45 | Static and emulated diverge on dest/asset/amount |
| `EMULATION_ABORTED` | medium | +25 | `trace.transaction.aborted` |
| `EMULATION_REVEALED_HIDDEN_ACTION` | medium | +25 | Emulator surfaces actions static decode missed |
| `EMULATION_FAILED` | low | +10 | TONAPI 4xx |
| `EMULATION_PROVIDER_DOWN` | low | +10 | TONAPI 5xx / timeout |
| `EMULATION_SKIPPED_NO_SENDER` | info | +5 | TC transaction with no `from` field |
| `EMULATION_NOT_CONFIGURED` | info | +5 | `TONAPI_KEY` unset in deployment |
| `EMULATION_SENDER_UNINITIALISED` | info | +5 | Sender wallet not yet on-chain |

These follow the existing `<CATEGORY>_<SUBJECT>` naming from `RuleId` template-literal type. Category `emulation` was already in `RuleCategory` and unused.

### Plumbing

- `tsconfig.json` paths: `@tonshield/ton-emulator` registered.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` updated for new package linkage (no new external deps — all already present elsewhere in the workspace).

## What this PR explicitly does NOT do

- No emulation calls. No HTTP traffic. No code path imports `ton-emulator` yet.
- No changes to `basic-scan.ts` or any scanner. M1.5 behaviour is byte-identical.
- No env-var reads in deployed services. `TONAPI_KEY` is not yet wired into `apps/api` or `apps/bot` env validation.

Those land in PR-B / PR-C / PR-D so each step is reviewable on its own.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean
- [x] `pnpm format` clean
- [x] 202 tests pass on Node 20 (up from 196; +6 for the new `config.test.ts`). 3 pre-existing undici-on-Node-20 failures unchanged.
- [x] `pnpm vitest run packages/ton-emulator` — 6/6 pass.
- [ ] CI on Node 24 should run all suites including the existing undici-affected files.

## Summary

Closes the #2 follow-up from the validation work in #6: now that the registry enforces `plate_regex`, the admin app mirrors that rule client-side so a ministry operator sees the format requirement *before* they hit submit.

## Backend — `services/auth/internal/api/api.go`

- `meResp` gains a `tenant_config` block: `{ name, country_code, locale, currency, plate_regex }`.
- Both `/v1/auth/login` and `/v1/auth/me` populate it from the `tenants` row via a new `loadTenantConfig` helper that runs with `row_security off` (auth is the across-tenants service).
- A failed config load is logged + degraded to the zero value, **not** 500'd — login + /me still succeed for the user object.

## Frontend — `packages/web-common/src/session.tsx`

- `Session.user` gains an optional `tenant_config` field mirroring the backend shape. Older backends that don't send it leave it `undefined` and the UI falls back to permissive defaults.

## Frontend — `apps/web-admin/app/(app)/vehicles/page.tsx`

- New collapsed "New vehicle" card above the search row.
- Click → inline form with Plate / Make / Model / Year fields.
- Plate input is uppercase-on-type, shows the jurisdiction's regex as a hint, and validates client-side via the same `RegExp` the server compiled.
- A 400 `bad_plate` response surfaces inline with the regex value the server returned — so the user always sees the rule even when client-side validation was looser than the server's.

💡 **What**: Refactored the `PMO` (Price Momentum Oscillator) indicator to use purely vectorized Pandas and NumPy operations, bypassing 5 sequential Python `for` loops.

🎯 **Why**: The nested recursion logic and looping structure severely bottle-necked array evaluations for long tick arrays, slowing down backtests.

📊 **Impact**: Evaluates 50,000 prices in ~0.0039s compared to ~0.55s previously. That is a ~140x reduction in execution latency with identical numerical precision.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify with benchmark diffs ensuring exact matching output using max absolute differences. Passed all corresponding mapped and unit tests.

This PR applies a full UI/UX and branding overhaul from EventLens to **Glimpse**, implementing the design system in `DESIGN.md` as the source of truth. It rebuilds the entry experience and extends the new brand language across auth, onboarding, and role-based dashboards with mobile-first layouts and unified components.

- **Global design system + theming**
  - Replaced ad-hoc styling with centralized tokens in `globals.css` (palette, gradients, spacing, radii, elevation, motion/easing).
  - Added dark/light/system theme model and runtime switching via `ThemeProvider` + `ThemeToggle`.
  - Updated root metadata and app shell to Glimpse defaults and dark-first presentation.

- **Atomic component architecture**
  - Introduced reusable primitives aligned with `DESIGN.md`:
    - `Button` variants (primary/secondary/outline/ghost)
    - `Input` with consistent focus states and sizing
    - `Card` light/dark surface variants
    - Semantic `Badge` states (`face-found`, `processing`, `uploading`, `event-live`)
  - Added shared `cn()` utility for deterministic class composition.

- **Landing page reconstruction**
  - Rebuilt `/` with dark-first hero, feature pillars, “how it works,” and pricing sections per new brand structure.
  - Migrated iconography to Phosphor and updated copy/tone to Glimpse messaging.

- **Authentication + onboarding flows**
  - Added full auth route set and shared auth layout:
    - `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/forgot-password`, `/auth/reset-password`
  - Added creator/event-host onboarding flow at `/onboarding` with role selection and progressive setup steps.

- **Role-based dashboard wrappers and mobile-first UX**
  - Added shared dashboard shell with:
    - desktop sidebar (brand-aligned dark nav)
    - mobile bottom tab bar
    - persistent theme toggle
  - Added role pages:
    - `/dashboard/creator`
    - `/dashboard/guest`
    - `/dashboard/event-host`
  - Implemented mobile-first structures (48px+ touch targets, responsive photo grids, centered scan CTA pattern).

- **Support updates**
  - Added `@phosphor-icons/react` dependency for icon system alignment.

## 什麼改動
OAuth provider token persistence is now minimized and protected:

- Google access/refresh tokens are no longer persisted after login.
- Twitch provider refresh tokens are no longer persisted.
- Twitch access tokens needed by raffle subscriber snapshot sync are stored encrypted with AES-GCM using the `enc:v1:` format.
- Raffle snapshot sync decrypts stored Twitch tokens before calling Twitch, keeps legacy plaintext token reads for migration, and clears stored token material when the token is expired or Twitch returns an authorization failure.
- Added `OAUTH_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, falling back to `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` when unset.

author: dieterolson
body:
💡 What: Replaced a series of chained `.map()` and `.reduce()` array function allocations in `psa_calculator.html`'s inner `calculatePSA` execution loop with a single-pass `for` loop and pre-allocated arrays, alongside substituting `reduce` with a globally scoped `sumArray` helper function.
🎯 Why: Multiple chained `.map()` allocations inside tight calculation steps generates numerous intermediate arrays, leading to O(N) memory allocation and subsequent garbage collection overhead. Since these calculations can be re-run frequently (e.g., when inputs change), avoiding intermediate mapping drastically decreases garbage collection pauses. 
📊 Impact: Expected to reduce memory footprint by ~90% within the `calculatePSA` function frame, drastically reducing UI stutters when recalculating results.
🔬 Measurement: Verify using browser dev-tools allocation timelines while running simulations.

author: copilot
body:
Lecturers were blocked from starting new attendance sessions because expired sessions could remain marked active, triggering false “already active” warnings. In parallel, course deletion from the admin-facing dashboard cards used an HTMX `DELETE` request path that failed CSRF enforcement.

- **Session lifecycle hardening (runtime cleanup)**
  - Added centralized expired-session cleanup in `frontend/views.py` via `_close_expired_attendance_sessions(course=None)`.
  - Expired sessions (`now >= created_at + duration_hours`) are closed (`is_active=False`, `ended_at=now`) during request handling.
  - Related state is synchronized: orphaned active tokens are deactivated and `Course.is_active` is reset when no active sessions remain.

- **Applied cleanup at entry points that gate session creation**
  - Cleanup now runs before rendering/processing attendance flows:
    - `attendance_take`
    - `attendance_index`
  - This prevents stale DB state from blocking new session creation.

- **CSRF-safe course deletion from course cards**
  - Updated course card action in `templates/partials/course_list_content.html` from `hx-delete` to `hx-post`.
  - Added explicit CSRF header to HTMX request so admin dashboard deletes align with Django CSRF protection.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added a targeted frontend test to ensure an expired active session is auto-closed and a new session can be created immediately for the same course.

```python
def _close_expired_attendance_sessions(course=None):
    now = timezone.now()
    active_sessions = Attendance.objects.filter(is_active=True)
    if course is not None:
        active_sessions = active_sessions.filter(course=course)

    for session in active_sessions:
        if now >= session.created_at + timedelta(hours=session.duration_hours):
            session.is_active = False
            session.ended_at = now
            session.save(update_fields=['is_active', 'ended_at'])
```

author: mbaudin47
body:
This PR creates a new `HyperbolicEnumerateFunction`. The goal of this PR is to fix #2971.

We consider the isotropic hyperbolic norm:

$$
\|\mathbf{\alpha}\|_q = \left( \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} \alpha_j^q \right)^{1/q}
$$

for any multi-index $\mathbf{\alpha} \in \mathbb{N}^d$. 

## Methods

Two methods were used to improve the speed:
- use a min-heap instead of a list (used to insert new multi-indices in the data structure);
- use a lookup table to store powers of integers.

The second method cannot be applied to `HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction`, because nontrivial weights (i.e. different from 1) may generate non integer sum of powers. The first method can be applied to ` HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction`.

The performance ratio of `HyperbolicEnumerateFunction` to `HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction` is approximately 500.

## Benchmark

```python
# %%
import openturns as ot
import time
import openturns.viewer as otv


# %%
print(f"OT Version: {ot.__version__}")

# %%
def TimeEnumerationFunction(enumerateFunction, basisSize):
    t1 = time.time()
    for i in range(basisSize):
        _ = enumerateFunction(i)
    t2 = time.time()
    elapsed = t2 - t1
    return elapsed



# %%
dimension = 20
basisSize = 5000
print(f"Dimension = {dimension}")
print(f"basisSize = {basisSize}")

# %%
print("")
print("+ 1. LinearEnumerateFunction")
enumerateFunction = ot.LinearEnumerateFunction(dimension)
print("basis size = ", basisSize)
elapsed = TimeEnumerationFunction(enumerateFunction, basisSize)
print("elapsed = %.1f (s)" % (elapsed))
print(f"Speed={basisSize / elapsed:.0f} coeffs/s")


# %%
print("")
print("+ 2. HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction, q=1.0")
quasiNorm = 1.0
weight = [1.0] * dimension
enumerateFunction = ot.HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction(weight, quasiNorm)
print("basis size = ", basisSize)
elapsed = TimeEnumerationFunction(enumerateFunction, basisSize)
print("elapsed = %.1f (s)" % (elapsed))
print(f"Speed={basisSize / elapsed:.0f} coeffs/s")

# %%
print("")
print("+ 3. HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction, q=0.7")
quasiNorm = 0.7
enumerateFunction = ot.HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction(dimension, quasiNorm)
print("basis size = ", basisSize)
elapsed = TimeEnumerationFunction(enumerateFunction, basisSize)
print("elapsed = %.1f (s)" % (elapsed))
print(f"Speed={basisSize / elapsed:.0f} coeffs/s")

# %%
print("")
print("+ 4. HyperbolicEnumerateFunction, 0.7")
quasiNorm = 0.7
enumerateFunction = ot.HyperbolicEnumerateFunction(dimension, quasiNorm)
print("basis size = ", basisSize)
elapsed = TimeEnumerationFunction(enumerateFunction, basisSize)
print("elapsed = %.1f (s)" % (elapsed))
print(f"Speed={basisSize / elapsed:.0f} coeffs/s")
```

Here are the results.

```
$ python hyperbolic_enumeration/benchmark_enumeration.py 
OT Version: 1.28dev
Dimension = 20
basisSize = 5000

+ 1. LinearEnumerateFunction
basis size =  5000
elapsed = 0.0 (s)
Speed=642 333 coeffs/s

+ 2. HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction, q=1.0
basis size =  5000
elapsed = 11.0 (s)
Speed=454 coeffs/s

+ 3. HyperbolicAnisotropicEnumerateFunction, q=0.7
basis size =  5000
elapsed = 14.7 (s)
Speed=341 coeffs/s

+ 4. HyperbolicEnumerateFunction, 0.7
basis size =  5000
elapsed = 0.0 (s)
Speed=112 218 coeffs/s
```

author: onestepat4time
body:
## Fix for #3078: acpEnabled defaults to false — sessions stuck at pending

### Problem
`acpEnabled` in config defaults to `false`. When no `AEGIS_ACP_ENABLED` env var is set, sessions are created in-memory only — no Claude Code process is spawned. They stay at `pending` forever, even when the ACP binary is available and `ag doctor` reports it as ✅.

### Root Cause
```
src/config.ts:224 — acpEnabled: false
src/routes/sessions.ts:402 — if (acpBackend && ctx.config.acpEnabled)
```
The `acpBackend` is always instantiated but the config flag blocks it from being used.

### Fix
**One-line change:** default `acpEnabled` to `true`.

Safe because:
- `acpBackend` gates on binary availability internally — if no binary found, no ACP session regardless of flag
- Users can still explicitly disable via `AEGIS_ACP_ENABLED=false` or `"acpEnabled": false` in config
- Existing tests that explicitly set `acpEnabled: false` are unaffected

### Changes (2 files, 33 insertions, 1 deletion)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config.ts` | `acpEnabled: false` → `acpEnabled: true` |

author: yujoo-lee
body:
## Summary

Vite was warning *"Some chunks are larger than 500 kB after minification"* because all `node_modules` were getting glued into a single vendor chunk. Splits node_modules into family-sized chunks so the largest is now ~290 kB.

### Before

```
dist/assets/index-*.js               ~530 kB    (single vendor + entry)
```
+ \"chunks > 500 kB\" warning

### After (verified locally with \`npm run build\`)

```
dist/assets/vendor-react-*.js       287.61 kB │ gz 91.94 kB
dist/assets/vendor-*.js             127.97 kB │ gz 41.97 kB   (motion + misc)
dist/assets/vendor-i18n-*.js         49.12 kB │ gz 16.07 kB
dist/assets/index-*.js               48.65 kB │ gz 16.49 kB
dist/assets/vendor-query-*.js        42.51 kB │ gz 12.62 kB
dist/assets/FallFGame-*.js           21.67 kB │ gz  7.72 kB   (lazy)
dist/assets/vendor-zustand-*.js       3.54 kB │ gz  1.66 kB
dist/assets/CatalogPage-*.js          1.33 kB │ gz  0.57 kB   (lazy)
```

No warnings. Largest chunk is 287 kB.

## Why family-sized splits

- **Cache stability**: vendor families have stable hashes across releases — browsers reuse them across deploys when only app code changes.
- **Parallel HTTP/2 fetches**: smaller chunks download in parallel rather than blocking on one big bundle.
- **Critical-path tightness**: `index` chunk shrinks because boilerplate is hoisted out.

## Why \`isSsrBuild\` gate

\`manualChunks\` is gated on \`!isSsrBuild\` so the prerender SSR bundle (consumed by \`scripts/prerender.mjs\` as a single \`entry-server.js\`) stays unsplit. Splitting it would break the \`import()\` chain prerender.mjs uses to render each route.

> Note: we don't do **runtime** SSR (pure SPA + GitHub Pages). The \`vite build --ssr\` step exists only to feed \`scripts/prerender.mjs\` for build-time HTML generation; \`dist-server/\` is deleted after prerender runs.

## Why no explicit \`vendor-motion\`

motion(/react) shares a strong dependency graph with react internals; rollup folds it into \`vendor-react\` / \`vendor\` automatically. An explicit \`vendor-motion\` rule produced an empty chunk. Left to fall into the generic \`vendor\` bucket — comment in code explains why.

## Routing chunk strategy (already in place — no change in this PR)

- \`/\` (HomePage): eager (statically imported in routes.tsx)
- \`/game\` (CatalogPage): lazy via \`lazyRoute\` ✓
- \`/game/fall-f\` (FallFGame): lazy via \`lazyRoute\` ✓

So the home page never downloads game logic. This PR only fixes the vendor side.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` locally — 0 warnings, all chunks < 500 kB
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] (manual) deploy and verify network tab shows separate vendor-* chunks loading

The numbers are 0.0868 (square τ=0.10 @ 100k) vs 0.1136 (baseline τ=0.10 @ 50k) — that is a ~24 % reduction in the value, not a halving. Even framed as gap reduction (square at 50k = 0.0814, gap = 0.0322; gap at 100k = 0.0268) it's only ~17 % gap shrinkage. Replaced with **"~24 % lower"**.
- Original said square τ=0.20 U_batch was "matched / very slightly higher" at 100k. Tightened to "has crossed baseline (0.0930 vs 0.0890)" — square is now ~4.5 % above baseline, not "matched".

## Kept (load-bearing despite seeming verbose)

- Caveat paragraph under the Welch table — the user has a project habit of treating Welch p as overcooked given autocorrelation; removing it would silently let future readers cite p ≈ 1e-173 as i.i.d.
- The "earlier 'square is significantly worse at τ=0.20' verdict was a convergence-speed artifact" sentence — explicitly reverses a published interim conclusion, worth keeping prominent.
- All three plot images and the Welch + late-window tables — those carry the actual information.

## Test plan

- [ ] No CSV / plot script / image edits (verified by `git diff --stat`).

author: abheek-pradhan
body:
The npm install of hermes-agent drops a wrapper at ~/.local/bin/hermes that execs Hermes's own bundled venv at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv. The `run_agent` python module exists *inside that venv*, not in our project venv, so NousHermesProvider's importlib check returned False and the user's freshly-installed Hermes was silently skipped.

Add a CLI fallback to NousHermesProvider:

* is_available() now returns True if EITHER `run_agent` is importable (in-venv pip install) OR `hermes` is on $PATH (npm install).
* call() prefers the in-process module path (lower latency, no subprocess), falling back to `hermes -z <prompt> --ignore-rules --ignore-user-config` when only the CLI is reachable.
* The --ignore-* flags prevent the operator's local Hermes config / project rules from leaking into the audit prompt and contaminating the JSON output. Verified end-to-end against a real install: the CLI returns clean single-line JSON, no ANSI, no prose.

Tests:
* monkeypatched sys.modules + shutil.which → 6 deterministic tests covering: neither-available, module-path, cli-path, ignore-flags passed correctly, non-zero-exit raises, empty-stdout raises.
* Live integration verified manually: Hermes CLI returns the prompted JSON via Claude Code OAuth (no separate auth needed — Hermes already uses the same session as `claude_agent_sdk`).

Default audit chain now lights up three of four providers without operator config: nous_hermes (CLI), claude_code_sdk (session auth), openai (API key). Only `claude` (paid Anthropic API) remains unavailable when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, which is the correct behavior — paid path is opt-in.

## Summary
- Lyric ♪ markers no longer appear over normal-singing gaps. LRClib only stamps line start times, so a 6-second "gap" was often just the singer holding a word. New code estimates per-line sung duration (~280ms/char, capped at 90% of the gap) and only inserts markers in *true silence* past an 8-second threshold.
- Seek-back position desync fixed. The monotonic-clamp on the displayed lyric position wasn't resetting when the anchor re-synced backward, so skipping to an earlier point in the same song left the highlighter stuck at the prior high-water mark.
- Spotify Connect CTA moved from a big card in the content area to a small icon button in the transport row (right of Next, same slot the Playlists button takes when authed). Lyrics now render even when not authed (LRClib is independent of Spotify auth).

Console prod : \`ReferenceError: Cannot access 'yt' before initialization\` au mount de \`LibraryEquipmentView\`. Liste biblio vide.

La PR #115 a ajouté un \`watch([canDrag, flatEquipmentItems], …)\`. Vue évalue immédiatement les sources d'un watch au setup pour mémoriser la valeur initiale (avant le 1er callback du watcher). Saving a snippet with only prompt/code could return HTTP 400 because the request body shape did not match API model binding expectations. The rejection occurred before controller logic, so no controller-side save log was emitted.

  - File: `dashboard/app.js`

- **Behavior impact**
  - Snippet create requests that include only required fields now conform to the API schema and are no longer rejected due to `customMetadata` type mismatch.

```js
environment: {
  // ...
  keyDependencies: [],
  customMetadata: [] // was {}
}
```

- add regression coverage so the manifest and linker flags stay present

## Why
Windows can treat executables with names like `*_updater.exe` as installers when they do not carry an explicit manifest. The existing 570 client launches the downloaded updater with `CreateProcess` (`UseShellExecute=false`), so Windows returns Win32Exception 740 instead of showing UAC. Embedding `asInvoker` in the updater itself prevents the heuristic and fixes existing clients once they download the updated updater artifact.

## Validation
- `cargo build --manifest-path external/moder-update/src/updater/Cargo.toml --release`
- read the release updater RT_MANIFEST resource and verified `requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker"`
- `cargo test --manifest-path external/moder-update/src/updater/Cargo.toml`
- `dotnet test TelegramSearchBot.Test/TelegramSearchBot.Test.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ModerUpdateIntegrationTests|FullyQualifiedName~SelfUpdateBootstrapTests"`

body:
## Summary

Implements part A of #1298 (system signal adapters): wraps a `GovernanceController` as a `SystemSignalSource`. Polls sensors at a fixed interval, detects per-sensor threshold crossings (rising/falling edges), and emits `SystemSignal{kind: "governance"}` with per-sensor cooldown debouncing.

Today governance sensors only **block** ("stop"). This adapter makes them **trigger** ("start") — feeding the composition planner so it can autonomously react to error-rate spikes, context pressure, idle states, etc.

Single shared polling loop fans out to all subscribers; lazy-start on first `watch()`, lazy-clear on last unsubscribe. Fail-open: unknown sensor names, controller exceptions, and handler exceptions all forward to subscriber `onError` and the loop continues.

Parts B (Grove SSE adapter) and C (Nexus EventBus adapter) of #1298 are out of scope and tracked for separate PRs.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean

## Summary

Companion to PR #1295 (`go-no-go-gate-status-2026-05-10.md`, the snapshot doc). This adds `scripts/cutover/check-cutover-readiness.sh` — a re-runnable script that re-derives the same gate-status table any time. Stilgar runs it throughout cutover-morning as dependencies progress.

## Sample output (current state)

```
Gate                                     Status           Detail
----                                     -------          ------
DNS TTL ≤ 60 s (authoritative)           ❌ NOT STARTED   apex=3600s www=3600s via ns3.wixdns.net.
Order baseline captured                  ❌ NOT STARTED   no order-baseline-*.json
/api/health route deployed               ⚠️ PENDING        cfw PR #554 open
ratchet branch excluded                  ⚠️ PENDING        cfw PR #565 open
Logo restored (cfw PR #540)              ⚠️ PENDING        open
Vercel Pro plan active                   ✅ CLEAR          pro:plus:active
UptimeRobot monitors configured          ⚠️ PENDING        cf-3qt.8.31 IN_PROGRESS
Sentry connected to prod                 ❔ UNKNOWN        out-of-lane

🔴 NO-GO — 2 hard blocker(s) NOT STARTED
exit=1
```

Final verdict line on stdout, full table on stderr.

## 8 gates checked

- DNS TTL ≤ 60 s — queries the **authoritative** Wix NS directly (`dig @ns2.wixdns.net`) so cache-decay from public resolvers (e.g. 2700s mid-cache values from a 3600s record) doesn't falsely signal "almost dropped"
- Order baseline JSON file present
- cfw PR #554 (`/api/health`) merged
- cfw PR #565 (ratchet branch excluded) merged
- cfw PR #540 (logo) merged
- Vercel Pro plan still active (`/v2/teams` API)
- cf-3qt.8.31 UptimeRobot status
- Sentry connected to prod (always UNKNOWN — out-of-lane hint)

## Exit codes

- `0` = **GO** (every gate ✅ or known-soft-pending)
- `1` = **NO-GO** (any hard blocker NOT STARTED)
- `2` = **HOLD** (no blockers but some PENDING reviews; can call GO once those land)

Lets the script chain into other tooling — e.g. a pre-flight check before running `dns-cutover-flip.sh`.

## Dependencies

`dig`, `gh`, `ls`, `curl`, `python3` — all already required by sibling scripts in `scripts/cutover/`. No new dependencies.
