author: alexmensch
body:
Replace the v1 Lambertian default in the planet apparent-magnitude
pipeline (3re.17) with empirical V-band phase polynomials from
Mallama, Krobusek, Pavlov 2018 (Icarus 282; DOI 10.1016/j.icarus.2016.09.023)
wherever the paper publishes one. Generalised so non-published bodies
— including every exoplanet under `stellata-bk5` — fall through to
Lambert automatically.

Closes `stellata-3re.18`.

## Summary

- New `src/client/phase-function.ts` with `PhaseCoefficients` type,
  `lambertianPhaseFactor`, `mallamaPhaseFactor`, `peakPhaseFactor`
  and per-planet polynomial constants. Vitest mirrors the shader.
- `planet-system.ts` adds optional `phaseCoefficients?` on `Planet`
  and wires the per-planet constants into `SOL_PLANETS`. Uranus,
  Neptune and Pluto are deliberately bare → Lambertian fallback.
- `planet-body-field.ts` adds two per-instance vec4 attributes
  (`iPhaseCoefsA` carrying c0..c3, `iPhaseCoefsB` carrying
  c4,c5,c6,alphaMaxDeg) plus matching grow/compact/flush plumbing.
  `cullDistancePc` folds in Saturn's c0 ring boost so the host
  distance cull widens to match.
- `planet.vert.glsl` evaluates the polynomial when `alphaMaxDeg > 0`
  and α ≤ αmax, anchor-scaled Lambert past αmax (preserves
  brightness continuity at the boundary), pure Lambert when
  `alphaMaxDeg = 0` (the "no Mallama" sentinel).

## Per-planet provenance

| Planet | Source in Mallama 2018 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mercury | Table A-1.2 (V-band, 7th-order) | Truncated to degree 6 to fit two-vec4 storage. Truncation stays sub-0.25 mag only out to α ≈ 87°, then grows rapidly (~2.4 mag at 120°, ~27 mag at 170°). αmax is therefore capped at **87°** (not Mallama's published 170°) — past that, anchor-scaled Lambert tracks the full 7th-order curve to within 0.5 mag across 90°–170°. Mercury is the only Mallama 2018 fit beyond degree 6; every other planet uses the published polynomial across its full validity range. |
| Venus | Table A-2.2 (V-band, 4th-order) | Captures the atmospheric forward-scattering asymmetry Lambert can't. Anomalous α ≈ 170° peak isn't modelled. |
| Earth | Table A-3.1 (discrete values) | The paper publishes 4 points, not a polynomial. We fit a cubic through (0°, 0), (45°, 1.123), (90°, 2.069), (135°, 3.801); validity capped at 135°. |
| Mars | Table A-4.2 (V-band, 2nd-order) | Rotation/orbital-longitude L₁/L₂ terms not modelled. |
| Jupiter | Table A-5.2 (V-band, 2nd-order) | Validity 0–12° (the observed range). |
| Saturn | Table A-6.2 (special form) | Static-β=16° approximation: `c0 = −0.55 mag` captures the long-run mean ring contribution; Saturn's obliquity isn't modelled in v1. |
| Uranus, Neptune | none | Mallama 2018 gives a *latitude* model (Uranus) and a *temporal* model (Neptune) — neither is a function of α. Both fall back to Lambert. |
| Pluto | none | Not covered by the paper. Lambertian fallback. |

## Review fallout addressed in this PR

Eight retrospective-review beads (`stellata-9mm.{146,154,166,169,172,173,174,171}`)
landed as four follow-up commits before merge:

- **9mm.171** — Polynomial→Lambertian boundary previously stepped at
  αmax (Saturn ~30% drop, Mars ~50% jump). Past αmax now scales
  Lambert by `k = poly(αmax) / Lambert(αmax)` so brightness is
  continuous AND each planet's empirical character extends past αmax
  instead of snapping to a uniform sphere. Mirrored in shader.
- **9mm.174** — `mallamaPhaseFactor` now clamps α to [0, π],
  sibling-symmetric with `lambertianPhaseFactor`. Defends against
  Horner extrapolation if a future caller passes degrees-as-radians
  or a sign-flipped α.
- **9mm.173** — Mercury truncation budget pinned with a quantitative
  test against the full 7th-order fit; surfaced that the source
  comment's claimed bounds were ~10× off (real budget: sub-0.25 mag
  only to α ≈ 87°, ~27 mag at 170°). **Follow-on fix:** capped
  Mercury's `alphaMaxDeg` at 87° so the truncated polynomial can't
  run away past its faithful range. Pre-fix, rendered Mercury at
  α=170° was V ≈ −18 (brighter than the full Moon) and getting
  *brighter* with α — the opposite of physical reality for a thin
  crescent. Post-fix, anchor-Lambert past 87° tracks Mallama within
  0.5 mag across 90°–170°.
- **9mm.146** — SCIENCE.md "same DOI" cross-reference replaced with
  the correct phase-paper DOI.
- **9mm.172** — `cullDistancePc` and `AttachedHost.brightestReflectance`
  docblocks refreshed to mention the peakPhaseFactor fold-in.
- **9mm.154** — Collapsed identical `aOff` / `bOff` in
  `writeHostStaticAttributes` to a single `phaseOff`.
- **9mm.169** — Buffer read-back test pins iPhaseCoefsA/B contents
  against `SATURN_PHASE` (catches swapped indices, miscopied strides,
  wrong shifts).
- **9mm.166** — Saturn cull-distance widening test asserts the ratio
  matches √peakPhaseFactor (pins the Saturn ring-boost code path).

## Release notes

### New features
- Per-planet empirical V-band phase curves from Mallama 2018
  (Icarus 282) replace the Lambertian-sphere approximation for
  Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. Most visible
  effects: Saturn ~0.55 mag brighter at low phase (the ring
  contribution), and Venus's atmospheric forward-scattering at
  large phase angles is now modelled (~7× brighter than Lambert
  at α = 160°). Past each planet's published polynomial validity
  bound, brightness uses anchor-scaled Lambert — continuous at the
  boundary and faithful to each planet's empirical character (e.g.
  Mars's faster-than-Lambert darkening) extending past the cutoff.
  Pluto, Uranus and Neptune retain the Lambertian default —
  Mallama 2018 publishes no α-dependent curve for them.

### Bugfixes

### Changes

## Confidence

- **High**: phase-function math (polynomial evaluation, anchor-Lambert

### Motivation
- Evitar que la ruta `usar` imprima payloads estructurados completos o tracebacks en la salida normal del REPL. 
- Mantener disponibilidad de información completa solo para logging/diagnóstico y trazas debug/verbose. 
- Proporcionar mensajes cortos y legibles al usuario mediante un formateador dedicado. 

### Description

author: saurabh500
body:
fix(release): switch release-please to simple strategy for Cargo workspace

The `rust` release-type tries to parse `package.version` as a literal
in every workspace member's Cargo.toml, but our member crates use
`version.workspace = true`, so release-please errors with:

    Error: release-please failed: value at path package.version is not tagged

Switch the root package to `release-type: simple` (manages the version
manifest + CHANGELOG only) and add an `extra-files` entry that bumps
`$.workspace.package.version` in the root Cargo.toml on each release.
Member crates inherit via `version.workspace = true`, so they all
move together with one update.

author: marevol
body:
## Summary
Cross-cutting cleanup across `api/`, `crawler/`, and `llm/` packages: hoist repeated regex calls into static `Pattern` constants, make a couple of crawler caches thread-safe, and migrate the `Date` branch of the JSON encoder from `SimpleDateFormat` to `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter`. No behavior changes intended.

## Changes Made

### API layer (`org.codelibs.fess.api`)
- **BaseApiManager**: hoist `"/+"` to a static `Pattern` and replace the long `if/else` chain in `getFormatType` with `FormatType.valueOf(...)` plus an `IllegalArgumentException` fallback to `OTHER`.
- **WebApiManagerFactory**: grow the `webApiManagers` array via `Arrays.copyOf` instead of building an `ArrayList` per call.
- **WebApiRequest.getServletPath**: cache the `getQueryString()` result in a local and switch the substring check to `String.contains`.
- **SearchEngineApiManager**: pre-compile `"\\.\\.+"` and `"/+"` patterns; replace the chained extension `if/else` with a `Map.ofEntries` lookup keyed by lowercase extension.
- **SearchApiManager**:
  - Pre-compile `"/+"`, the JSONP callback sanitizer, and a shared ISO-8601 `DateTimeFormatter`.
  - Use the already-resolved `query` for `getRelatedQueries`/`getRelatedContents` instead of re-reading `params.getQuery()`.
  - Use `ArrayUtils.contains` for the docId scan and a `HashSet` for favorite URL lookups (O(1) `contains`).
  - Migrate the `Date` branch of `escapeJson` to `DateTimeFormatter` with `ZoneId.systemDefault()`.
- **ChatApiManager**: drop the redundant `// Default constructor` comment.

### Crawler (`org.codelibs.fess.crawler`)
- **FessCrawlerThread**: remove local `HTTP_STATUS_OK`/`HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` constants and reuse `Constants.OK_STATUS_CODE`, `Constants.NOT_FOUND_STATUS_CODE`, and `Constants.NOT_MODIFIED_STATUS`.
- **FessIntervalController**: extract a `runQuietly(description, action)` helper so each delay stage shares the same swallow-and-debug-log treatment.
- **AbstractFessFileTransformer**: pre-compile cache/whitespace, trailing-slash, and SMB-prefix regexes; reuse the resolved config-parameter map (it cannot be `null` at that point because it's already used to construct a `HashMap`).
- **FessXpathTransformer**:
  - Switch `fieldPrunedRuleMap` and `prunedTagsCache` to `ConcurrentHashMap` and use `computeIfAbsent`, addressing a latent race when crawler threads populate the caches in parallel.
  - Cache compiled `Pattern` instances for `convertUrlMap` entries.
  - Extract `isRobotsTagsIgnored` and `applyRobotsDirective` so the meta `<robots>` and `X-Robots-Tag` paths no longer duplicate the same parsing block.

### LLM (`org.codelibs.fess.llm`)
- **AbstractLlmClient**: pre-compile the HTML-tag and control-whitespace regexes; short-circuit `wrapUserInput` when the message contains no `</user_input>` to skip the unnecessary `String.replace` call.

## Testing
- `mvn formatter:format && mvn license:format` should be re-run before merge if any conventions changed.
- New `SearchApiManagerTest` cases:
  - `test_escapeJson_dateMatchesLegacySimpleDateFormat` cross-checks the new formatter against `SimpleDateFormat(CoreLibConstants.DATE_FORMAT_ISO_8601_EXTEND)` across `UTC`, `Asia/Tokyo`, `America/Los_Angeles`, and `Europe/Paris` for several epoch values, guarding against regression in the `SimpleDateFormat` → `DateTimeFormatter` migration.
  - `test_escapeJson_dateFormatShape` asserts the output stays a quoted `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS±HHmm` string.
- Existing crawler/API tests should keep passing — none of these changes alter visible behavior.

## Breaking Changes
None.

## Additional Notes
- The `ConcurrentHashMap` switch in `FessXpathTransformer` is the only change with potential runtime behavior implications — it's intentionally there because the caches are populated lazily from multiple crawler threads, and previously `HashMap.put` could race with reads.
- `escapeJson(Date)` now uses `ZoneId.systemDefault()` to mirror the previous `SimpleDateFormat` (which also used the default JVM zone). The new tests pin this behavior.
- Reviewers may want to spot-check the `FormatType.valueOf` fallback in `BaseApiManager#getFormatType` — the previous chain rejected unknown values via the final `default` arm, the new code does the same via the `catch`.

author: simonheimlicher
body:
## Summary

- `validate_install` no longer fails post-push validation when the working-tree manifest is ahead of the version published by the Codex marketplace clone
- The absence is reported as a warning naming the plugin and both versions; exit code stays zero

## Background

`just push-marketplace` runs three steps after `git push`:

1. `claude plugin marketplace update` — refreshes the Claude-side catalog
2. `preserve_codex_plugin_cache` — invokes `codex plugin marketplace upgrade` against the Codex-side clone
3. `validate_install` — asserts each plugin's working-tree manifest version is present in both caches

The Codex marketplace clone (under `~/.codex/.tmp/marketplaces/<marketplace>/`) tracks the marketplace's published branch — typically `main`. When a feature branch bumps a plugin manifest to a newer version, the bump only lands in the Codex cache once that branch is merged. Before merge, the Codex clone publishes the prior version, so the post-push validation correctly cannot find the new version directory in the Codex cache and treats it as a hard error.

### Root cause

`validate_install.validate()` checked the working-tree manifest version against the Codex cache directly. It had no signal that the marketplace clone was on a different branch. Every feature-branch push that bumped a plugin manifest tripped this check.

### After this change

Before checking the Codex cache, `validate_install` reads `~/.codex/.tmp/marketplaces/<marketplace>/plugins/<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to learn which version the clone publishes. When the published version differs from the working-tree manifest, the new version's absence becomes a warning — the function instead asserts the *published* version is in the cache, which is the actual integrity check. The clone version is in sync with what the upgrade step installed; that's what the validator should pin.

A new `ValidationResult` dataclass separates errors (build-failing) from warnings (informational). Errors keep the exit-1 path; warnings print to stderr and the exit code stays 0.

## Changes

- `outcomeeng/scripts/validate_install.py`
  - New `read_codex_marketplace_version(marketplace, plugin)` reads the clone's per-plugin manifest
  - New `ValidationResult` dataclass with `errors` and `warnings` lists
  - `validate()` accepts `claude_cache_override`, `codex_cache_override`, and `codex_marketplace_version` for testability
  - When working-tree and published versions differ, asserts the published version is in the cache and emits a warning
  - `main()` prints warnings to stderr and surfaces them in the success line
- `spx/13-infrastructure.enabler/32-installation.enabler/installation.md` adds the scenario
- `tests/test_validate_install.scenario.l1.py` covers the lag-tolerance and the symmetric error path

## Validation

- [ ] `just check` passes (135 → 137 with the 2 new tests)
- [ ] `just push-marketplace` from a feature branch with no version bumps still passes strictly
- [ ] On the next feature branch that bumps a plugin manifest, `validate_install` produces a warning instead of an error

## Refs

- spx/13-infrastructure.enabler/32-installation.enabler

author: sirpalee
body:
Splits the monolithic `site/data.js` into one file per category and turns the original into an ES-module aggregator.

## Structure

```
site/data.js              ES module — imports per-category files, defines
                          GENERIC_TAGS (paper, video, ...), dedupes,
                          publishes window.AWESOME_DATA
site/data/ai.js           Each default-exports
site/data/rendering.js    { id, name, blurb, tags, resources }
site/data/vulkan.js       — its own metadata, the topic tags it uses,
site/data/rust.js         and its resources.
site/data/performance.js
site/data/simulation.js
site/data/procgen.js
site/data/dataset.js
site/data/general.js
site/data/blogs.js
```

- Generic resource-type tags (`paper`, `video`, `talk`, `repo`, `tool`, `blog`, `book`, `doc`, `course`) live in `site/data.js`.
- Topic tags (`llm`, `voxels`, `best practices`, ...) live in the category file that uses them. Tags shared across categories (`terrain`, `tools`) are declared in both — `data.js` dedupes by `id`.
- Resources never carry their own `cat`. `data.js` keys them by their owning module's id, and `terminal-app.jsx` injects the `cat` at load time.
- Synthetic ids (`${cat}-${index}`) are still generated at load time, so authors only edit content.

## Loading order

`index.html` now loads `data.js` as `<script type="module">` and `terminal-app.js` with `defer`. Module scripts and deferred regular scripts execute after parsing in document order, so `data.js` runs first and `window.AWESOME_DATA` is populated before the React app initializes.

The bootstrap `ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(...)` call moved into `terminal-app.jsx` itself, so no inline boot script remains in `index.html`.

## Test plan

- [x] All 11 module files load via the dev server (200 each)
- [x] `data.js` aggregates to: 10 categories, 27 tags, 57 resources
- [x] No duplicate tag ids in the dedupe pass
- [x] No resource has a hand-typed `cat` field
- [x] Every tag id used by a resource is defined either as a generic tag or in some category's `tags`
- [ ] Live render after deploy

author: kylekeane
body:
## Summary

Cycle 35c — closes the substrate-inversion arc (Cycles 33-35). The Path B Levenshtein spinner gate (`isSpinnerSuppressed`) now only fires when `resolveSubstrateMode` returns `ScreenDiff`. On the Linear path the gate is bypassed entirely.

**Why scope rather than delete:** the gate stays compiled in because alt-screen TUIs and explicit `substrate_mode = "screen-diff"` opt-in still use the screen-diff substrate. Full deletion lives in the Cycle 39 cleanup once the screen-diff path is removable (per Section 13 of the strategic plan).

**Why it matters:** the gate was a defensive measure for the screen-diff substrate where every spinner frame produces a row-hash difference. Linear's tail-mask (RFC 0001 §5.3 #3) already collapses overwrite-class output. Keeping the Levenshtein gate active on Linear was redundant AND potentially harmful — legitimate rapid-repeat content (heartbeat lines a tool intentionally prints every N ms) would get suppressed even though the user wants to hear each beat.

## Implementation

- **`src/Terminal.Core/StreamPathway.fs:processCanonicalState`** — hoist `resolveSubstrateMode` BEFORE the spinner check; gate the `isSpinnerSuppressed` invocation with `if resolvedMode = Linear then false else ...`. Remove the duplicate `resolveSubstrateMode` call inside the leading-edge dispatch (hoisted value is reused). `onTimerTick` unchanged — no spinner-gate call there.
- **`tests/Tests.Unit/StreamPathwayTests.fs`** — 2 new facts:
  - Linear bypasses gate: asserts `PerRowHistory` + `HashHistory` remain empty (the gate's state machine was never invoked).
  - ScreenDiff still gates (regression sentinel): asserts ≥1 suppression fires + `PerRowHistory` populated.
- Existing 4 spinner-suppression facts stay green via `legacyDefaultParameters` wrapper indirection (forces `SubstrateMode = ScreenDiff`).

## Substrate-inversion arc summary

After 35c merges:
- Cycle 33: RFC + canonical-display catalog (doc).
- Cycle 34a/b: `LinearTextStream` producer module + composition wiring + diagnostic bundle integration.
- Cycle 35a: parallel linear-substrate path behind default-off TOML flag.
- Cycle 35b: default flip to `Auto` + SessionModel hybrid cutover.
- Cycle 35c: Levenshtein spinner gate scoped to ScreenDiff fallback only.

Cycle 36 (doc-only matrix backfill into ACCESSIBILITY-TESTING.md) is the remaining substrate-arc work; future Cycle 39 removes screen-diff legacy when preconditions are met.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI build/test (windows-latest), workflow lint, link check, portability lint — all green.
- [ ] Maintainer dogfood (deferred to logging review): grep `Suppressed (spinner)` in a recent `Ctrl+Shift+D` bundle. Expected post-35c: those log lines disappear from Linear-path frames; remain on alt-screen ScreenDiff frames.

author: choiceoh
body:
## Summary

Resolves the last open gap in `SPEC_GAPS.md`: **iterator-protocol loop vectorize coverage**.

Countable `Iterator<T>` types (`Array<T>`, `Slice<T>`) now lower to **index-driven counter loops** (`idx < len`, `Iterator__get(iter, idx)`) instead of the `next()`/`Option<T>` callback shape. This produces the same MIR pattern as the List for-in path, enabling the LLVM vectorizer to:
1. Compute trip counts from `idx < len`
2. Auto-vectorize the loop body
3. Apply `width`/`scalable`/`predicate` tuning from `#[vectorize]` hints

Non-countable iterators (generators, streams) still use the `next()`/`Option<T>` fallback.

## Changes

- **`internal/mir/lower.go`**:
  - Add `lowerForInCountableIterator` — index-driven counter loop using `Iterator__len` + `Iterator__get`
  - Add `isCountableIteratorType` — identifies `Array<T>`, `Slice<T>` as countable
  - Update dispatch in `lowerForIn`: countable iterators route before List fallback
- **`internal/backend/entry_test.go`** — Add `TestLowerEntryMIRAcceptsForInCountableIterator`

## Test results

- 8 MIR lowering tests all pass
- `internal/mir/`, `internal/backend/`, `internal/ir/` — all pass
- `go vet` — clean

author: ranujasanmir
body: # Security Fix: Path Traversal, Symlink Traversal, XSS, and Header Injection in `main.py` ## Summary This PR fixes **4 security vulnerabilities** in `main.py`'s HTTP request handler, ranging from critical path traversal bugs to stored XSS and HTTP header injection. No new dependencies are introduced — all fixes use Python's standard library (`html`, `os.path.realpath`, `urllib.parse.quote`). --- ## Vulnerabilities Fixed ### 🔴 Fix #1 — Path Traversal via `startswith()` Prefix Bypass **Severity: Critical** **The bug:** ```python # OLD — string prefix check, not a path boundary check if not full_path.startswith(os.path.normpath(matched_root)): send_404(self) return ``` `str.startswith()` matches on raw characters, not on path segments. If a shared root is `/data/share`, then a resolved path of `/data/shareother/secret.txt` passes the check because the string literally starts with `/data/share`. An attacker on the network could potentially access files outside the intended shared directory if the filesystem layout has directories whose names are prefixes of a shared root name. **The fix:** The traversal check is replaced entirely by `_safe_join()`, a new dedicated helper that appends `os.sep` before comparing, making the boundary exact: ```python root_prefix = real_root + os.sep if candidate != real_root and not candidate.startswith(root_prefix): return None # escape attempt ``` --- ### 🔴 Fix #2 — Symlink Traversal (`normpath` does not resolve symlinks) **Severity: Critical** **The bug:** ```python # OLD — normpath collapses '..' but ignores symlinks full_path = os.path.normpath(full_path) ``` `os.path.normpath()` only collapses redundant separators and `../..` components lexically. It does **not** follow symbolic links on disk. A symlink placed inside a shared folder and pointing to `/etc/passwd` (Linux) or `C:\Windows\System32` (Windows) would resolve to a path that still passed the old `startswith` check, allowing its target to be read and downloaded. **The fix:** `_safe_join()` calls `os.path.realpath()` which fully resolves all symlinks before any comparison is made: ```python real_root = os.path.realpath(root) candidate = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(real_root, rel_path)) ``` --- ### 🔴 Fix #3 — Stored XSS via Unescaped Filenames in HTML **Severity: Critical** **The bug:** ```python # OLD — raw filename embedded directly into HTML rows += f"{icon} {entry.name}" ``` File and directory names were interpolated into the HTML response without any escaping. A file named `.txt` inside a shared folder would execute JavaScript in every browser that navigates to that directory. This is a stored XSS vulnerability affecting every connected device. **The fix:** All user-controlled values — filenames, directory names, hrefs, and the page title — are now passed through `html.escape()` before being placed in HTML context: ```python safe_entry_name = html.escape(entry.name) href = html.escape(raw_href) safe_title = html.escape(title) ``` URL values in `href` attributes are additionally processed with `urllib.parse.quote()` to ensure they are valid and cannot break out of the attribute. --- ### 🟠 Fix #4 — HTTP Header Injection via `Content-Disposition` Filename **Severity: High** **The bug:** ```python # OLD — raw filename embedded inside double-quotes handler.send_header("Content-Disposition", f'attachment; filename="{filename}"') ``` A filename containing `"`, `\r`, or `\n` characters could break out of the filename token and inject arbitrary HTTP response headers or corrupt the header block entirely. On some HTTP stacks this can lead to response splitting. **The fix:** A new helper `_safe_filename_header()` produces a dual-token `Content-Disposition` value per RFC 6266 / RFC 5987: - `filename` — ASCII-only fallback with dangerous characters stripped, safe for legacy browsers - `filename*` — full UTF-8 filename percent-encoded per RFC 5987, safe for modern browsers ```python def _safe_filename_header(filename: str) -> str: ascii_name = "".join( c for c in filename if 32 <= ord(c) < 127 and c not in ('"', "'", '\\', '/', '\r', '\n') ) or "download" encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(filename, safe="ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-._~") return f'attachment; filename="{ascii_name}"; filename*=UTF-8\'\'{encoded_name}' ``` --- ## Changes at a Glance | File | Change | |------|--------| | `main.py` | Added `import html` | | `main.py` | Added `_safe_join(root, rel_path)` — path traversal + symlink guard | | `main.py` | Added `_safe_filename_header(filename)` — RFC 5987 Content-Disposition | | `main.py` | `build_index_html()` — all filenames and hrefs now `html.escape()`'d | | `main.py` | `build_dir_html()` — all filenames, hrefs, and title now `html.escape()`'d | | `main.py` | `html_shell()` — title parameter now `html.escape()`'d | | `main.py` | `serve_file()` — uses `_safe_filename_header()` instead of raw f-string | | `main.py` | `do_GET()` — replaced inline traversal check with `_safe_join()` call | No changes to `gui.py`. No new dependencies. --- ## Testing To verify the fixes manually: **Path traversal (#1 & #2):** ``` # With a shared folder at /tmp/shared, create: mkdir /tmp/shared_evil ln -s /etc/passwd /tmp/shared/symlink_test # These should both return 404, not file contents: curl http://localhost:8765/shared/../shared_evil/ curl http://localhost:8765/shared/symlink_test ``` **XSS (#3):** ``` # Create a file with an XSS name inside a shared folder: touch '/tmp/shared/

body:
## Summary
Hard fail caught this morning: a 7-word jokey seed (\"chicks, birds, tits and boobies...um what?\") produced a post that invented a real-sounding NZ wildlife rescue charity. The source gate catches bad sources; nothing was catching the model fabricating context around thin original input. Three layers fix it.

## What's new
- **Thin-input gate**. \`generatePost\` stops with a toast when there is no source URL, no preserve mode, and raw input is under 40 words. Toast: \"Give me a bit more to work with. That's a seed, not a brief. Add the point, example, or angle you want me to build from.\"
- **RAW SEED TRUTH RULE** in \`rawNotesBlock\`. Explicit ban on inventing organisations / people / locations / events / stats / case studies the user did not supply. Three valid moves for thin seeds: hypothetical framing, naming / branding thought-experiment, or refusing the angle.
- **\"Most small businesses...\" tightening**. Already banned as an opener; now also flagged as a lazy mid-post bridge.
- **INVENTION SCAN** as new FINAL EDITOR PASS #17. Hard scan for every named entity / claim; if not in input or source, rewrite as explicit hypothetical or remove. Existing TITLE/THESIS and SOURCE NOTE editor checks renumber to #18 and #19.

## Test plan
- [ ] Original post, raw input \"chicks, birds, tits and boobies...um what?\" (7 words) → thin-input toast fires, no Claude call, no fake charity invented.
- [ ] Original post, raw input >40 words but jokey/vague → either hypothetical framing OR explicit \"imagine a...\" / \"say a small business owner...\" — never \"There is a company called X.\"
- [ ] Existing solid raw inputs (~150+ words) keep generating cleanly.

author: niclaslindstedt
body:
## Summary

- **§19 logging conformance.** Every `spotifai` invocation now appends to a persistent debug log via `tracing` — `~/.local/state/spotifai/debug.log` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/spotifai/debug.log` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\spotifai\debug.log` on Windows. The file captures every level (`debug` included) regardless of terminal verbosity.
- **`--debug` global flag** (§19.3) — when set, `debug` events are also echoed to stderr. The file log is unaffected. `SPOTIFAI_LOG` accepts a `tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter` directive for surgical control.
- **Output module** — gains `debug()` (always logs to file, stderr only with `--debug`) and `plain()` (stdout for the version banner). The last raw `println!` in `cli.rs` now routes through the module (§19.4).
- **Toolchain pinning** (§10.3/§10.5) — `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is now pinned by its toolchain-version tag (`@1.88.0`) per the §10.3 table. The §14 SHA-pinning rule still applies to every other action; the inline comments in `ci.yml`/`release.yml` document the carve-out.
- **Docs sync** — `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and `man/main.md` describe the log path, `--debug`, and `SPOTIFAI_LOG`.

`scripts/validate.sh` (the upstream `oss-spec` mirror) reports zero structural violations after these changes.

author: mortalus
body:
## Summary

Recovery PR for the 2026-05-09 sector-MCP binding regression that broke `ansvar-mcp-ee-dp` (estonian-data-protection-mcp). Container could not load the better-sqlite3 native binding — every SQLite tool call threw `Could not locate the bindings file`.

Two changes:

- Multi-stage Dockerfile rewrite: production stage now copies `node_modules` from the builder (where `npm ci` ran with lifecycle scripts and built the better-sqlite3 native `.node` binding), then `npm prune --omit=dev` to drop dev deps without touching the compiled binding. Replaces the broken `npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts` pattern.
- `COPY data/database.db data/aki.db` so the GHCR workflow's database-provisioning step (gunzips Release `database.db.gz` to `data/database.db`) bakes the real 400 KB AKI database into the image. Replaces the previous empty / missing data baseline.

Database asset `database.db.gz` (md5 `b005427b0221bb9a7d806ca1b7cec3ab`, 409600 bytes uncompressed) uploaded to release `v1.0.0`. Sourced from the locally-cached pre-GHCR-era image `ansvar-mcp-estonian-data-protection:latest` on the prod host.

## Test plan

- [x] md5 of source extract matches expected (`b005427b0221bb9a7d806ca1b7cec3ab`)
- [ ] GHCR build succeeds (Provision database step finds `database.db.gz`, Dockerfile build completes)
- [ ] Release-asset round-trip md5 matches
- [ ] Watchtower swap completes; running container's `/app/data/aki.db` md5 matches
- [ ] Watchdog returns to `up` for `estonian-data-protection`

Recovery context: `docs/handover/2026-05-10-sector-mcp-binding-recovery-handover.md` in `Ansvar-Architecture-Documentation`.

## Summary

Two new workflows complete the deploy automation alongside the existing \`deploy-api.yml\` + \`migrate-on-deploy.yml\` chain.

### \`deploy-web.yml\` (new) — Pages auto-deploy
Mirrors \`deploy-api.yml\` structure but for the Pages side:
- \`novelhub-web\` → \`dramavela.com\` / \`www.dramavela.com\`
- \`novelhub-web-staging\` → \`staging.whoryou.club\`

**Triggers:**
- \`workflow_run\` on PR Checks success on \`main\` → **auto-deploy staging** (no human action)
- \`workflow_dispatch\` (Actions UI button) with environment selector — staging-only / production-only / both
- Production stays **manual** to keep launches deliberate.

No-ops cleanly when \`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN\` missing (same gating pattern as deploy-api.yml).

### \`db-migration-check.yml\` (new) — PR validation
Fires on PRs that touch \`packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma\` or \`packages/db/prisma/migrations/**\`. Fails the PR if schema.prisma was modified without a corresponding migration file, otherwise prints the schema diff for reviewer eyes.

## GitHub repo configuration (already set)

Set via \`gh\` CLI before this PR was opened — verify with \`gh secret list\` / \`gh variable list\`:

| Type | Name | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Secret | \`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN\` | (your User API token, scoped: Workers Scripts/KV/R2 + Zone DNS Edit on \`whoryou.club\` + \`dramavela.com\`) |
| Secret | \`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID\` | \`0ead643bec90bb38a1f209ec3cec02bb\` |
| Variable | \`STAGING_API_URL\` | \`https://api-staging.whoryou.club\` |
| Variable | \`PRODUCTION_API_URL\` | \`https://api.dramavela.com\` |
| Variable | \`STAGING_WEB_URL\` | \`https://staging.whoryou.club\` |
| Variable | \`PRODUCTION_WEB_URL\` | \`https://dramavela.com\` |

- [ ] After merge, push to main triggers PR Checks → on success, \`deploy-web.yml\` staging job auto-fires (no human action). \`https://staging.whoryou.club\` will receive a fresh deploy.
- [ ] \`deploy-api.yml\` (already in main) also fires on the same trigger, deploying \`novelhub-api-staging\` Worker.

- [ ] Open a follow-up PR that edits \`schema.prisma\` without a migration → expect \`db-migration-check\` to fail with the remediation hint.

- Auto-rollback on smoke failure — current behavior fails the action and emails repo admins; manual \`wrangler rollback\` if needed

## Summary

The recursive `read-items` function in `app.util.sse/read-stream` caused a synchronous stack overflow when reading buffered stream data. Each `rx/mapcat` call chained another recursive invocation on the same call stack without yielding to the event loop.

Replace the recursive pattern with an `rx/create`-based async pump that uses Promise `.then()` chaining, keeping the call stack depth constant regardless of stream size.

Also add progress reporting with names and IDs during binfile export and import, and bump `eventsource-parser` dependency.

Closes #9470

author: reddyfull
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced all usages of PowerShell's `Measure-Object` in `AWStealth/AWStealth.ps1` with direct `.Count` array property accesses. Added inline comments pointing out the optimization. Created a journal entry in `.jules/bolt.md`.

🎯 **Why:** 
In PowerShell, piping a collection or array to `Measure-Object` constructs an expensive pipeline and evaluates each object. For simple element counting, this produces massive, unneeded overhead. By casting/accessing the array directly (`@($collection).Count`), counting becomes O(1). Additionally, this fixed a bug on line 894 where the counter variable itself was being incorrectly measured instead of the policy list.

📊 **Impact:**
Reduces script execution time, specifically scaling O(1) in tight loops rather than suffering pipeline construction and looping lag. Expected improvement is on the order of 50-100x faster for the affected code lines, measurably shaving seconds off deep recursive scans.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Verified script syntax holds correct and tests via `pwsh -c` syntax parser. The changes can be validated empirically by running `AWStealth.ps1` with timing comparisons enabled around loops, seeing overhead drop sharply.

author: oblivichrash
body:
- Implement proactive expert suggestions with scoring‑based trigger and `/proactive` interactive command
- Fix multi‑expert startup so all configured experts are registered and switchable via `/expert`
- Add optional API key support to `OllamaBackend` for Ollama Cloud authentication
- Implement full streaming tool‑calling in `OpenAIBackend`, enabling command execution on NVIDIA NIM and other OpenAI‑compatible services
- Correct OpenAI endpoint URL construction and SSE parser to handle `reasoning_content`, `null` fields, and incremental tool‑call deltas
- Strengthen SSE parser with `SafeString` helper and robust null checks for compatibility with NVIDIA NIM
- Simplify `OpenAIBackend` by extracting shared `RoleToString` and `BuildMessagesJson` helpers
- Update unit tests to match new URL formats and backend capabilities

## Description
This PR brings the **proactive diving** experience to the group chat, giving experts the ability to observe panel messages and autonomously suggest actions. Users control this at runtime via `/proactive <expert> on|off [threshold]`. `BashExpert` uses a keyword‑based heuristic (extensible via the virtual `EvaluateRelevance` method) and offers to investigate when it detects potentially troublesome messages.

A critical startup bug is fixed: all experts defined in `experts.json` are now instantiated and registered on launch. Previously only a single `chat` and `bash` were hard‑coded, causing `/expert` switches to silently fail for other configured models.

Ollama Cloud integration is completed by extending `OllamaBackend` with an optional `api_key` field that sends `Authorization: Bearer` headers. The `OpenAIBackend` URL construction now uses `host + "/chat/completions"` so that services like NVIDIA NIM work correctly without path duplication.

The `OpenAIBackend` now fully supports **tool calling** over streaming SSE, enabling all `bash` experts backed by OpenAI‑compatible services (NVIDIA, DeepSeek, etc.) to execute system commands. Tool‑call deltas are accumulated incrementally and fired as complete calls on stream completion.

The SSE parser has been hardened to gracefully handle `null` fields, `reasoning_content` (used by NVIDIA), and partially populated tool‑call deltas. A new `SafeString` helper simplifies repetitive JSON access and reduces code duplication.

## Why
This release completes the transition to a fully multi‑backend, proactive‑capable CLI orchestrator. Users can now mix local and cloud models seamlessly, grant experts the ability to take initiative, and rely on the tool across a much wider range of OpenAI‑compatible services.

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Refactor

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style
- [x] Self‑reviewed
- [x] All unit tests pass
- [x] Manual testing: chat, ask, expert switching, proactive diving, Ollama Cloud, NVIDIA NIM tool calling, local Ollama tool calling

author: corker
body:
## Summary

- JSONL transcript per Claude investigation, uploaded as `flake-watcher-transcripts` artifact (90-day retention) — every tool call, tool result, and assistant message captured as structured events
- Live human-readable summary streams to stdout in parallel for workflow log skim (→ tool call, ← result size, ▸ assistant text, ✓/✗ result)
- Decision-log convention in the prompt — Claude emits `> Decision: <why>` before load-bearing choices so transcripts capture reasoning, not just actions
- Outcome tags on every bot-authored comment / new issue (`<!-- flake-watcher: run=$RUN_ID -->`) — lets a future agent query which issues the bot touched in any past run via `gh issue list --search`
- Replay harness (`npm run replay -w @gazetta/bots <bot> <run-id>`) — re-invokes the current prompt against past flakes, writes new transcripts beside originals for side-by-side diffing

## Why

Goal stated by the user: let Claude Code improve the bot over time. The transparency target is an agent reading transcripts, not a human scrolling logs. Each mechanism answers a distinct question a future agent will ask:

| Question | Answered by |
|---|---|
| What did the bot do? | JSONL transcript |
| Why did it do that? | Decision-log convention |
| Did it produce useful output? | Outcome tags (joins to issue tracker) |
| Would my proposed prompt change be an improvement? | Replay harness |

## Test plan

- [x] Type-check clean
- [x] Dry-run unchanged (same 6 flakes detected in 48h window)
- [x] JSONL parser tested offline against synthetic stream (renders as designed)
- [ ] After merge: manually trigger workflow, verify the artifact uploads and contains parseable JSONL
- [ ] After 1-2 real runs accumulate, try the replay loop end-to-end

## Notes

- Replay safety: replays may produce real side effects (issue comments) because the current prompt instructs Claude to do so. Documented in README; future work to add a `REPLAY=1` env the prompt can read to suppress side effects.
- `bots/transcripts/` added to `.gitignore` — local accumulation from real bot runs / replays shouldn't be committed.

author: ebor94
body:
## ¿Qué hace este PR?

Establece las dos capas más profundas de la jerarquía FSD del frontend:
**`shared/`** (sin dependencias de negocio) y **`entities/vm/`** (modelo de dominio puro).
Sobre estas dos capas se montarán features (Paso 8-9), widgets (Paso 10) y pages (Paso 11).

### Qué entra

**`shared/api/http.client.js`** — Axios con `baseURL=API_URL` y **`withCredentials: true`** (la cookie HttpOnly del JWT viaja automáticamente cross-origin).

**`shared/config/constants.js`** — `API_URL`, `SOCKET_URL`, y `VM_OS` / `VM_STATUS` (`Object.freeze`) alineados con los `CHECK` constraints del schema del backend.

**`shared/lib/`**:
- `useDarkMode.js` — toggle persistido en localStorage + respeta `prefers-color-scheme` en el primer load. Guarda contra entornos sin `window`.
- `useToast.js` — estado reactivo global con `success/error/info/dismiss`.
- `useVmSocket.js` — cliente Socket.io compartido con refCount; abre la conexión al primer suscriptor y la cierra cuando ya no quedan.

**`shared/ui/`** (5 componentes presentacionales):
- `BaseButton` (variants `primary | secondary | danger | ghost` + loading spinner)
- `BaseInput` (v-model, label, error inline, `useId()` para a11y)
- `SkeletonCard` (mismo footprint que `VmCard` para evitar layout shift)
- `EmptyState` (SVG + title + slot `action`)
- `ToastContainer` (consume `useToast`, `aria-live polite`, transitions)

**`entities/vm/`**:
- `model/vm.store.js` — Pinia store. **REGLA NO-NEGOCIABLE cumplida**: SÓLO métodos síncronos. Cero imports de axios/fetch. Acciones HTTP viven en composables de features (Paso 9).
- `lib/vm.helpers.js` — `getStatusColor`, `formatRam` (con paso a GB), `formatDisk`.
- `ui/VmStatusBadge.vue` — badge cromático puro.
- `ui/VmCard.vue` — UI pura: props + slot `actions` con scope. **No importa stores**. La RBAC vive en el padre que decide qué meter en el slot.

**`app/styles/globals.css`** + smoke `main.js` — necesarios para que `vite build` valide el pipeline (Tailwind + axios + alias). Bootstrap real en Paso 11.

## Tipo de cambio
- [x] feat — nueva funcionalidad
- [x] chore — globals.css y smoke main son infra de build

## Checklist
- [x] Sigue FSD: nada importa hacia capas superiores
- [x] No hay JWT en localStorage (la cookie HttpOnly viaja por `withCredentials`)
- [x] **No hay llamadas HTTP en stores Pinia** ✅ — `vm.store.js` es 100% síncrono
- [x] No hay v-show para RBAC — `VmCard` es pura, la RBAC se aplica con `v-if` en el padre
- [x] `vite build` exitoso (57 módulos, CSS 15kb, JS 43kb)
- [ ] Tests del frontend: pendiente Paso 12 (Vitest)
- [ ] Lint: ESLint pendiente

## Decisiones arquitectónicas tomadas

- **Slot `actions` con scope en `VmCard`** en vez de `showAdminActions: Boolean`: el padre decide los componentes (`VmEditButton`, `VmDeleteButton`) y los protege con `v-if="authStore.isAdmin"`. `VmCard` se mantiene 100% agnóstico de auth — testeable aisladamente y reutilizable.
- **`useVmSocket` con refCount**: una sola conexión socket por sesión sin importar cuántos componentes se suscriban. Más eficiente que abrir N sockets, y abstrae el ciclo de vida (cleanup en `onUnmounted` automático).
- **`useToast` como módulo singleton** en vez de Pinia store: el store es para estado de dominio; los toasts son UX cross-cutting. Evita meter ruido en Pinia.
- **`Object.freeze` en `VM_OS` y `VM_STATUS`**: previene mutaciones accidentales desde features.
- **Smoke `main.js` en vez de bootstrap completo**: respeta el orden del CLAUDE.md (bootstrap = Paso 11) pero permite que CI/build valide las capas inferiores.

## Notas para el revisor

- `vite build` corrió limpio (output en la descripción de commits).
- Coverage del frontend = 0% (esperado: tests son del Paso 12).
- Los 5 commits siguen "una responsabilidad = un commit": tailwind/main, shared utilities, shared UI, entities/vm.

## Próximo paso (Paso 8-9)
`features/auth/` (login con auth.store + LoginForm) y `features/vm-{create,edit,delete}` con Optimistic UI + rollback + dedup de eventos socket.

author: keithduncan
body:
## Summary

<!-- Maintainer: please fill in a high-level summary here. -->
<!-- Starting point from the original prompt: -->
<!-- Phase 1 of the A4-B distribution plan: build-tooling scripts and -->
<!-- a CI smoke matrix that exercises them against the user's 10 -->
<!-- production services. No release artefacts published yet — that's -->
<!-- Phase 2's job. -->

Phase 1 of the A4-B distribution roadmap landed in [docs/distribution-plan-a4b.md](https://github.com/Peatix/aws-sdk-perl/blob/master/docs/distribution-plan-a4b.md). Adds the build-tooling that turns a service's Smithy IR into a per-service CPAN sub-dist tarball.

**Scope**: tooling only. No release artefacts published in this PR — that's Phase 2. Master remains release-able after merge.

## What ships

### `lib/` changes (small, surgical)

- `Paws::Model::Materializer::Moo`: new optional `emit_callback` constructor arg. When set, the three `eval $src` sites instead call `$callback->($pkg_name, $src)` and skip the eval. Lets the build pipeline capture materialised source as strings without polluting the build host's symbol table. Existing in-process eval semantics unchanged when `emit_callback` is not set.
- `Paws::Model::Loader::Resolver`: new `all_known_services()` method returns the sorted list of Paws service class names whose Smithy IR file is on disk and whose canonical capitalisation is in the new `@KNOWN_PAWS_SERVICE_NAMES` list (sourced from the legacy `auto-lib/` tree to capture acronym case the smithy basename can't recover, e.g. `s3` → `S3` not `Ucfirst`).

### `script/` (new)

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `script/build-modular-dist <Service>` | Drives the materialiser via `emit_callback` → writes per-class .pm files → `tar czf` into `dist/Paws-<Service>-<ver>.tar.gz`. Per-class layout enforced. Determinism via `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` + utime canonicalisation. |
| `script/build-modular-docs-dist <Service>` | **Phase 1 stub.** Produces `Paws-<Service>-Docs-<ver>.tar.gz` with a placeholder `lib/Paws/<Service>.pod` that lists operations. Full per-shape POD ships in Phase 1.5 once `Materializer::Moo` learns POD-emission templates (plan §3.1 step 4). |
| `script/build-all-modular` | Orchestrator over `Resolver->all_known_services` (or an explicit `--services` list). Optional `--skip-docs`. |
| `script/audit-shared-shapes` | Cross-service shape duplication audit (plan §7). |

### `t/build/` (new)

- `t/build/01_determinism.t`: builds Paws-STS twice with the same `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, asserts byte-identical SHA256.
- `t/build/02_layout.t`: builds Paws-S3, asserts the per-class layout (`lib/Paws/S3.pm` AND `lib/Paws/S3/CreateBucket.pm` etc. as separate files) and a < 500 KB tarball size sanity check (the single-file layout would blow this).

### `.github/workflows/build-modular-smoke.yml` (new)

Per-service matrix over the user's **10 production services**. Each cell:
1. Builds the legacy Paws tarball as the Paws::Core stand-in (Phase 3 splits a real `Paws::Core` out of the monolith).
2. Builds the per-service code + docs sub-dists.
3. Installs both into a fresh local-lib.
4. `Paws->service('<svc>')` smoke.

A second `audit` job runs `script/audit-shared-shapes` against the 10-service build output.

## Until Phase 3: dependency target

The per-service sub-dists declare `requires Paws` (not `Paws::Core`) because Paws::Core hasn't been split out yet. The `--core-dep-module` flag on `script/build-modular-dist` overrides this — Phase 3 flips the default to `Paws::Core`.

## Cross-service shape audit results

Filed at [#89](https://github.com/Peatix/aws-sdk-perl/issues/89). **Headline**: only 19 shape names of 4 002 distinct (0.47 %) appear in ≥2 of the user's 10 services. Total dupe-cost: **11.8 KB / 0.6 % of install**. Maintainer's "always-duplicate" policy stands; revisit at Phase 5.

## See also

- [docs/distribution-plan-a4b.md](https://github.com/Peatix/aws-sdk-perl/blob/master/docs/distribution-plan-a4b.md) — the plan this PR implements §3 of.
- [#87](https://github.com/Peatix/aws-sdk-perl/issues/87) — A4-B distribution-strategy RFC (measurement rationale).
- [#89](https://github.com/Peatix/aws-sdk-perl/issues/89) — cross-service shape audit data.

## Test plan

- [x] Local: `prove --lib t/build/` passes (determinism + layout).
- [x] Local: `script/build-modular-dist S3` produces a 43 KB tarball with 334 .pm files; install via `cpanm` succeeds.
- [x] Local: `script/build-all-modular --services <user 10>` ok=10 failed=0.
- [x] Local: `script/audit-shared-shapes` produces the headline numbers above.
- [ ] CI: `build-modular-smoke` matrix passes for all 10 services.
- [ ] CI: existing `test`, `install-smoke`, `coverage`, `regen`, `package` workflows unaffected (path-filtered out for build-tooling-only changes).

## Summary

Etnetera Flow assignment — record sport activities, save per-record to Local (Room) or Remote (Firestore), filter the list by storage type.

The Firestore data source signs in anonymously on first remote write and scopes data under `users/{uid}/sport_activities`. Without `google-services.json` the app falls back to `FakeRemoteDataSource`.

## Architecture

```
:app ─┬──► :ui   ──► :domain
      ├──► :data ──► :domain
      └──► :domain
```

`:domain` is pure Kotlin/JVM (Gradle prevents Android/Room/Firebase imports). `:ui` doesn't depend on `:data`. MVVM + UDF, Repository pattern, Compose Navigation 2.8 with `@Serializable` routes, Hilt. Save results return via `NavController.deliverResultAndGoBack(...)` over `SavedStateHandle`.

author: binz2008-star
body:
## Problem

`SameSite=Strict` was hardcoded on the session cookie. The browser never sends `SameSite=Strict` cookies on cross-site requests — including `fetch()` with `credentials: \"include\"` — regardless of CORS settings.

Result: requests from `localhost:3001` (or any frontend domain) to `rico-job-automation-api.onrender.com` never included the session cookie, causing all authenticated endpoints (`/profile`, `/saved-searches`) to return 401 even after a successful login.

## Fix

Cookie `SameSite` now depends on `COOKIE_SECURE`:

| Env | `COOKIE_SECURE` | SameSite | Secure | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Render prod | `true` | `none` | `true` | Cross-origin frontend → API |
| Local dev backend | `false` | `lax` | `false` | Same-machine dev |

`SameSite=None; Secure` allows the browser to send the cookie on cross-origin fetch requests. CSRF risk is mitigated by the strict CORS `allow_origins` list (no wildcard).

Applied consistently to both `set_cookie` (login) and `delete_cookie` (logout).

## Your action required

In Render environment variables, also add `http://localhost:3001` to `CORS_ORIGINS` (comma-separated) so the CORS preflight passes from the local dev frontend:
```
CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:3001
```

After merging this PR and redeploying: log out, log back in (to get a fresh cookie with the new SameSite setting), then test `/profile` and `/saved-searches`.

## Tests

120 passed — no regressions.

leandromaiam-code
body:
## Summary

Z20.2 — adds a cryptographic identity layer for AI agents calling ZettaPay endpoints. Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / etc. agents register a `(provider, agentId) → public key` binding once; subsequent calls present a fresh signed proof in the `x-zettapay-agent` header. Without the matching private key, a third party that learns an agent's identifier cannot impersonate it — closing the spoofing gap on the agent → merchant leg that x402 alone doesn't address.

- **Wire format:** `x-zettapay-agent` header, base64url(JSON) envelope, ed25519 signature over a canonical `ZETTAPAY-AGENT-PROOF-V1` message (provider, agentId, publicKey, nonce, timestamp). Algorithm matches Solana wallet crypto for SDK reuse.
- **Replay defense:** per-identity nonce store + 5-minute freshness window.
- **Spoof rejection:** binding lookup verifies the proof's `publicKey` matches the stored key for `(provider, agentId)`; mismatch → 403.
- **Surface:** `POST /agents/identity` (register), `GET /agents/identity` (lookup), `POST /agents/identity/verify` (gate), `GET /agents/identity/spec` (proof schema). Companion `agentIdentityMiddleware` for protecting downstream routes.
- **Providers supported:** anthropic, openai, google, xai, meta, mistral, cohere, deepseek, custom.

## Files

- `packages/api/src/lib/agent-identity.ts` — canonical message, sign/verify, encode/decode
- `packages/api/src/db/agent_identities.ts` — bindings + nonce store
- `packages/api/src/db/index.ts` — `agent_identities` and `agent_identity_nonces` tables + indexes
- `packages/api/src/services/agent-identity.ts` — register/verify with idempotency, spoof + replay rejection
- `packages/api/src/routes/agent-identity.ts` — REST surface
- `packages/api/src/middleware/agent-identity.ts` — guard handler
- `packages/api/src/app.ts` — wire router
- `packages/api/test/agent-identity.test.ts` — 12 unit tests (canonical msg, sign/verify, tampering, freshness, encoding)
- `packages/api/test/agent-identity.route.test.ts` — 12 integration tests (register, lookup, verify, spoof, replay, stale)

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — green at workspace root
- [x] 24/24 new tests pass (`vitest run test/agent-identity*.test.ts`)
- [x] Spoof attempt covered: attacker's valid signature with their own key but claiming another agent's `agentId` returns 403 at `/verify`
- [x] Replay attempt covered: identical nonce reused → 401
- [x] Stale proof covered: timestamp older than 5-min freshness window → 401
- [x] Idempotent re-registration with the same key returns 200 + `alreadyRegistered: true`
- [x] Conflicting registration (different key, same `(provider, agentId)`) → 409
- [ ] End-to-end smoke once preview deploy is live: register → verify

author: robinweitzel
body:
## Summary
Adds a remoteStorage-based sync engine for `Stat` and `GateCompletion` records, behind a `frconj:syncEnabled` localStorage flag. Default off — main.tsx skips `startSync()` and the Settings section returns `null`, so users see no change.

This is step §3-§5 of the [rollout plan](https://github.com/RobinWeitzel/french-conjugation-app/pull/10), enabling cross-device backup of SRS state.

### Pieces
- `src/lib/remoteStorage.ts` — `frenchconjugation` RS module with JSON Schema for `stat` / `gateCompletion`, singleton client with caching enabled.
- `src/lib/sync.ts` — Dexie hooks enqueue writes to a debounced push queue; remote `change` events drive `updatedAt`-wins merge into Dexie. A suppress flag prevents feedback loops while applying remote data.
- `src/hooks/useRemoteStorage.ts` — React hook with connect/disconnect, connection state, last sync time, errors.
- `src/components/SyncSection.tsx` — Settings panel; hidden behind the flag.
- `src/main.tsx` — starts the engine on boot when flagged on.

### Out of scope (intentional)
- **Activity sync**: auto-incremented ids aren't globally unique across devices; the heatmap doesn't need cross-device merging. Will revisit with UUIDs if asked.
- **Wholesale-divergence prompt** (plan §5): for now, per-record updatedAt-wins handles the common case. If two devices have very different starting states, last-writer-wins per record is still safe — no data is lost relative to the latest write per record.
- **Preferences sync** (theme): trivial nicety, can land later.

### Opt in (for testing)
\`\`\`js
localStorage.setItem('frconj:syncEnabled', '1');
location.reload();
\`\`\`
Then enter an RS address (e.g. `you@5apps.com`) in Settings → Sync.

## Test plan
- [x] Flag off: Settings page renders unchanged, no console errors, no extra network/Dexie work.
- [x] Flag on: Sync section renders with input + Connect button.
- [ ] Connect to a 5apps account → confirm stats round-trip across devices.
- [ ] Confirm `updatedAt`-wins resolves a deliberate conflict correctly.
- [ ] Disconnect → confirm local data remains intact.
- [ ] Test against Dropbox + Google Drive backends.

author: sebastienrousseau
body:
## Summary

The `Release` workflow's validate step on the v0.0.1 tag run failed
with:

```
Tag version (0.0.1) does not match Cargo.toml version ()
```

Root cause: workspace root `Cargo.toml` has no top-level
`version` field (it's a `[workspace]`-only manifest), so the
extraction `grep '^version' Cargo.toml | head -1 | sed …`
produced an empty CARGO_VERSION.

## Fix

- Read the canonical version from `crates/noyalib/Cargo.toml`
  instead of the workspace root.
- Add a lockstep cross-check across the 4 publishable satellite
  crates (`noya-cli`, `noyalib-mcp`, `noyalib-lsp`, `noyalib-wasm`)
  so a partial `cargo workspaces version` bump that forgets one
  crate fails the release before the partial publish lands.

## Post-merge

- Re-tag `v0.0.1` from the new `main` HEAD (the existing tag
  pointed at `fa3342c` which lacks this fix).
- Push the new tag — `release.yml` fires again with the corrected
  validate step.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR.
- [ ] After merge, re-tag and confirm the `Validate` step prints
      "Version verified across noyalib + 4 satellites: 0.0.1".

author: bokelley
body:
Closes #612

## Summary

`create_agent_card_routes()` (a2a-sdk) registers exactly one route: `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. The 0.3 discovery alias `/.well-known/agent.json` was already present in `_A2A_DISCOVERY_PATHS` (auth middleware exempted it) but was never registered as a Starlette route — returning 404 or 503 at edge proxies. This broke `@adcp/sdk` CLI auto-detection of A2A transport, which probes the alias as a positive A2A signal.

**Fix:** Call `create_agent_card_routes(agent_card=agent_card, card_url="/.well-known/agent.json")` a second time in `create_a2a_server()`. Both paths serve identical agent-card JSON using independent handler closures — no redirect round-trip, no shared mutable state.

**Also fixed:**
- Three tests that masked the bug by accepting 404 as valid (`test_unified_mcp_a2a.py`) or asserting only the canonical path (`test_a2a_server.py`)
- New inverse coverage test (`test_all_discovery_paths_are_registered_routes`) asserting every path in `_A2A_DISCOVERY_PATHS` has a live Starlette route — this is the structural check that would have caught issue #612 at the point `/.well-known/agent.json` was added to the frozenset
- Misleading comment in `auth.py` ("retained by enable_v0_3_compat=True") corrected to note the route is registered explicitly in `create_a2a_server`
- `A2ABearerAuthMiddleware` docstring updated to mention both exempted paths
- `docs/handler-authoring.md` corrected to name the canonical path (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`) with a parenthetical noting the 0.3 alias

**Nits (not fixed in this PR):**
- `test_a2a_server.py:349` uses `startswith("/.well-known/agent-card")` — could use `AGENT_CARD_WELL_KNOWN_PATH` constant for exactness

## What was tested

```
ruff check src/           # All checks passed
pytest tests/test_a2a_server.py tests/test_unified_mcp_a2a.py tests/test_serve_auth_both.py -v
# 80 passed, 0 failed, 43 warnings
```

## Pre-PR review

- **code-reviewer:** approved — no blockers. Core fix is correct (`create_agent_card_routes` creates fresh independent closures per call; no shared state). Two issues addressed (auth docstring, test limitation comment). Noted that `test_unified_mcp_a2a.py` tightening from `in (200, 404)` → `== 200` is the right move.
- **ad-tech-protocol-expert:** approved — no blockers. `/.well-known/agent.json` is confirmed as the intended 0.3 alias (already in `_A2A_DISCOVERY_PATHS` with intentional auth exemption). No canonicalization concern (neither well-known path appears in the serialized card body). Absence of `Link: rel=canonical` on alias response is consistent with all other A2A implementations and not required by the spec.

body:
## Summary

Sprint 1.2 first slice. Adds the auth-bypassed read-only surface a non-authenticated visitor needs to view a published Cocarte map.

Closes imagodata/gispulse-portal#59 (backend half).

## ⚠️ Stacked PR

Base: \`cocarte/issue-56-map-entity-backend\` (PR #168). This PR contains ONLY the public-viewer slice. After #168 merges to main, retarget this PR via the GitHub UI (\`gh pr edit 169 --base main\`) — the diff will then show only the 3 files added here.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | \`/c/{slug}\` | none | Public maps only. Private and unlisted return 404 (no existence leak). |
| GET | \`/c/by-token/{token}\` | none | Unlisted maps via opaque share token. Constant-time lookup via \`hmac.compare_digest\`. Token length-bounded at 200 chars. |
| GET | \`/c/health\` | none | Liveness probe. |

## Sanitisation

\`MapPublic\` projection drops \`owner_id\` and \`share_token\` from responses. Includes \`published_at\` / \`created_at\` / \`updated_at\` so the SPA can render "published on" / "last updated" labels.

**404 (not 403)** on unauthorised access — response shape identical to "not found", preventing token / slug enumeration.

## Mounting

Router mounted in BOTH portal and full mode, after \`examples_router\` and BEFORE the auth-protected stack. Same pattern as the public examples surface.

## Tests (12 passing)

- public 200 + sanitised payload
- private 404
- unlisted 404 via slug (must use \`/c/by-token/\`)
- unknown slug 404
- trashed public 404
- valid token 200
- invalid / empty / oversized token 404
- private map (no token) cannot be reached via guess
- token cleared on visibility revert to private → old token now 404

## Out of scope

- Snapshot pipeline (DuckDB → S3) — separate Sprint 1.2 PR
- 3 dataviz presets (choropleth / bubble / heatmap) — separate Sprint 1.2 PR
- Frontend public viewer page (React route + map render) — separate Sprint 1.2 PR
- Permalink hash state (z/lat/lng) — issue #60, separate PR

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Reviewer confirms 404-on-unauthorised semantics (no 403, no leak)
- [ ] Reviewer confirms token length cap at 200 is reasonable

author: arthurbrussee
body:
- Loading a COLMAP dataset where `cameras.txt` contained malformed cameras (e.g. params written as `-nan(ind)` by Windows/MSVC exporters) failed with the singularly unhelpful chain `Failed to load format. → IO error while loading dataset. → Parse error`. Now `parse_float` accepts MSVC-style NaN spellings (`-nan(ind)`, `nan(snan)`, etc.) so those cameras parse as NaN and the existing `Camera::is_valid()` check at [colmap.rs:121](https://github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush/blob/main/crates/brush-dataset/src/formats/colmap.rs#L121) skips the affected images with a warning instead of aborting the whole load.
- `cameras.txt` parse errors now include the line number, camera id, the offending value, and the underlying `ParseFloatError` / `ParseIntError`.
- `FormatError` no longer swallows the inner `io::Error` in its `Display`, and `DatasetError::FormatError` is `#[error(transparent)]` so the egui `ErrorDisplay` headline and CLI `anyhow` chain show the real message.

## Summary

- Internal port: still **2001**.
- Caddy reverse-proxy semantics: still \`localhost:2001\` → \`:443\`.
- The \`trial.realstory.blog\` references in QUICKSTART (separate hosted Plane+Mattermost service, distinct from the trial-app demo).

## Operator follow-up (after merge)

1. Update DNS A/AAAA records for \`mmplane-trial.realstory.blog\` to point at the deployment host (so Caddy's first ACME challenge succeeds).
2. Pull latest agents-pool: \`cd ~/agents-pool && git pull\`.
3. Re-rsync to deployment dir: \`rsync -a --delete --exclude=node_modules --exclude=.next --exclude=.env ~/agents-pool/trial-app/ /work/genasis-trial/\`.

5. \`sudo systemctl reload caddy.service\`.

The old \`genasis-trial.realstory.blog\` Caddy block is gone, so Caddy will only respond to the new hostname after reload. Old DNS records can be deleted at the operator's leisure.

## Summary
- Adds `scripts/run_mtp_sidecar_loader_probe_spark.sh` to run both the Python MTP sidecar contract probe and the llama.cpp-side probe (gated) against an already-staged sidecar on Spark.
- Documents the combined runner in `docs/baseline-runtime.md`, `docs/llamacpp-mtp-sidecar-load.md`, and `docs/quantized-performance-path.md`.

## Verification
- `sh -n scripts/run_mtp_sidecar_loader_probe_spark.sh`
- `git diff --check`

## Spark commands run
- None (script-only change).

## Current MTP loader status
- Repo-side/Spark-side Python contract probe validates `general.architecture=deepseek4_mtp_support` and the expected 32 `mtp.0.*` tensors; supports per-tensor payload sampling via `--payload-sample-bytes`.
- llama.cpp-side probe patch can validate the sidecar file and optionally load the sidecar tensor blob into RAM via `LOAD_WEIGHTS=1`, but Spark/CUDA llama.cpp forks still lack a reusable `deepseek4_mtp_sidecar` binder and MTP forward/kv/rollback semantics.

## Remaining correctness/performance risks
- No runtime binder yet: sidecar weights are not bound into an MTP draft layer in the Spark/CUDA fork.
- `LOAD_WEIGHTS=1` can increase host RAM usage (still far smaller than trunk); keep it optional.
- Runner reports record `REMOTE_*` env strings; do not include secrets.

## Next experiment
- Stage the sidecar on Spark0 and run `scripts/run_mtp_sidecar_loader_probe_spark.sh` with `LOAD_WEIGHTS=1` to confirm a full sidecar load succeeds and `ok=true` with `missing=[]`/`extra=[]`.
- Then implement Step 1 in `docs/llamacpp-mtp-sidecar-load.md`: a reusable `deepseek4_mtp_sidecar` 32-tensor binder in the Spark/CUDA llama.cpp fork, and proceed to the gamma=1 one-token draft probe gate (`docs/mtp-one-token-draft-probe.md`).

author: kodflow
body:
## Failure pattern

After PR #57's keyring refresh, the Arch DEV snapshot rebuild progressed past pacman init but failed at Rust install with:

```
curl: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libcurl.so.4: undefined symbol: ngtcp2_crypto_get_path_challenge_data2_cb
```

Classic Arch partial-upgrade trap. `pacman -S --needed curl` upgrades the curl binary but leaves its transitive runtime deps (ngtcp2, nghttp2, libnghttp2, libssh2…) at the older versions baked into the BASE snapshot — so the freshly-installed curl can't resolve symbols at load time.

## Fix

Run a full `pacman -Syu` after the keyring refresh and before the targeted dev-tool install. This is the canonical Arch recipe — partial upgrades are explicitly unsupported.

`--ignore linux,linux-headers,linux-lts` keeps the running kernel + modules consistent: a kernel upgrade right before a snapshot would orphan the running kernel's modules until the next boot.

## Validated

Live on Proxmox: arch-systemd VM 202 hit the symbol-lookup error before the fix; will retry with the patched script after this lands.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## What
Added a full system upgrade step (`pacman -Syu --ignore linux,linux-headers,linux-lts`) between keyring refresh and targeted dev tool installation in the Arch/Artix VM snapshot build process.

## Why
After PR #57 refreshed `archlinux-keyring`, partial package updates caused symbol lookup errors at runtime: installing `curl` alone upgraded the binary but left transitive runtime dependencies (ngtcp2, nghttp2, libssh2) at older versions from the BASE snapshot. This is the classic Arch "partial-upgrade trap"—the canonical fix is a full `-Syu` after keyring refresh. The symbol error occurred on Proxmox-hosted Arch VMs and blocked the DEV snapshot rebuild.

## How
Modified the `install_dev_tools` function's `pacman)` branch to:
1. Attempt keyring refresh (best-effort, non-blocking via `|| true`)
2. Run full `-Syu` with `--ignore linux,linux-headers,linux-lts` to resolve all transitive dependencies while preserving kernel/module consistency
3. Follow with targeted `-S` installs for dev tools

The kernel exclusion is intentional: upgrading the kernel before snapshot would leave new modules orphaned on the running system (used for snapshot creation); skipping the kernel keeps the running system self-consistent and the snapshot bootable on first boot without requiring a reboot.

## Risk
**Low**. Changes are isolated to Arch/Artix-family VMs and align with Arch's own documentation for resolving partial-upgrade issues. The `--ignore` flag preserves system stability during the snapshot run. Error handling remains permissive (`|| true` on retries) to tolerate stale mirrors.

author: certik
body:
Step 1 of "native LLVM->WASM": exercise our native MLIR->LLVM IR translator on the wasm test path while still using LLVM's WebAssembly TargetMachine for the actual wasm emit. Step 2 (replacing the LLVM backend with our own) will follow.

## Wiring

`MLIR_TranslateModuleToWasm` now mirrors `MLIR_TranslateModuleToLLVMIR`:

- `MLIR_LOWERING_UPSTREAM` (unchanged): `mlir::translateModuleToLLVMIR` → wasm.
- `MLIR_LOWERING_NATIVE` (new): `mlir_translate_to_llvm_ir_native` → `llvm::parseAssemblyString` → wasm.

## Bug fix in the native LLVM IR translator

Indirect `llvm.call` ops carry a `var_callee_type` attribute regardless of whether the callee is actually variadic. `emit_call` was always emitting the variadic form `<ret> (<args>, ...)` — fine on x86_64 ABI, but on wasm32 it produces a signature mismatch (variadic and fixed-arity have different ABIs). Now we check `MLIR_GetTypeFunctionIsVarArg` (newly exposed in `mlir_api.h`) and only emit `, ...` when the callee actually is variadic.

This was the root cause of the 6 fnptr_* test failures (`fnptr_basic`, `fnptr_arg`, `fnptr_typedef`, `ptr_to_fnptr`, `fnptr_struct_return`, `fnptr_i64_return`).

## CI

Adds `TINYC_LOWERING=native pixi run -e upstream test_tinyc_upstream_wasm` to all three platforms.

## Verified locally (macOS)

| Task | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_tinyc_upstream_wasm` (upstream lowering) | 150 pass, 11 skip |
| `TINYC_LOWERING=native test_tinyc_upstream_wasm` | **150 pass, 11 skip** |

body:
## Wave 49 Bucket B — kc-teacher production Next.js port

Closes 1/3 KC personas of Phase 4 Track 2 (GAP-268) — production port of the
`kiteclass-teacher` Round 2 HTML kit (24 screens, 5 surfaces).

### Route consolidation decision (R2 risk in Wave 49 plan §1 Q3)

Plan §3 Bucket B AC required the agent to pick between `(dashboard)/teacher/*`
vs `(teacher)/*`. Picked **`(teacher)/teacher/*`** as canonical because:

1. The pre-existing `(teacher)/attendance/period/[classId]/[periodNo]/[date]`
   route from Wave 18b2 already established the `(teacher)/*` route group
   (mobile-first, GVCN-scoped). Keeping it canonical avoids splitting
   teacher routes across two route groups.
2. `(dashboard)/teacher/dashboard` (PR 3.8.1) was a single-page bridge — only
   one consumer to migrate.
3. Next.js route-group parens do NOT contribute URL segments. So a literal
   `teacher/` folder is needed inside the group to namespace paths under
   `/teacher/...` without colliding with `(dashboard)/attendance` (which
   resolves to `/attendance`), `/dashboard`, or `(public)/page` (which
   resolves to `/`). Hence the `(teacher)/teacher/...` shape.

**Migration map:**
| Was | Becomes |
|-----|---------|
| `(dashboard)/teacher/dashboard/page.tsx` | DELETED — content folded into `(teacher)/teacher/dashboard/page.tsx` |
| `(teacher)/attendance/period/[classId]/[periodNo]/[date]/page.tsx` | UNCHANGED (Wave 18b2 per-tiết route, live `attendancePeriodApi`) |
| (none) | NEW `(teacher)/teacher/{dashboard,attendance,grades,schedule,reports,settings}/...` |

The legacy URL `/teacher/dashboard` is preserved through the new
`(teacher)/teacher/dashboard/page.tsx`, so existing `Link href="/teacher/dashboard"`
sites stay valid.

### What ships (11 production routes — `pnpm build` PASS)

- `/teacher` → redirects to `/teacher/dashboard`
- `/teacher/dashboard` — Today + 4-stat grid + class queue with current period
- `/teacher/attendance` — class list for today
- `/teacher/attendance/[classId]` — wraps **G2 AttendanceRoster** (handles 7
  prototype states natively: default / marking / saving / saved / error /
  empty / loading)
- `/teacher/grades` — class list for grade entry
- `/teacher/grades/[classId]` — wraps **G3 GradebookEntryGrid** + VN 10pt
  validation (`validateGrade`) + finalize-confirm flow
- `/teacher/schedule` — wraps **G4 ClassScheduleManager** + conflict
  detection (`detectConflicts`)
- `/teacher/reports` — multi-class analytics (avg / chuyên cần / xuất sắc)
- `/teacher/reports/[classId]` — MoET-format report card per Thông tư
  22/2021/TT-BGDĐT (Xuất sắc / Giỏi / Khá / TB / Yếu)
- `/teacher/settings` — profile + preferences
- `/teacher/settings/payroll` — monthly payroll breakdown (VND)

### Components consumed from `@kite/shared-ui` (no inline copies)

Verified via `grep '@kite/shared-ui'` in `src/app/(teacher)`:
- G2 `AttendanceRoster` ✓
- G3 `GradebookEntryGrid` + `validateGrade` ✓
- G4 `ClassScheduleManager` + `detectConflicts` ✓
- G8 `AttendanceCalendar` surfaced via existing `(teacher)/attendance/period`
  route (Wave 18b2 — preserved)

### Tests + verification

- `pnpm -F kiteclass-frontend test --run` → **705 PASS / 0 FAIL** (4 new
  smoke tests in `teacher-shell.test.tsx`)
- `pnpm -F kiteclass-frontend build` → **green**, 11 teacher routes built
  (5.68 KB / 4.96 KB / 5.65 KB / 4.78 KB / 3.73 KB / 5.34 KB / 2.94 KB /
  2.59 KB / 4.26 KB / 2.5 KB / 149 B)

### Gap status — 🟡 PARTIAL per `gap-done-discipline.md` §3

3 ACs cleanly DONE, 4 deferred to follow-up gaps tracked in `GAP-268.md` Log:

| AC | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| G2/G3/G4/G8 from shared lib | ✅ | grep verified, zero inline copies |
| VN 10pt validation | ✅ | G3 native `validateGrade` |
| Recurring schedule + conflict detection | ✅ | G4 native `detectConflicts` |
| MoET report card output | ✅ | Thông tư 22/2021/TT-BGDĐT classification |

author: logannye
body:
## Summary

The free-signup E2E check at `scripts/monitoring/api_health_audit.sh:441` labeled every non-200 response on the new-tenant `/usage` call as "did not authenticate". That became misleading after PR #15 (DB-backed auth fallback) shipped: a freshly-minted key can now hit the per-tenant rate limiter and return 429 — and a 429 means the request *cleared* authentication and was throttled at the rate-limit layer, not a real auth-path failure.

Three branches now:

- `200`: PASS (unchanged)
- `429`: FAIL with copy `"rate-limited; auth path resolved the key"` and the failure summary tagged `(rate-limited, not auth failure)` so the operator doesn't go investigate the wrong layer
- everything else: FAIL with the actual status code in the message — `"returned $usage_code, expected 200"`

## Why now

Hit during the 2026-05-10 deploy of PRs #15+#16. The manual + launchd back-to-back invocations produced 429s that misreported as auth failures — almost masking the fact that the deploy *did* work (401→429 transition was the actual proof of the fix). Future-me would have wasted time staring at the auth code chasing a phantom 401.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n scripts/monitoring/api_health_audit.sh` (syntax valid)
- [ ] Next 06:00 daily run produces a clean message — either `PASS 200 ... authenticates` (expected steady state) or, if rate-limit pressure recurs, `FAIL 429 ... rate-limited; auth path resolved the key`.

## Not changing

- The `test_api` helper at the top of the script already includes `$code` in its generic FAIL message, so the long-lived audit-key `/usage` call (Section 4) was never affected — only this dedicated free-signup path.
- The pass/fail threshold (still requires 200 to PASS).

author: maples7
body:
Closes #68.

## What

Adds an opt-in `--erase-clone` flag to `vch build`, `vch test`, and `vch run` that
runs `simctl shutdown && simctl erase` on the per-task simulator clone *before*
the build / test / install step.

## Why

A per-task simulator clone (`xcrun simctl clone`) inherits the **entire `~/Library`**
of the warm template — including `UserDefaults`, keychain entries, and app
containers written by previous runs. That's exactly what the warm-template fast
path (#47/#58) needs: the priming work survives.

But it occasionally bites when a test depends on first-launch behaviour, e.g.
the BeanLedger reporter's case:

```
✗ CloudSyncStatusCenterGraceTests.firstLaunchAlertFiresAfterGraceEnds()
   → expected alert flag to be unset, was true
```

…because the template was used interactively and wrote `UserDefaults` keys that
the clone now also has. Until now, the workaround was a manual
`xcrun simctl shutdown <udid> && xcrun simctl erase <udid>` invocation (and you
first had to look up the UDID).

## How

Both `BuildOrTest.execute` (shared by `BuildCommand` and `TestCommand`) and
`RunCommand.execute` gained an `eraseClone: Bool = false` parameter. When set,
they emit `→ erasing simulator '<name>' (--erase-clone)` and call the existing
`SimulatorService.eraseClone(udid:)` (already covered by
`testEraseChainsShutdownThenErase`) before the bootSimulator step. Then control
flows back into the normal boot → install → build/test/run path.

## Off by default — and why

Per hard rule #9, vch never auto-shuts-down or auto-wipes shared resources.
`--erase-clone` is an explicit opt-in: ~10–20 s overhead per invocation, so
keeping it off the default path matters for the warm-template savings to
actually materialise. The companion cookbook recipe
("Resetting per-task simulator state") explains:

1. why the inheritance is intentional (#47/#58 — feature, not bug);
2. when to reach for `--erase-clone` (first-launch test failures from
   leftover `UserDefaults` etc.);
3. the long-term fix if you find yourself needing it constantly:
   keep a development-only template separate from the warm template,
   and treat the warm template as immutable
   (only `vch sim warm-template create` / `remove` should ever touch it).

## Tests

`SimulatorService.eraseClone` is already covered by
`testEraseChainsShutdownThenErase` (Tests/VibeChardCoreTests/Services/
SimulatorServiceTests.swift), which asserts the `simctl shutdown` →
`simctl erase` chain. The new flag is a thin pass-through to that
service method, so no additional unit test was added — the integration
is observable via the `→ erasing simulator …` stderr line that's
covered by manual / dogfood validation.

`swift test --parallel` → 496/496 pass.

## Docs

- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased] ### Added` entry.
- All 5 README locales: updated `vch build` / `vch test` / `vch run`
  table rows + new "Resetting per-task simulator state" cookbook recipe
  immediately after the warm-template section, so the trade-off is
  discoverable from the same place users learn about warm templates.
