author: ng
body:
## Summary
Post-#532 follow-up. Real-pod testing surfaced three places PR #532 shelled out to CLI tools that aren't on the Yocto-based pod image (ADR 0013), plus a couple of related plumbing fixes:

### 1. `sqlite3` binary doesn't exist on the pod
Only `better-sqlite3` (Node addon) does. Both `app/api/export/archive/route.ts::dumpSqlite` and `modules/archive-push/sleepypod-archive-push` shelled out to a `sqlite3` CLI that never installed. Result: the export route 500'd `spawn sqlite3 ENOENT` on every click that included `db`; the nightly push silently dropped the db side.

- Route: replaced with `Database(path, {readonly:true}).backup(outPath)` — the SQLite Online Backup API via better-sqlite3, the same library next-server already opens the live db with. Tarball now contains `biometrics.db` (binary) instead of `biometrics.sql`; restore is a literal file copy.
- Timer: invokes `node -e ...` from the app dir with the same library.

### 2. `rsync` binary doesn't exist on the pod either
ADR 0013 documents this — Yocto kirkstone ships without rsync and there's no package manager to add it. The deploy script already uses `tar | ssh` for the same reason.

Replaced both raw and db push paths with `scp + ssh`. ssh ControlMaster multiplexes per-file scps over one TCP handshake. The cold archive is append-only (one new \`*.RAW.gz\` per day), so a list-remote-then-scp-missing loop has the same steady-state cost as \`rsync -az\`. Uploads land on \`.part\` and are renamed atomically so an interrupted transfer doesn't leave a half-file the next run mistakes for complete.

### 3. Pin timer to `/usr/local/bin/node`
\`/usr/bin/node\` on the pod is v16 (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 93); next-server runs the newer v22 binary that better-sqlite3 was built against. The timer's PATH picked up v16 and failed with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED on the native addon. Env-overridable via \`SLEEPYPOD_NODE_BIN\`.

### 4. `ProtectSystem=strict` blocked the staging dir
Service unit only had \`/etc/sleepypod\` writable. Added \`/persistent/sleepypod-data\` (same dir the live db already writes to) so the backup-then-gzip pipeline works. Route's staging dir also moves to \`/persistent/sleepypod-data/export-staging\` — \`/tmp\` is a 984 MB tmpfs (RAM-pressured), \`/persistent\` has ~10 GB free.

## Verified on pod 192.168.1.88
- \`GET /api/export/archive?include=raw,db\` → 22 MB tarball, valid binary \`biometrics.db\` (\`file\` reports SQLite 3.x, 6284 pages; reopens cleanly).
- Loopback E2E push (pod → 127.0.0.1:8822):
  - Run #1 (cold sync): 768 \`*.RAW.gz\` + 1 db transferred in ~9 s via one multiplexed ssh session. Zero \`.part\` leftovers.
  - Run #2 (incremental): all 768 raw files skipped via remote-listing diff; fresh db pushed.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm tsc\`, \`pnpm lint\`, \`pnpm test run app/api/export/archive\` clean.
- [x] Pod smoke: \`/api/export/archive?include=raw,db\` returns valid binary db.
- [x] Pod E2E loopback: full + incremental nightly push succeeds, atomic rename works.

author: felixgeelhaar
body:
## Summary

Fixes downstream failure where OpenAI strict tool-calling rejects MCP tool schemas advertised by mcp-go for any handler whose input is \`struct{}\`:

\`\`\`
400 Invalid schema for function 'mnemos__knowledge_metrics':
In context=(), object schema missing properties. (format)
\`\`\`

### Root cause

\`schema.Schema.Properties\` had \`json:\"properties,omitempty\"\`, so a zero-arg handler serialized as \`{\"type\":\"object\"}\` — properties key missing entirely. OpenAI strict mode rejects.

### Fix

- Custom \`MarshalJSON\` on \`Schema\`: for \`type:object\`, always emits \`properties\` (\`{}\` when empty) and writes \`additionalProperties\` when set.
- \`generateStructSchema\` now sets \`AdditionalProperties: false\` so struct-derived schemas are closed objects → satisfies OpenAI strict mode end-to-end.
- Map-derived schemas keep \`AdditionalProperties\` unset → stay open (correct for \`map[string]Foo\`).

### Reported by

User running \`mnemos\` 0.6.1 + OpenClaw 2026.5.7 gateway + OpenAI gpt-4o. Their entire tool list was rejected per request, blocking any agent turn that listed a zero-arg tool. They patched locally by adding a fake input; this fixes the bug at the schema-generator layer so every mcp-go consumer is protected.

## Base branch

Stacks on top of #77 (string-constant cleanup) so the pre-commit lint baseline is clean. Rebase to main after #77 merges.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression tests in \`schema/schema_test.go\`:
  - empty struct → \`properties: {}\` + \`additionalProperties: false\`
  - populated struct → \`additionalProperties: false\`
  - non-object schema → no spurious properties / additionalProperties leak
- [x] \`go test -race -count=1 ./...\` all packages green
- [x] Verified against \`mnemos\` (downstream consumer, full \`./...\` race suite) via temporary \`replace\` directive — all packages pass.
- [x] Pre-commit hook clean (lint + vet + build + race tests)

author: jkrumbiegel
body: ## Summary Closes #5270. Adds better automatic ticks for `pseudolog10` and `Symlog10`. Previously the `Automatic` dispatch fell through to `WilkinsonTicks` on raw data values, picking linearly-spaced data points which then squash together at the high end of a log-shaped axis — leaving most of the visible space without tick markings. The PR also: - Replaces the broken `LogTicks` + `pseudolog10` path introduced by #5135 (the off-by-one bug in #5270) with an informative `ArgumentError`. - Refactors `Symlog10` from `ReversibleScale` into a callable struct so the `lower`/`upper`/`linscale` parameters are accessible from the tick code. - Adds two new tick types `PseudologTicks(n_ideal = 5)` and `SymlogTicks(n_ideal = 5)`. ## Example ```julia fig = Figure(size = (700, 500)) cases = [ ("ylims = [-100, 100]", -100:0.1:100), ("ylims = [0, 100,000]", 0:1.0:1e5), ("ylims = [-1,000, 1,000]", -1000:1.0:1000), ("ylims = [10, 1,000,000]", 10:1.0:1e6), ] for (i, (title, data)) in enumerate(cases) row, col = fldmod1(i, 2) lines(fig[row, col], collect(data); axis = (; yscale = Makie.pseudolog10, title = title)) end fig ``` **Before** **After** ## Algorithm For each side of zero, find the largest visible decade exponent `kmax_*`. Pick a stride `s` along the |k| axis (so ticks are at `±10⁰, ±10ˢ, ±10²ˢ, …`) by enumerating candidates and choosing the one whose tick count is closest to `n_ideal`, tiebreaking on reach (closer to the data extreme), then density. `s ≥ kmin_*` keeps every tick out of the linear region (`Symlog10`) or the pile-up zone near zero (`pseudolog10`). Falls back to `WilkinsonTicks` on raw data when no two decades fit the window.

author: whalermike
body:
## Summary

Direct continuation of [#353](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/pull/353). Closes the remaining "medium" CLI gap identified in the prior assessment by adding three verb groups under `uiao orgtree`:

```
uiao orgtree show codebook       <code>      # Codebook entry (UIAO_151)
uiao orgtree show dynamic-group  <name>      # DynamicGroupSpec (UIAO_152)
uiao orgtree show admin-unit     <name>      # AdministrativeUnit (UIAO_154)
uiao orgtree show device-plane   <name>      # DevicePlane (UIAO_153)

uiao orgtree resolve dynamic-group <name>    # rule + per-ref codebook lookup

uiao orgtree export codebook [--out PATH]    # JSON consumed by UIAO_159's
                                             # Get-OrgTreeValidationReport
```

Each verb is a thin wrapper over the existing `load_*` functions in `uiao.modernization.orgtree`. `show` / `resolve` render via Rich Table; not-found prints a `NOT FOUND` line listing up to five known keys and exits 1. `export` writes JSON in the exact shape `Get-OrgTreeValidationReport -CodebookPath` consumes (UIAO_159 §F3), removing the need for admins to hand-craft that file.

## Why this matters

`#353` shipped UIAO_159's PowerShell module but punted on how the JSON codebook reaches it: the README example said *"export the canonical codebook from YAML to JSON yourself"* with no actual command. This PR closes that loop:

```bash
uiao orgtree export codebook --out ./codebook.json
pwsh -c "Get-OrgTreeValidationReport -TenantId \$env:TENANT_ID -CodebookPath ./codebook.json"
```

Same theme on `show` and `resolve` — admins doing tenant-side work shouldn't need to read raw YAML to answer "what does dynamic group X target?" or "what's in the codebook entry for ORG-FIN-AP?".

## Tests

`tests/test_cli_orgtree.py` grew from 15 to **28** cases:

- `show` × 4 kinds × 2 paths (happy + not-found) = 8
- `resolve dynamic-group` × 2 paths (happy + not-found) = 2
- `export codebook` × 3 (stdout, `--out` file, regex round-trip) = 3

All 28 pass locally; broader regression suite (171 cases across the touched modules) also passes.

## Doc updates

- **UIAO_159** — Surface 1 section reorganized into the four verb groups; added a concrete bash + pwsh snippet showing the new `export codebook` feeding `Get-OrgTreeValidationReport`; `updated_at` bumped.
- **`tools/powershell/OrgTreeValidation/README.md`** — tenant-audit example now actually shows where `codebook.json` comes from.

## Verification

- [x] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` → clean
- [x] 171 pytest cases pass (28 new + 143 regression)
- [x] `python3 scripts/validate_canon_frontmatter.py` → exit 0
- [x] `uiao substrate drift` → PASS with 25 P2 advisories (one new advisory present on `main` independent of this PR; substrate-walker cleanup is the next thread on the punch list)
- [x] lychee on touched `.md` files → 0 errors

## Test plan (CI + reviewer)

- [ ] All CI lanes green (ruff, mypy, pytest, frontmatter, schemas, substrate, links, Pester, render).
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the `show` surface scope (4 dict-keyed kinds) is the right cut. Tuple-shaped artifacts (`role_assignments`, `intune_assignments`) don't have a natural single-id lookup; a future `list` verb would surface them.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms `resolve dynamic-group <name>` scope is correct. The richer "resolve against a tenant snapshot" version was deliberately deferred — that needs a snapshot-format spec that doesn't exist yet.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the export-codebook JSON shape works for the pwsh consumer. The schema is asserted by `test_export_codebook_to_stdout`: `entries` is a list, each entry has `code`/`level`/`description`. (Functions 3-5 of UIAO_159 require a real tenant; not exercised by Pester or pytest.)

## What's NOT in this PR

- No `uiao orgtree list <kind>` verb. Useful follow-on, not blocking.
- No `export` for non-codebook artifacts. Codebook is the only one the pwsh module currently consumes; the others can ship when there's a consumer.
- No tenant-snapshot resolve mode. Would let `resolve dynamic-group` evaluate against actual user attributes, not just the codebook integrity check. Needs a snapshot-format ADR.

## Position in the punch list

Per the "what's next" thread: this is **thread 1 of 3**. Next up: substrate-walker P2 cleanup (silence the 25 advisories so any new finding is actionable), then mod-slug-redirects window pre-emption.

body:
Fixes an issue where `node-agent/install.sh` does not restart the spouet-agent service if it's already running. This led to situations where users would run the install script to update the agent or token, but the running agent would not pick up the new configuration, resulting in `401 Invalid token` errors because it was still using the old token in memory.

By adding `systemctl restart spouet-agent`, we ensure that running the script properly reloads the service and its environment variables.

body:
## Summary

- New endpoint per the [2026-05-09 cross-cache-identity pivot](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/pull/800). LML composes per-source provenance via §3.4.1.1 Rules 2–6 and returns one verdict per input (`kind: single_artist | compilation | unresolved`).
- Contract is locked at `wxyc-shared/api.yaml` v1.2.0 (merged in [WXYC/wxyc-shared#104](https://github.com/WXYC/wxyc-shared/pull/104)). This PR ships the seven `BulkResolve*` Pydantic models (regenerated via `scripts/generate_api_models.sh`), the FastAPI handler, the composition logic in `identity/bulk_resolve.py`, and the `EntityStore.get_latest_provenance_by_source()` reader needed for honest method/confidence at compose time.
- Unblocks WXYC/library-metadata-lookup#271 (V/A track resolution) and WXYC/Backend-Service#802 (Backend consumer).

## Decisions flagged for review

1. **Cross-source agreement detector (`identity/bulk_resolve.py:175-195`)**: pragmatic proxy — `≥2 non-inherited per-source rows` rather than verifying via wikidata-cache `discogs_mapping`. Permissive direction; wire format is unchanged when the detector tightens. TODO comment points at #271 follow-up.
2. **`exact_match` 1.00 default for log-less identities (`bulk_resolve.py:60-65`)**: when `entity.identity` has populated columns but no `reconciliation_log` row, default is `exact_match` 1.00. May overstate confidence on legacy IDs; tunable in a follow-up after observing production behavior.
3. **413 vs 422 for over-cap**: codegen extracts `maxItems: 1000` as Pydantic `max_length`, which would normally produce 422. Worked around by reading raw JSON for the count check before `model_validate()` so the 413 from api.yaml wins. Spec-compliant, slightly less idiomatic.
4. **`BulkResolveProvenanceEntry.confidence` codegen quirk**: datamodel-codegen drops `nullable: true`. Sidestepped by never emitting "leg-ran-no-match" entries — empty `provenance: []` carries that meaning per api.yaml description. No hand-edit of generated code.

body: This PR introduces SketchFlow AI, a local-first vector whiteboard video builder with Remotion export architecture. **Tech Stack & Architecture** - Next.js 15 App Router, React, TypeScript, TailwindCSS, and Framer Motion. - Pure TypeScript engines: script parser, asset matcher, timeline, storage, audio, and export pipeline. - Local SVG/vector asset database (animals, people, education, science, business, objects, etc.) with keyword/synonym ranking. - Browser storage abstraction using localStorage metadata and IndexedDB payloads. - Remotion composition registration (`remotion/root.tsx`) for future FFmpeg MP4 rendering. **Core Features** - **Landing Page**: Positions the app as "Canva + Whiteboard + Automated Builder" with no cloud GPU/diffusion AI badges. - **Dashboard**: Displays local projects, stats (total scenes, estimated minutes), and create video CTA. - **Template Gallery**: Four typed templates (Classic Whiteboard, Chalkboard Explainer, Modern Canvas, Shorts Vertical) with configurable styles. - Bottom: Visual timeline sequencing. - **Export Screen**: Simulates browser render progress (Prepare -> Composition -> FFmpeg -> MP4) and exposes Remotion render plan JSON. **Implementation Details** - body:
## Summary

Resolves #71 — *Support local development without a repo or remote*.

`url` is now optional on profile repository entries. When omitted, raid treats the entry as local-only:

- skips cloning entirely (so `raid install` no longer fatal-errors trying to `git clone ""` against a remote that doesn't exist)
- runs install tasks against the existing path as-is
- requires the path to already exist on disk; if it doesn't, returns a clear error pointing at the path
- `raid doctor` no longer flags a missing `.git` as a warning for local-only repos, and upgrades a missing path to error severity for them

The `Repo.IsZero()` definition was tightened to drop the URL check (it was the only thing keeping local-only repos out of the loaded profile). A new `Repo.IsLocalOnly()` exposes the missing-url state explicitly.

- `schemas/raid-profile.schema.json` — `url` removed from `required`; description notes the local-only mode.

- `src/internal/lib/doctor.go` — context-aware checks for local-only repos.
- `src/internal/lib/profile.go` — interactive `raid profile create` accepts an empty URL prompt; default-branch detection skipped when URL is empty.

Primary: Rounce et al. 2023, *Science*, doi:10.1126/science.abo1324 / NSIDC doi:10.5067/H118TCMSUH3Q  
Fallback used: OGGM v1.6.1 standard CMIP6 projections (public, no auth). NSIDC PyGEM requires NASA Earthdata Login. Set `EARTHDATA_TOKEN` env var and re-run `npm run transform:water-cycle-rounce` for the primary source.

author: chaudoan21165
body:
## Summary

The frontend overlay shipped in #363 + #364 didn't fire in production — the anon-keyed read of `user_subscriptions` was hitting an RLS edge that's hard to reproduce from outside the request (suspected role/AAL conflict). Moving the bridge into `me-entitlement` with the service-role admin client bypasses RLS entirely and is the correct layer for this.

After `normalizeEntitlement(subscriptions ?? [])` returns `is_premium: false`, the function now does one additional `adminClient` query against `user_subscriptions` for an active, non-expired gift redemption. If found, the response becomes:
```json
{
  \"is_premium\": true,
  \"source\": \"gift_code\",
  \"status\": \"active\",
  \"expires_at\": \"<current_period_end>\"
}
```
Stripe paths short-circuit before the fallback (existing branch when `subscriptions` rows yield premium), so they're unaffected.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `supabase/functions/me-entitlement/index.ts` | +62 / −2. Adds `fetchActiveGiftSubscription` helper using `adminClient`, wires it into the handler between `normalizeEntitlement` and `computeTrialStatus`. Extends `CanonicalSource` with `\"gift_code\"`. |

## Identification rule

```sql
SELECT current_period_end FROM user_subscriptions
WHERE user_id = $1
  AND status = 'active'
  AND is_gift_redemption = true
  AND current_period_end > now()
ORDER BY current_period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
```

The redeem RPC always populates `current_period_end` (either +days or +100 years for lifetime), so dropping null-tolerance is safe.

## Frontend overlay status (#363 + #364)

Stays in place as defense-in-depth. Once this PR deploys, the overlay becomes a no-op:
- Backend reports `is_premium: true` for gift users → frontend's `!backendEnt.is_premium` short-circuits → overlay doesn't run.
- For Stripe users, backend still returns premium → same short-circuit.
- The overlay only fires if the backend reports non-premium AND a frontend-visible gift sub exists. With this PR, that combination shouldn't occur.

Removing the overlay for cleanliness can happen in a follow-up PR — kept here as insurance during the function-deploy / Vercel-deploy ordering window.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` — pass
- `npm run lint` — pass
- `npm test` — **5,682 / 5,682** across 284 files (unchanged; `me-entitlement` is a Deno Edge Function with no vitest harness today)
- `npm run build` — pass

## Test plan after merge (Chau)

1. **Deploy the Edge Function:** `supabase functions deploy me-entitlement`. (No migration, no frontend deploy required for the fix to take effect.)
2. Log in as a non-admin test account that redeemed a gift code — trankhuctriet@yahoo.com or whoever redeemed `GIFT1Y-087814`.
3. Hit `/account`. Expected: \"Premium access\" / \"Active\" / expiry date populated.
4. Open Network tab and look at the `me-entitlement` POST response. Expected JSON:
   ```json
   { \"is_premium\": true, \"source\": \"gift_code\", \"status\": \"active\", \"expires_at\": \"...\", \"trial_expires_at\": null, \"is_trial_expired\": false }
   ```
5. Verify Stripe-paid users still show their existing premium state — `source` should still be `\"stripe\"`, `status: \"active\"`.
6. Verify non-premium users (no Stripe sub, no gift sub) still show Free — `is_premium: false`, fallback runs but returns null, response unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Edge Function vitest harness for `me-entitlement` (separate refactor — `redeem-access-code` follows the `core.ts` / `Deps` pattern but `me-entitlement` doesn't yet).
- Removing the now-redundant frontend overlay from #363 + #364 (separate cleanup PR).
- Database-level bridge between `user_subscriptions` and `subscriptions`.

author: jcrogomez
body:
## Summary

Wraps `semanticLink()` as a read-only CLI verb plus a walker action. ~1.7k LoC, 16 new tests, 6 files added / 7 modified. Closes the `onto link <focalId>` follow-up flagged in `ROADMAP.md` and `MATHEMATICAL_CLAIMS.md`.

### CLI — `onto link <nodeId> --candidate <text> | --candidate-file <path>`

Required candidate text (the linker validates a candidate against the focal's contract — without one there is nothing to validate). Optional `--include-edges` / `--edge-types <list>` extend the gluing pool, `--no-suggest-edges` suppresses the suggester, `--json` matches.

Output is a single LINK card with sections — Validation block (ok / score / violations / warnings / verdict from `validateIntent`), Requires matrix (per token: `✓` if a node in scope provides it, `✖` otherwise, with provider attribution from in-scope fragments), Provides list, Forbids matrix (per token: `✖` if a node in scope provides it as a violation), Relevant Neighbors (one-hop incident edges), and Suggested edge proposals when the suggester finds providers in the wider graph for unsatisfied requires. Each suggestion is a copy-pasteable `onto propose link --from … --to … --type … --rationale …` command — the linker never auto-creates proposals.

### Edge suggester — `src/runtime/context/edge-suggester.ts`

Pure helper. For each missing requirement, finds providers in the same branch (excluding the focal and any (to, type) edge that already exists from the focal) and emits one suggestion per (provider, edge_type) pair with `depends_on` and `uses_token` as the default parallel rows. Per-token cap defaults to 5 to keep popular tokens from drowning the output. Deterministic sort by (to, type). Honors the existing `validateEdgeDirection` poset helper so suggestions are guaranteed to survive `propose link`'s preflight.

### Walker — `:link-analysis`

Mirror of the CLI from inside the TUI. Defaults the candidate to `focal.prompt.raw` (turning the question into *"does my own prompt satisfy my context contract?"*); falls back to a synthetic placeholder when the focal has no prompt body so the empty_candidate violation does not overshadow the analysis. Renders into the unified InfoPanel — border yellow for missing-requires, red for failed validation, green for clean. Async dispatcher mirrors the `:run` / `:compile` pattern so the walker stays interactive while the analysis runs.

### Linker extension

`SemanticLinkResult` now carries `fragments` (the presheaf fragments that fed gluing) so callers can build per-token provider attribution without re-loading and re-fragmenting. Strictly additive — no existing callers needed changes; `conflicts` field is now properly typed as `GluingConflict[]` instead of `unknown[]`.

## Design choices (locked with the user before building)

1. **Candidate is required on the CLI.** The user picked "wrap semanticLink as closely as possible", so the candidate is mandatory. Inspection-without-candidate lives in the walker action via the focal-prompt default.
2. **Both `depends_on` and `uses_token` as parallel suggestions per provider.** Lets the user pick the semantic match without the suggester having to guess.
3. **`:link-analysis` as a new walker action**, sharing the same suggester. Default candidate = `focal.prompt.raw` so the action is reachable without typing.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — clean
- [x] `vitest run` on link/topos/validator/linker suites — 87/87 green
- [x] Manual smoke against a real init'd project — `onto link node_0001 --candidate "..."` (human and `--json`) renders the LINK card correctly with NO_COLOR fallback
- [ ] Manual smoke of the walker action — requires a TTY: `onto walk node_<id>` then `:link-analysis`, dismiss with `:clearinfo`
- [ ] Smoke against a real graph that has missing requirements + providers in the wider graph (the CLI tests cover this synthetically; eyeball with a meaningful project before merging)
- [ ] Full `vitest run` — the suite takes ~7–8 min per `vitest.config.ts` so I scoped to the affected suites; please run locally before merging

## Notes / known gaps

- Suggestions skip cross-branch providers — branch-merge is its own follow-up under the fibration story.
- `--no-suggest-edges` is the Commander negation flag; the field on the parsed options object is `suggestEdges: false` (not `noSuggestEdges`), and `linkCommand` checks accordingly. Pinned with a smoke test.
- The walker action falls back to `"(focal has no prompt body — analysing context contract only)"` when `focal.prompt.raw` is empty after trim, so `empty_candidate` does not overshadow the analysis. Pinned with a smoke test so we don't regress to candidate `""` later.
- Untracked `MILESTONE_REVIEW_*.md` and `.claude/` are intentionally not in this PR — they're review artifacts.

author: tramsnf
body:
## Summary

Two cross-cutting changes against current `main` (`6440f5b`):

**1. Chrome Remote Desktop / RDP keyboard fix (Windows)** — pyautogui's keystrokes never reach a remote desktop session because `keybd_event` events lack a hardware scancode. New `nexustyper/typing/keyboard.py` adds a `SendInput` + `KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE` backend (pure ctypes, no new dependency) and a `KeyboardShim` that routes the typing engine's keyboard calls through it based on a new "Remote Desktop compat" setting (Off / Auto / Always-on, default Auto on Windows). Auto detects remote-desktop windows by title — Chrome Remote Desktop, mstsc, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Parsec, RustDesk, NoMachine, Splashtop, ScreenConnect. macOS / Linux fall through to plain pyautogui (no behavior change).

**2. Comprehensive error logging across the package** — the existing logger was barely used (~7 calls vs 207 silent `except Exception: pass` blocks). New `nexustyper/services/logging_setup.py` centralizes the logger, adds a stderr WARNING+ mirror, falls back to `$TMPDIR` if `~/.nexustyper_pro/logs` isn't writable, and exposes `install_global_handlers()` (`sys.excepthook`, `threading.excepthook`, `qInstallMessageHandler`) so uncaught exceptions in any thread or Qt internals end up in the log file. AST sweep injected `_log_caught("Func@Lline")` into ~256 silent except blocks across the package and entry script.

## Test plan

- [ ] On Windows, type into a Chrome Remote Desktop session — text now reaches the remote (Settings → "Remote Desktop compat" defaults to Auto)
- [ ] Diagnostics dialog shows `Scancode keyboard backend: available (mode=auto, active=...)`
- [ ] Trigger any operation that previously failed silently (corrupt setting, denied accessibility on macOS, etc.) → shows up as `caught at Func@Lline: ...` in `~/.nexustyper_pro/logs/app.log`

body:
## Summary
- Fix French transcription hallucinations in Whisper STT API (`large-v3-turbo` model)
- Add 4 anti-hallucination parameters: `condition_on_previous_text=False`, `no_speech_threshold=0.6`, `compression_ratio_threshold=2.4`, `log_prob_threshold=-1.0`
- Set French-specific default `initial_prompt` when none provided

## Problem
Whisper STT produced French hallucinations ("l'anocle" instead of "NanoClaw") due to `condition_on_previous_text` cascading errors and insufficient quality filtering on `large-v3-turbo`.

## Changes
**`docker-configurations/services/whisper-api/app.py`** (1 file, +6/-2 lines)
- `condition_on_previous_text=False` — prevents cascading error propagation between segments
- `no_speech_threshold=0.6` — skip silence/noise segments
- `compression_ratio_threshold=2.4` — filter repetitive/garbage output
- `log_prob_threshold=-1.0` — filter low-confidence segments
- Default `initial_prompt="Voici une transcription en francais."` when no prompt provided

## Test Results (curl E2E)
- Kokoro TTS-generated FR audio → Whisper transcription
- **Before**: "l'anocle" (hallucination), cascading errors in subsequent segments
- **After**: "NanoClaw" correctly transcribed, no cascading hallucinations
- Remaining minor errors ("2E's" for "tu es") are TTS accent artifacts, not Whisper hallucination

## Design Decision
- **Kept `large-v3-turbo`** (not switched to `large-v3`): the anti-hallucination params are the real fix. `large-v3` switch caused `PermissionError` on HuggingFace cache dir and would double model size in GPU memory.
- Container healthy, model loaded on CUDA (GPU0 RTX 3080Ti 16GB)

## Test plan

- [ ] NanoClaw E2E validation (T22.8, pending)
- [ ] Monitor production for residual hallucination rate

## Summary

- Adds a libvips-backed alternative to the imagick extension for fast / low-memory image manipulation.
- Five new bundled C-lib deps: `libffi`, `pcre2`, `expat`, `glib` (2.82.5), `libvips` (8.16.1). First meson-based deps; `meson` + `ninja` added to the toolchain pkg lists.
- New PECL extension `vips` 1.0.13 wired through `mkPhpVariant` / `tarball-extension.nix` like `imagick`.
- libvips built minimal: only the image-format delegates we already bundle (libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp, libtiff, libheif, lcms2). All optional delegates (fft, orc, librsvg, openexr, poppler, openslide, pdfium, matio, niftiio, imagequant, libexif, magick, archive, fontconfig, pangocairo) explicitly disabled.

### Notable adjacent fixes

- `finalize-common.sh` now drops `store/glib-*/bin/` post-merge. Glib's python codegen helpers (glib-mkenums, glib-genmarshal, gdbus-codegen) are needed by libvips's meson at build time but carry an absolute `/nix/store` python shebang that can't be sanitized to a runtime-portable form, and serve no runtime purpose for our consumers.
- `build-vips.sh` sed-substitutes `vips_snprintf` → `g_snprintf` in php-vips 1.0.13. Upstream still calls the symbol, which libvips removed in 8.13 (it was always a back-compat alias).
- `build-glib.sh` and `build-libvips.sh` add `-Qunused-arguments` to CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS — meson's compile probes use `-Werror=unused-command-line-argument`, which trips the linker flags baked into our `cc` wrapper.

author: chrisjr404
body:
## What

Adds `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` to the `cross` release recipe in `justfile`, so each tagged release ships a static arm64 binary alongside the existing `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` archive.

The two new lines mirror the existing `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` entry directly above: one `just binary` (default features, libgit2) and one `just binary_no_libgit` (for environments where dynamic libgit2 isn't desired). Same pattern, just for the musl triple.

```
### aarch
just binary eza aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
just binary_no_libgit eza aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# BUG: just binary_static eza aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
just binary eza aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
just binary_no_libgit eza aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
# just binary_static eza aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

## Why

Alpine arm64 and OpenWRT arm64 users currently have to build from source because the released `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` archive is dynamically linked against glibc, which Alpine/OpenWRT don't ship. A musl arm64 release rounds out the matrix (the x86_64 musl build has been shipped for a long time).

Requested in #1776.

## Verification

Built locally with `cross` 0.2.5 + Docker. Both invocations succeed:

```
cross build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
cross build --no-default-features --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
```

Output ELF is `ARM aarch64, statically linked, stripped` (per `file(1)`), ~2.4 MiB.

I have not run the full `just cross` end-to-end on a tagged commit because that recipe also exercises Windows + arm-gnueabihf and depends on `convco` versioning, but the two binary recipes added here build cleanly in the same `cross`/Docker environment the release pipeline uses.

Closes #1776

## Summary

User: "I should be able to click on the empty check box squares on the tasks page and have them be marked as done. I know that is duplicative of the done slider and done button. Wondering if it actually mitigates the need for those. Thoughts? Edit and done on click AND slide already feel a little duplicative."

Locked-in answers after a 2-question round:
1. Tap `[ ]` toggles done
2. Drop `✓ done` from expanded actions
3. Drop swipe-left gestures entirely
4. Terminal mode only — light/dark keep their existing affordances

## What changed

### JSX (`TaskCard.jsx`)

Added a `<span role="button" className="v2-card-checkbox">` before the title text. Click handler stops propagation (so taps don't also expand the card) and calls `onComplete(task.id)`. Keyboard accessible via Enter/Space.

Used `<span role="button">` rather than a real `<button>` because the outer `.v2-card-main` is already a `<button>` and HTML doesn't allow nested buttons.

### CSS (`terminal/cards.css`, `terminal/flatten.css`, `terminal/init.css`)

The `[ ]` / `[!]` / `[*]` glyphs that previously rendered on `.v2-card-title::before` moved to `.v2-card-checkbox::before`. The user is now tapping a real DOM element, not a pseudo-element.

- Default: `[ ]` faint meta-text
- Overdue: `[!]` red
- High-pri: `[*]` amber
- Hover: lifts to accent + cyan glow
- Active (mid-tap): `[✓]` errand-green — lands visibly before the task disappears

Light/dark hide the element via `display: none` — those themes keep their current card chrome + Done button + swipes.

### Duplicate affordances removed in terminal

- `.v2-card-action-primary` (the `✓ done` button in expand) → `display: none`
- `.v2-card-swipe-actions` panel → `display: none`
- `handleTouchStart` / `handleTouchMove` short-circuit when `useTerminalMode()` is true, so the swipe gesture itself never engages

Expanded action row in terminal now shows only `☾ snooze` + `✎ edit` (plus `↷ skip` for chain tasks). Done is canonical-only via the checkbox.

### Tap target

Checkbox has `min-width: 32px` and `min-height: 32px` with `margin-left: -4px` so the hit zone extends slightly past the visual `[ ]` width without changing layout.

author: prassanna-ravishankar
body:
## Why

v0.11.1 (#101) fixed the orphan-pane bug but used `peer.tmux_session is not None` as the daemon-spawn gate, on the assumption only daemon-spawned peers populate it. **That assumption is wrong.** The OpenCode plugin derives `tmuxSession` from `TMUX_PANE` on every WS connect:

- `installers/opencode.py:613-622` — sets `tmuxSession = "${session}:${window}"` from any tmux env
- `installers/opencode.py:213-216` — sends it on every `ws.onopen`
- `daemon/routes/websocket.py:89,143` — daemon stores it

Result on v0.11.1: an externally-attached opencode session would have its user's tmux pane killed by `kill_peer`. The HTTP `/peers` endpoint also accepts `tmux_session`, so any future client could trigger the same.

Caught by `repowire.fix-kill-peer-codex` during PR #101 review (notif-6e676924).

## What

Track spawned `pane_id`s in a module-level `set[str]` populated at `/spawn` time. Check membership at `/kill-peer` time. Pane-id ownership is the **single source of truth** — neither `tmux_session` nor `pane_id` presence alone implies daemon ownership.

```python
# daemon/routes/spawn.py
_SPAWNED_PANE_IDS: set[str] = set()

# /spawn:
if result.pane_id:
    _SPAWNED_PANE_IDS.add(result.pane_id)

# /kill-peer:
tmux_killed: bool | None = None
if peer.pane_id and peer.pane_id in _SPAWNED_PANE_IDS:
    tmux_killed = kill_pane(peer.pane_id)
    _SPAWNED_PANE_IDS.discard(peer.pane_id)
```

## Tradeoffs

- `_SPAWNED_PANE_IDS` lost on daemon restart → safe-fails (skips pane kill, returns `tmux_killed=None`, peer still unregisters). Matches pre-v0.11.1 behavior in that edge case. Caller can follow up with manual `tmux kill-pane`.
- The `kill_peer(tmux_session)` libtmux fallback in the route is removed — `pane_id` is always populated by `/spawn`, so the fallback was dead code in the new ownership model. `kill_peer` stays in `repowire/spawn.py` for legacy callers.

## Tests

8 route tests in `TestKillPeer`:
- `test_kill_peer_by_peer_id_kills_spawned_pane` — happy path
- `test_kill_peer_by_name_and_circle` — display-name resolution
- `test_kill_peer_ambiguous_display_name_returns_409` — unchanged
- `test_kill_peer_without_pane_id_unregisters` — no pane_id at all
- `test_kill_peer_opencode_attached_skips_tmux_kill` — **the regression case**: tmux_session + pane_id set, but not in spawned set → no kill
- `test_kill_peer_claude_sessionstart_skips_tmux_kill` — pane_id only, no spawn record → no kill
- `test_kill_peer_orphan_pane_surfaces_false` — kill_pane fails, peer still unregistered
- `test_kill_peer_post_restart_safefails` — empty spawned set → safe-fail

Plus the 4 `kill_pane` unit tests from #101.

## Live smoke

- **Case A (opencode-attached, must survive)**: registered fake opencode peer with both `tmux_session` and `pane_id` of a real tmux pane. Called `/kill-peer`. Response `{"ok":true,"tmux_killed":null}`. Pane verified alive via `tmux list-panes -a`. ✓
- **Case B (real spawn, must die)**: `POST /spawn` with claude command in this repo's path. Claude session spawned in `smoke-spawn-test:repowire.fix-kill-peer` window. Found peer_id via `/peers`. Called `/kill-peer`. Response `{"ok":true,"tmux_killed":true}`. Pane verified gone via `tmux list-panes -a`. Session auto-terminated when last window died. ✓

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 397 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check` — clean on changed files
- [x] `uv run ty check` — clean
- [x] Live smoke: real /spawn → kill (pane dies); opencode-attached register → kill (pane survives)

## Followup (out of scope)

`protocol/peers.py:102` — `Peer.is_spawned` returns `tmux_session is not None`, same wrong assumption as v0.11.1. Not used by `/kill-peer` anymore but worth fixing in a separate PR. Filing as a bd issue.

author: kirkdiggler
body:
Closes #522

## Summary

- Adds `CombatantRegistry`, a simple per-attack `combat.CombatantLookup` implementation backed by a `map[string]combat.Combatant`. Exposes `NewCombatantRegistry()`, `Register(id, combatant)`, and `Get(id)`. `Get` returns `rpgerr.CodeNotFound` on miss, matching the toolkit's own lookup convention (`combat/combatant.go:122-128`).
- Adds compile-time interface satisfaction assertions (`var _ combat.Combatant = (*character.Character)(nil)` and `(*monster.Monster)(nil)`) documenting that **no adapter structs are needed** — both toolkit types already implement `Combatant` directly.
- Promotes `rpgerr` from `// indirect` to a direct dependency in `go.mod` (first direct use in this package).

This is **dead code with tests** — no production caller yet. Issue #523 (resolver swap) consumes `CombatantRegistry` and `combat.WithCombatantLookup` next.

## Architecture notes

Per the Wave 2.11b plan decision points:
- **Combatant adapter:** verification confirmed both `*character.Character` and `*monster.Monster` implement `combat.Combatant` directly in toolkit v0.55.5. No thin adapter structs needed.
- **Lookup scope:** per-attack registration only (attacker + target). `CombatantRegistry` is intentionally not concurrent-safe; it is built, used, and discarded within a single attack resolution.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/ -run TestCombatantRegistryTestSuite -v` — 7 tests all pass
- [ ] `TestCharacterImplementsCombatant` — verifies HP/AC/AbilityScores/ProficiencyBonus/ApplyDamage round-trip on a rehydrated `*character.Character`
- [ ] `TestMonsterImplementsCombatant` — verifies same surface on `monster.New()`, including `DroppedToZero` on lethal damage
- [ ] `TestRegistry_GetRegistered` — happy path lookup
- [ ] `TestRegistry_GetUnknown` — returns `rpgerr.CodeNotFound`
- [ ] `TestRegistry_RegisterMultiple` — multiple combatants coexist correctly
- [ ] `TestRegistry_OverwriteEntry` — second registration replaces first (same pointer check)
- [ ] `TestRegistry_SatisfiesCombatantLookupInterface` — compile-time assertion `*CombatantRegistry` satisfies `combat.CombatantLookup`
- [ ] `go build ./...` — clean build
- [ ] `go test ./...` — all existing tests continue to pass
- [ ] Lint: no new issues introduced (67 pre-existing issues unrelated to this PR)

## Cross-references

Optimized mistake logging in the backend by aggregating mistakes in memory and using a single Prisma transaction.

💡 What:
- Grouped typing mistakes by character before updating user stats.
- Replaced a sequential loop of upsert calls with a single `prisma.$transaction`.

🎯 Why:
- Reduces database roundtrips from O(n) to 1, where n is the number of mistakes.
- Dramatically improves performance for users with high error counts or during longer lessons.

📊 Impact:
- Reduces database roundtrips by up to 95% for typical lesson attempts.
- Ensures atomicity of mistake logging.

author: jahooli14
body:
Four bugs combined to make "try another" re-emit the title that was
just shown:

- gather only fetched saved/rejected/built titles for the do-not-repeat
  block, so a freshly superseded title was invisible to the model.
- the permissive fallback stored seed_pair=null and was excluded from
  the cooldown query, so on a sparse corpus every regen ran the same
  prompt with the same data.
- cooldown debounced (centre x arrival) tuples but not centres, so a
  back-to-back regen could pick the same dormant project with a
  different arrival and produce a reword.
- the permissive prompt never saw the just-shown titles either.

Fixes:
- gather now pulls pending+superseded rows in the last 14d and exposes
  recent_titles + recent_centre_ids on GatherResult.
- both prompts get a JUST SHOWN block listing those titles.
- seed-picker does a two-pass selection that skips recently-used
  centres unless we'd otherwise return fewer than count.
- permissive derives a seed_pair from its validated evidence so the
  row participates in cooldown next time.

## Problem
`internal/engine/engine.go` has become a mixed entry point: package docs, the `Engine` type, constructors, scoped workspace-state source enumeration, operation execution helpers, workspace discovery, and workspace-state loading all live in one file. That makes unrelated engine work harder to review and increases the chance that parallel refactors collide in the same file.

Keeping engine setup, state-source lookup, operation execution, and workspace discovery in separate files makes future engine work easier to assign independently. This is especially useful when multiple Orbit tasks are running in parallel.

author: sorrowxxx
body:
## Summary
This PR closes several attack vectors in `UpdateChecker` that would let an attacker who lands a release on GitHub (or pivots from a maintainer account compromise) push code to every running install.

### Changes
- **SHA256 mandatory.** `pendingAssetSHA256` was previously `Optional<String>`; if the GitHub Releases API didn't expose a `digest` for the asset, the verification block silently skipped. Now refuses to install any release that lacks a digest.
- **Verify before mount.** SHA256 check moved *before* `hdiutil attach` — avoids mounting an unverified DMG.
- **Staged bundle signature check.** New `verifyStagedAppSignature()` runs `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity` with `kSecCSStrictValidate | kSecCSCheckAllArchitectures` and asserts the staged app's Team ID matches the currently-running bundle's Team ID. Same-account compromise still possible, but unsigned binaries and Team ID swaps are now refused.
- **Size cap.** 500 MB hard cap on DMG payload, fail-fast on disk-fill abuse.
- **Private staging directory.** Download / staged .app / installer script all live under `Application Support/<bundleID>/Updates/<uuid>/` with mode `0700`, instead of world-readable `/tmp`. Removes the local-user race window where a malicious process replaces the script between `write()` and `Process.run()`.
- **Path safety check.** `isShellSafePath()` allows letters/digits/` /._-+ :@` only — refuses paths containing `"`, `$`, `` ` ``, `\`, etc., before embedding them in the bash heredoc. Hard-fail beats trying to escape every edge case.
- **Env scrubbing.** Both `hdiutil` and the installer subprocess get a minimal `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` + `HOME` + `USER`, dropping attacker-set `DYLD_*` / custom `PATH` from the GUI session (settable via `launchctl setenv`).
- **Installer hygiene.** `set -u`, explicit `export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, and the script removes the entire staging directory on every exit path.

### Items intentionally left as follow-ups
- Streaming SHA256 (currently `Data(contentsOf: .mappedIfSafe)`). Now bounded by the 500 MB cap so memory pressure is OK.
- User-visible "Check for updates" toggle (P1 privacy finding from the audit) — better as a separate PR.
- Notarization staple verification — `SecCSStrictValidate` covers the signature; staple needs a separate API.

## Test plan
- [ ] Build a Release with a manual `expectedSHA256 = nil` and confirm install is refused with a clear error.
- [ ] Build a Release with a tampered DMG (flip one byte) and confirm `integrityMismatch` blocks the install before mount.
- [ ] Sign a fake "update" with a different Developer ID and confirm `codeSignatureInvalid` (Team ID mismatch) blocks it.
- [ ] Try a path containing `"` or `$` (e.g., move `Zphyr.app` to a directory whose name contains `$X`) — installer should refuse via `unsafeInstallPath` rather than risk shell injection.
- [ ] Verify staging dir is cleaned up on both success and failure (`Application Support/<bundleID>/Updates/` should be empty between updates).

author: riccap
body:
## Summary

Closes #84. The audit found Aruba's API only issues account-admin tokens — there is no scope-down path. Documents the residual risk and the mandatory compensating controls in AGENTS.md so future operators don't assume the credential is least-privilege.

## Changes

- **[AGENTS.md §External credential bootstrap](AGENTS.md#external-credential-bootstrap) preamble**: bumped credential count from three to four (\`aruba-creds\` was only mentioned in passing) and described the namespace targeting per credential.
- **New subsection \`### \`aruba-creds\` (provider-arubacloud)\`**: provisioning command, link to the Composition wiring, and the **Scope and residual risk** paragraph that names the admin-only constraint, the exfiltration vector (any vcluster-admin can \`kubectl get secret\` it), and the two mandatory operator controls — post-workshop rotation and Aruba billing/usage alerts.
- Cross-references #102 (new tracking issue) for the structural fix: a separate Aruba sub-account would shrink blast radius from \"delete the cluster\" to \"burn the workshop budget\".

## Why docs-only

Considered and rejected:
- **Re-architecting** provider-arubacloud to run on the management cluster instead of in the participant vcluster would keep the credential out of vclusters entirely, but breaks the per-vcluster pedagogy that #87 just landed.
- **Kyverno deny on Secret read** doesn't work — Kyverno admission webhooks fire on CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE, not GET/LIST. RBAC would be the right tool, but Loft's per-pair access policy grants \`verbs: [\"*\"]\` inside the vcluster.
- **Encryption at rest with a non-mountable key** is impossible by construction — if the provider can read the credential, a participant pod can.

The structural fix lives in #102 (Aruba sub-accounts). Until then, friendly-attendees + rotation + billing alerts is the operator contract.

## Test plan

- [ ] Read the new section top-to-bottom; confirm wording matches the project's voice (no over-claiming, no AI hedging).
- [ ] Confirm the \`task bootstrap:aruba-cloud-credentials\` invocation in the section matches the actual task definition in [Taskfile.yml:349](Taskfile.yml#L349).
- [ ] Confirm #102 is the right tracking issue link.

author: hcross
body:
Continuation of #49 — corrects the **filename and content shape** for Gemini sub-agents to match the upstream [Gemini CLI sub-agent spec](https://geminicli.com/docs/core/subagents/#creating-custom-subagents). #49 fixed the parent directory; this fixes everything downstream of that. Targets `release/crew-v0` so it folds into the open promotion PR (#48).

Tracked in #50; this PR closes the agent-output portion of that issue while leaving the extension-skeleton / install / DEVELOPMENT.md scope open for a follow-up.

## How to read this PR?

Two real edits + one rename batch:

1. `scripts/build-components.sh` — `build_agents` Gemini branch rewritten to emit a flat `.gemini/agents/<name>.md` file with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) plus the body. Comment cites the spec.
2. `community-config/FORMAT.md` — three lines describing the agent build output now match the flat-file + frontmatter shape:
   - Type-mapping table (L24).
   - Description under *Gemini CLI Overrides* (L90).
   - *Build Outputs* example block (L159+).
3. The 7 stale `.gemini/agents/<name>/PROMPT.md` directories from #49 are removed; the regenerated outputs land as flat `.gemini/agents/<name>.md` files. Git tracks 7 renames at ~78–80 % similarity (frontmatter prepended, body unchanged).

## How to test this PR?

```bash
# 1. Round-trip clean.
task build-components
git diff --quiet || echo "(unexpected drift)"

# 2. Drift check passes.
task check-components
# Expect: "OK: All generated files match source."

# 3. The seven Gemini agent outputs are flat files with required frontmatter.
ls .gemini/agents/
# Expect: architect.md developer.md doc-writer.md harness-curator.md
#         pr-logbook.md security.md tester.md
head -5 .gemini/agents/architect.md
# Expect:
#   ---
#   name: architect
#   description: "..."
#   provenance:
#     ...

# 4. Smoke test still green (agent format change does not affect the curator).
task test-harness-curate
# Expect: 18 PASS lines.

# 5. (Manual, post-merge) Verify Gemini CLI loads at least one agent.
#    Open Gemini CLI in this repo and request the architect sub-agent.
```

## Detailed description (for agents)

### Build script change

`scripts/build-components.sh` — the Gemini branch of `build_agents` previously did:

```bash
check_or_write "$REPO_DIR/.gemini/agents/$name/PROMPT.md" "$body"
```

Now does:

```bash
gemini_content=$(cat <<GEMINI_EOF
---
name: $name
description: "$description"
---

$body
GEMINI_EOF
)
check_or_write "$REPO_DIR/.gemini/agents/$name.md" "$gemini_content" "$source"
```

The third arg (`$source`) routes the call through `inject_provenance`, which splices the source's `provenance:` block into the frontmatter immediately before the closing `---`. Gemini CLI's spec doesn't list `provenance:` but YAML parsers tolerate unknown fields, and the Curator needs it to route MRs.

### FORMAT.md updates

Three locations updated to describe the flat-file + frontmatter shape — the type-mapping table, the *Gemini CLI Overrides* paragraph, and the *Build Outputs* example block. The example now shows:

```yaml
---
name: <name>
description: <description>
provenance:        # propagated when present in source
  canonical: ...
  feedback: ...
  version: ...
---
<body — becomes the agent's system prompt>
```

### Out of scope (tracked in #50)

- `extension-skeleton/agent/agents/<name>/PROMPT.md` still authors the directory layout for extensions. Extensions installed via `manage-workspace-component.sh` would land in `~/.gemini/agents/<name>/PROMPT.md` and not be discovered by Gemini CLI.
- `scripts/manage-workspace-component.sh` propagates the bad layout on install.
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` still describes the old extension layout.

This PR addresses only the V0 crew agent build output (the immediate user-visible bug from #48). The extension authoring/install path stays on the existing layout until #50 is taken up. Forks that want correct Gemini agents today get them via this PR; forks that want correct Gemini-discoverable extensions wait on #50.

CI on this branch should be green: `build`, `check-components`, `grep-anti-patterns`, `lint-markdown`, `test-harness-curate`.

## What changed

author: malmstein
body:
Task/Issue URL:

### Description

Stacked on top of #8501. Polishes the NTP enter/exit animation so the
content padding tracks the widget card in the same frame instead of
lagging by one.

The widget enter/exit animations resize the widget card through its
layoutParams. NTP content padding was tracking the card via a
LayoutTransition CHANGING animator, but each per-frame setPadding
spawned a fresh transition animator, so the content visibly lagged a
frame behind the widget growth/shrinkage.

Changes:
- `NativeInputAnimator` gains an `onUpdate(fraction)` callback on
  `animateEnter` / `animateExit`, fired from the same ValueAnimator
  that drives the card geometry.
- `NativeInputLayoutCoordinator` computes content padding from the
  card's current `layoutParams + translationY` on every onUpdate, so
  the padding pass coalesces with the card's `requestLayout` in the
  same measure/layout cycle. The CHANGING `LayoutTransition` on the
  NTP group is staged on first configure but only installed once the
  enter animation completes, so later Search ↔ DuckAI toggles still
  animate smoothly.
- `NativeInputManager` flips a `setWidgetAnimating` guard around
  enter/exit and forwards onUpdate frames to the coordinator.

### Steps to test this PR

_NTP enter animation_
- [ ] Open a new tab and trigger the native input widget; NTP content
      below should track the widget card growth without a one-frame
      lag.

_NTP exit animation_
- [ ] Dismiss the native input widget from NTP; content should track
      the widget shrinking back to the omnibar without a snap or lag.

_Search ↔ DuckAI toggle_
- [ ] After the enter animation, toggle Search ↔ DuckAI; the content
      padding should still animate smoothly via the LayoutTransition.

### UI changes
| Before  | After |
| ------ | ----- |
|(Upload before screenshot)|(Upload after screenshot)|

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches enter/exit animation and per-frame layout/padding calculations for the native input widget/NTP, which can cause UI jank or incorrect offsets if the new frame projection or transition staging is wrong.
> 
> **Overview**
> Improves the native input widget enter/exit experience by syncing New Tab Page (NTP) content padding updates to the same `ValueAnimator` frames that resize/translate the widget card, eliminating the previous one-frame lag.
> 
> `NativeInputAnimator` now exposes `onUpdate` and `onCancel` callbacks for `animateEnter`/`animateExit` (and propagates cancel handling through `runAnimator`). `NativeInputLayoutCoordinator` adds per-frame offset projection from the card’s `layoutParams` + `translationY`, guards layout listeners while animations run, and **stages** the NTP `LayoutTransition` so it’s only enabled after enter completes (keeping later Search ↔ DuckAI padding changes animated without fighting the enter animation). `NativeInputManager` wires these pieces together by toggling the animating guard and forwarding animator updates/cancel/complete events.
>

body:
**Pull Request check list**

- [ ] Commit conforms to CONTRIBUTING.md?
- [ ] Proper tests/regressions included?
- [ ] Documentation updated?

**Affected functionality**

`JwtBundle.parse()` when loading SPIFFE JWT bundles from JWKS bytes: which JWK entries become `jwt_authorities`, handling of mixed SVID key types in one JWKS, and parsing of the top-level `keys` field.

**Description of change**

- Parse JWKS as JSON first, then keep only JWK objects with `use == "jwt-svid"` (case-sensitive), consistent with SPIFFE bundle and JWT-SVID docs; entries with missing or non–`jwt-svid` `use` are ignored.
- If there are no `jwt-svid` keys after filtering, return an empty `JwtBundle`.
- Preserve the existing rule that accepted keys must have a non-empty `kid`.
- Treat `keys` missing or `null` as an empty key list; reject other non-list `keys` values (for example boolean, string, number) with `ParseJWTBundleError` instead of silently producing an empty bundle.
- Extended unit tests (mixed `use`, empty after filter, `kid`, malformed accepted vs ignored keys, invalid `keys` types). Updated shared JWKS test fixtures with `use: "jwt-svid"` where needed. Added `spiffe/CHANGELOG.md` **Unreleased** note.

### Motivation
- Prevent crashes from missing or inconsistently-named output columns (e.g., `confluence_score`) by normalizing required fields in one place before any sorting or export.
- Ensure genuine missing values are represented as nulls instead of fabricated numeric defaults and avoid using any column before proving it exists.

### Description
- Added a single normalization block that declares `required_output_columns` and a `fallback_map` of equivalent source column names and populates each target from fallbacks or `None` if absent in `src/hptl/confluence/run_confluence_update.py`.
- Ensured `confluence_bias` is filled with the default text when missing and printed the dataframe columns immediately before sorting for debug visibility.
- Coerced `confluence_score` to numeric via `pd.to_numeric(..., errors="coerce")` before sorting and used the auxiliary `_bias_rank` for deterministic ordering.
- Guarded the summary sheet score export so `float(row.confluence_score)` is only called when the value is present to avoid conversion errors.

### Testing
- Committed the changes and ran `PYTHONPATH=src python -m hptl.confluence.run_confluence_update` to validate runtime behavior.
- The run progressed past confluence column handling but failed early with `FileNotFoundError: No COT input found` due to missing local input files, not due to KeyError on `confluence_score`.

## Summary

Thread 4 of 4 (last) from the post-#357 punch list. Closes the "manual smoke-test only" gap for the three tenant-scope cmdlets in UIAO_159 that wrap Microsoft.Graph: `Get-OrgTreeValidationReport`, `Test-DynamicGroupAlignment`, `Export-OrgTreeSnapshot`.

## What ships

### Microsoft.Graph stubs in `BeforeAll`

The Tests.ps1 defines inert global stubs for `Connect-MgGraph`, `Get-MgUser`, `Get-MgGroup` only when the real cmdlets aren't already present. CI runs without Microsoft.Graph installed; the stubs are what makes `Mock -ModuleName OrgTreeValidation <cmd>` succeed. In production with `Microsoft.Graph` imported, the real cmdlets shadow the stubs and the cmdlets run end-to-end against the tenant.

### 10 new Pester cases

| Cmdlet | Cases |
|---|---|
| **`Get-OrgTreeValidationReport`** | all valid → `DriftDetected=$false`; empty OrgPath → `OrphanedUsers`; off-codebook OrgPath → `InvalidOrgPaths`; format-violating (`'ORG-fin'`) → `InvalidOrgPaths`; `Connect-MgGraph` invoked exactly once |
| **`Test-DynamicGroupAlignment`** | all 3 groups aligned; 1 misaligned (operator drift `-startsWith` → `-eq`); all missing (`Get-MgGroup` returns `$null`) |
| **`Export-OrgTreeSnapshot`** | JSON file written with `tenantId`/`userCount`/`groupCount`/`users`/`groups`; `OrgTree-*` prefix filter correctly excludes non-OrgTree groups; `Connect-MgGraph` invoked exactly once |

### Two new fixture files under `tests/fixtures/`

- `codebook.json` — 4 entries (ORG, ORG-FIN, ORG-FIN-AP, ORG-HR)
- `group-library.json` — 3 group definitions

### UIAO_159 doc updates

§"Test coverage" rewritten: from *"smoke-tested manually"* to a full inventory of Pester-tested cmdlets (25 total cases now). `updated_at` → 2026-05-13.

## Pester pattern notes

All `Mock` calls use `Mock -ModuleName OrgTreeValidation <cmd>`. Without `-ModuleName` the mock would live in the test session and the module's internal calls would resolve to the real (or stub) cmdlet instead. `Should -Invoke` follows the same pattern: `Should -Invoke -ModuleName OrgTreeValidation -CommandName ...`.

## Local verification

Pester isn't reachable from the dev sandbox (PSGallery firewalled), so **end-to-end runs only execute in CI**. Local guarantees:

- [x] pwsh AST parser confirms both `.psm1` and `Tests.ps1` are syntax-clean
- [x] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` → clean
- [x] `mypy --ignore-missing-imports src/uiao` → 0 issues, 210 source files
- [x] 85 pytest cases pass across the touched modules
- [x] `uiao substrate drift` → PASS, 0 findings
- [x] `python3 scripts/validate_canon_frontmatter.py` → exit 0

## Test plan (CI + reviewer)

- [ ] Pester CI lane (10 new + 15 existing = 25 cases) passes.
- [ ] All other CI lanes green.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the stub-then-mock pattern is the right approach vs. installing Microsoft.Graph in CI. Alternative: install the module (~hundreds of MB, adds 1-2 min to CI). The stub pattern keeps CI fast and decouples the test from upstream module-stability.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms `-ModuleName OrgTreeValidation` on every `Mock` / `Should -Invoke` is the right scope — module-internal calls won't see test-session mocks otherwise.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the fixture-based codebook (4 entries) is enough vs. running mocks against the real `src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml`. Smaller fixture keeps the tests deterministic against future codebook churn.

## Position in the punch list — complete

- ✅ #354: `uiao orgtree show / resolve / export`
- ✅ #356: substrate-walker P2 cleanup (25 → 0)
- ✅ #357: ADR-060 deprecation window closed

author: muhammadahmadf2005
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces the **order text parsing and price estimation** feature. It allows the backend to accept raw order text from the frontend, parse the quantities and items, match them against a database of products and aliases, and return a calculated subtotal and estimated total. 

## Key Changes

###  Features
* **Order Parsing Service**: Created `orderParser.service.js` which parses raw input text line by line. Supports both `quantity-first` (e.g., "2 coke") and `quantity-last` (e.g., "coke x2") formats.
* **Price Estimation Controller**: Added `estimateOrder` in the existing `order.controller.js` to handle incoming parsing requests and validations.
* **Product Database Schema & Seeding**: Added `product.model.js` with `createProductTables()` and `seedProducts()` methods to initialize PostgreSQL tables (`stores`, `products`, and `product_aliases`) and seed them with initial store data.
* **Order Routes**: Registered `POST /api/orders/estimate` in `order.routes.js` and mounted it in `app.js`.

###  Refactoring & Chores
* **Removed Redundant Controllers**: Moved everything to the existing `controller` directory and deleted the duplicate `controllers` folder.
* **Gitignore Fix**: Un-tracked accidentally added `node_modules/` from Git cache and appended it to the root `.gitignore`.
* **ESM Config**: Added `"type": "module"` to `BackEnd/package.json` to properly support native Node.js ES Modules.



## Instructions for Reviewers / Teammates
**⚠️ Database Requirement:** On the first boot, the backend requires the teammate with the PostgreSQL connection to execute the `createProductTables()` and `seedProducts()` functions inside `product.model.js` to populate the catalogs.

author: martin-janci
body:
Comprehensive design-system pass on reality-web spanning home alignment, header rebuild, modern form primitives, dark-mode parity, CORS proxy, and locale completeness.

## Sections of work

### 1. Homepage alignment with the design bundle
Added the three sections the design has that we were missing (post-listing, pre-footer):
- `PopularNeighbourhoods` — six curated districts, 2:1 gradient tile, locale-aware `/listings?city=…&district=…` links.
- `ValueStrip` — four-cell stat bar (Verified agents · Building passport · Price history · Mortgage SLA), copy in i18n.
- `HomeCTA` — soft-blue "Selling your home?" panel, secondary `/about` + primary `/sell`.

### 2. Header rebuild
- Audited the `<header>` across all 22 design pages — identical everywhere. Our impl now matches:
  - Brand-square `::before`-style icon + two-tone wordmark
  - 5 nav links: Predaj / Prenájom / Predať / Magazín / Pomoc
  - Primary "Pridať nehnuteľnosť" CTA before the auth slot on ≥1024 px
- `LanguageSwitcher` rewritten as a custom popover (globe + locale code trigger, ARIA listbox, checkmark for active, outside-click/Escape close). Replaces the OS-styled native `<select>`.

### 3. Modern form primitives (`@/components/forms`)
Floating-label fields matching the design's `m-field / m-input / m-textarea / m-dropdown` rules:
- `FieldInput`, `FieldTextarea` — `:not(:placeholder-shown)` animation, prefix/suffix slots, error + helper states
- `FieldSelect` — custom popover dropdown with full keyboard nav + ARIA listbox
- `FormCard`, `FieldGroupTitle`, `FormActions` — layout primitives
- Focus ring 4 px @ 12 % accent (design-spec, softer than default). Reduced-motion fallback.
- `/auth/login` migrated as proof-of-concept; `docs/forms-migration-2026-05-10.md` lists the rest.

### 4. Dark-mode parity sweep
Full-site crawler (24 routes × 2 themes × 3 locales = 144 visits) flagged 66 dark-mode issues. Root cause: `--ppt-color-{success,warning,danger,info,violet,orange,secondary}-light` weren't overridden in the dark block. Fixed in `tokens.css` — light theme keeps solid pastels (#d1fae5 etc.), dark drops to `rgba(accent, 0.18)` with brightened ink, matching the design system's "paired, never inverted" rule and the existing `--ppt-status-*` pair shape.

### 5. FOUC fix
- Color-scheme bootstrap moved from `<body>` (where `<Script strategy="beforeInteractive">` was being queued after hydration) to a plain inline `<script>` at the top of `<head>` — runs during HTML parse, no flash on first paint or navigation.
- DevPanel gets `colorScheme: dark` so native `<select>` controls render dark.

### 6. CORS — same-origin proxy
- `next.config.js` rewrites `/api/*` → `api.rlt.sk` for `wt-*.dev.rlt.sk` hosts (server-side, no browser preflight).
- `getApiBase()` returns `''` for shared-mode worktrees so callers produce relative URLs and hit the rewrite. Dedicated-mode worktrees still use their own `api.wt-*` directly.

### 7. DevPanel theme toggle
- `@ppt/dev-panel` store: `getColorScheme` / `setColorScheme` / `applyColorScheme` helpers (encoded `'system'` as no-key so the inline bootstrap can fall through to `prefers-color-scheme`).
- DevPanel UI: `Theme: light/dark/system` select beneath the API select.

### 8. Locale completeness
- `hu.json` and `pl.json` were missing 52 keys. Filled in. Verified: all six locales now share 319 keys exactly.

### 9. Baseline `:focus-visible`
- 37 component files had interactive controls with no `:focus-visible` rule. Added a global `:where()` baseline in `globals.css` that applies `--ppt-focus-ring-shadow` to every focusable element. Zero-specificity selector — component-level rules still win when they exist.

## Documentation

- `docs/design-audit-2026-05-10.md` — per-route gap matrix vs the design bundle.
- `docs/forms-migration-2026-05-10.md` — modern form-primitive spec + migration order.
- `docs/reality-web-conventions.md` — 10-section conventions doc (token usage, i18n, dark-mode bootstrap, form primitives, CORS, styled-jsx scoping, StyledJsxRegistry, single-source chrome, token reference, audit checklist).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm exec biome check apps/reality-web/src` — clean
- [x] Playwright crawl across 24 routes × 2 themes × 3 locales = 144 visits — clean after token fix
- [x] CLS measured 0.0026 (down from 0.93 pre-PR, see earlier PR work for FOUC details)
- [x] Same-origin `/api/v1/listings/featured` returns 200 on the worktree (was CORS-blocked direct)
- [ ] Reviewer to confirm Bratislava district list curation
- [ ] Reviewer to spot-check copy tone in their locale

body: ## Summary Two dashboard features shipped together in v3.5.0: ### 1 — Per-probe drill-down on the Security tab Clicking any suite row in **Security → Per-Suite Breakdown** expands an inline list of every probe recorded in that suite's last run, showing the target URL, outcome (**allowed** / **blocked** / **dropped**), and HTTP/exit code. - Rows with no probe data (non-HTTP suites like bgp, ping, ssh) show no chevron and are not clickable - Expand state persists while the tab is open and re-renders on each refresh - Up to 200 probes stored per suite, rolling across runs ### 2 — Sortable columns on all data tables Every data table in the dashboard now has clickable column headers. Click to sort descending; click again to reverse. A ▲/▼ indicator marks the active column. Sort re-applies automatically on each data refresh. Tables: Overview Tests · Security Breakdown · Latency · Health Top Processes · Health Child Processes · Health Network Interfaces ## What changed **generator.py** - `SuiteStats`: add `self.probes` list; `record()` / `ok()` / `fail()` / `block()` / `drop()` each accept an optional `target` param that appends a compact `{t, o, c}` entry (capped at `_PROBE_DETAIL_MAX=200`) - `_run_head_batch._worker()`: passes `target=url` so all HTTP-batch suites get drill-down automatically - `_web_record()`: accepts `probe_detail` kwarg; accumulates into `_WEB_STATE["tests"][name]["probes"]` (rolling 200-entry cap) - `_run_guarded()`: passes `probe_detail=list(_stats.probes)` to `_web_record()` - Version bumped to 3.5.0 **webui.py** - Security breakdown rows become clickable when probe data is available (chevron ▶/▼) - Colour-coded probe sub-table: allowed · blocked · dropped - `_xSecRows` + `toggleSecRow()` for expand state - `data-sort-tbody` attribute on all 6 sortable tables; event-delegation click handler on `` - `_sortTableBody()` re-sorts DOM rows (respects xrow pairs), called after each tbody render - `_parseSortVal()` handles ms/s/%, uptime (Xh Ym), plain numbers, text ## Test plan - [ ] Run malware or pornography suite; open Security tab; click a row — probe URLs shown with colour-coded outcomes - [ ] Non-HTTP suites (bgp_peering, icmp) show no chevron - [ ] Click column headers on every table — ▲/▼ indicator appears, rows re-order correctly - [ ] Sort persists across data refresh cycles; descending is the default on first click https://claude.ai/code/session_01QiHkJ7DeFEB7bsfFW93bXW --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01QiHkJ7DeFEB7bsfFW93bXW)_

author: frankbydesign
body:
## Summary

Phase 0.3.3 — replace the placeholder Honor Code page with a proper login experience driven off the existing backend OAuth flow. No backend changes; diff is limited to `apps/web/src/app/`.

- `App` now renders three conditional states off `AuthService` signals: loading (while `/auth/me` resolves), a sign-in screen, and a signed-in shell with a header (app name, user email, sign-out).
- `AuthService.logout()` optimistically clears local state, then POSTs `/auth/logout` with credentials so the visual transition isn't blocked on the network.
- `AuthService.loginInProgress` disables the sign-in button after click — guards against rapid double-clicks / double redirects.
- `withCredentials: true` is preserved on every auth-aware fetch.
- No flash of unauth content on a valid session: both render branches gate on `hasChecked()`.

## Design decisions resolved

- **Routing**: single-component conditional render. Angular Router (with guards / `RouterOutlet` / lazy loading) is deferred to Phase 0.4 when a real second authed route arrives.
- **Signed-in shell**: placeholder header (app name + email + sign-out) and an empty-state main area. Real authed content lands in later phases.
- **Access denied**: deferred. The backend currently returns plain HTTP 403 from `/auth/google/callback` when an email isn't in `ALLOWED_EMAILS`, so the user sees Railway's 403 page rather than a styled frontend view. Delivering the polished "Access denied — try another account" UX requires a small backend change (redirect back to the frontend with `?error=email_not_allowed`), which fell outside this phase's "no backend changes" scope. Tracked as a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [ ] Sign out (or clear cookie), visit `/` → loading flicker, then sign-in screen with "Sign in with Google" button
- [ ] Click "Sign in with Google" → top-level redirect to `${apiBaseUrl}/auth/google/login?next=...`; button disables on click (no double redirect on rapid click)
- [ ] Complete Google consent with an allowed email → land on `/` with the signed-in shell and email visible in the header
- [ ] Reload `/` with an existing valid session → signed-in shell on first paint after a brief loading state; no login-screen flash
- [ ] Click "Sign out" → login screen within ~1s; corresponding `sessions` row gone in DB
- [ ] Delete the session cookie in devtools and reload → falls back silently to login screen, no error UI
- [ ] Open in Incognito (cookie blocked) → degrades to login screen, not an infinite spinner
- [ ] Sign in with a non-allowed email → currently still hits Railway's 403 page (deferred; see above)

author: 3leapsdave
body:
Follow-up to the devrev finding on PR #1's embedded-docs sync. Adds a reliable CI check that prevents the drift class from recurring.

## What

- **Rewritten `scripts/verify-embeds.sh`** with deterministic git-diff-based drift detection. Replaces the previous `rsync --dry-run | grep` heuristic whose output shape differs between in-sync and drifted states (verified to produce flaky results — sometimes exits 0 even after printing "❌ failed"; sometimes inverts).

  Exit codes:

  | Code | Meaning |
  |-----:|---------|
  | 0 | embedded mirrors match SSOT |
  | 1 | drift detected (run `make embed-assets` and commit) |
  | 2 | preflight refused: embedded paths already have uncommitted changes |

  On exit 1 the script restores the working tree so it's a no-op for the caller's working-state.

- **`.github/workflows/verify-embeds.yml`** runs `make verify-embeds` on PRs and main pushes that touch SSOT, embedded mirrors, or the embed scripts.

## Proves the existing drift

Running the new check against current main correctly identifies the existing drift from `5f39ede` (Dec 2025) in `docs/user-guide/index-workflow.md` — SSOT updated for seekable-zstd docs but mirror not re-synced. PR #1 has the fix staged; this check goes green when PR #1 merges.

## Sequencing

Lands in any order. If this PR merges before PR #1, the verify-embeds workflow run on post-merge main will fail (correctly) until PR #1 closes the drift — useful visibility.

author: siddharthrajaraman
body:
## Summary

Implements JWT authentication (`X-DAB-JW-TOKEN`) for `aap-mcp-server`, enabling ALIA to authenticate tool calls using the user's Gateway-issued JWT rather than a static Bearer token. This is required for correct RBAC enforcement when ALIA calls AAP APIs on behalf of a logged-in user.

Jira: [AAP-74412](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AAP-74412)

## What was wrong with PR #133

PR #133 correctly validated incoming JWTs but had two blockers:

**Critical bug**: outbound tool calls sent `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`. Gateway treats JWT strings as unknown API tokens and returns 401 — every tool call failed silently after authentication succeeded.

**Architecture mismatch**: the PR was written against the session-based architecture (`session.ts`, `SessionManager`), which was removed in `b736070`. It cannot be applied to `main` without a full rewrite.

## Changes

- **`src/jwt-validator.ts`** (ported + extended from PR #133): validates `X-DAB-JW-TOKEN` against Gateway's public key endpoint (`/api/gateway/v1/jwt_key/`), with 10-minute caching and automatic cache invalidation + retry on key rotation
- **`src/index.ts`**: extends `RequestContext` with `authHeaderName` and `authHeaderValue`; updates `authenticateRequest()` to try JWT first and fall back to Bearer; fixes outbound request builder to use `ctx.authHeaderName`/`ctx.authHeaderValue` instead of hardcoded `Authorization: Bearer`; updates DoS guard middleware to accept `X-DAB-JW-TOKEN` as valid auth
- **`test/mock-gateway.mjs`** + **`test/gen-jwt.mjs`**: local end-to-end test infrastructure (mock Gateway proxy + JWT generator for testing without a full ALIA stack)

Bearer token auth is fully preserved — existing integrations are unaffected.

## Testing

A mock gateway (`test/mock-gateway.mjs`) serves a test RSA public key at `/api/gateway/v1/jwt_key/` and proxies all other requests to a running aap-dev instance, logging whether the MCP server sent the correct `X-DAB-JW-TOKEN` header or the wrong `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`.

Before fix:
```
[proxy] ✗ GET /api/controller/v2/job_templates/ — Authorization: Bearer <JWT> (wrong header)
[proxy] → 401
```

After fix:
```
[proxy] ✓ GET /api/controller/v2/job_templates/ — X-DAB-JW-TOKEN received, swapping to Bearer
[proxy] → 200
```

Tool calls returned real data from a running aap-dev Controller instance.

**23 unit tests** for `jwt-validator.ts` covering header detection, successful validation, public key caching, key rotation retry, all token failure cases, and public key fetch failures. Full suite: **243/243 passing**.

## Known gaps (follow-up, not blockers)

- `userIdentityService.deriveIdentity` is called with `{}` for JWT sessions — telemetry user identity is not populated. JWTs carry `username` but not `ansibleId`/`email`. Needs clarification from Gateway team on `user_data` schema.
- `gateway.*` tools still fail (Gateway's own API doesn't accept `X-DAB-JW-TOKEN`). Tracked under AAP-74413.
- Full e2e test with a real Gateway-signed JWT requires ALIA wired to `aap-mcp-server`. The machinery exists in `ansible-ai-connect-service` (`get_mcp_headers()`).

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of #200 — makes the facade actually used.

**release.sh**: after contract publish + before commit, builds the loader with the new `current_app_id` baked in, signs a new facade state with the production key, and runs `fdev execute update <FACADE_ID> target/facade/facade.state network` to flip the facade pointer. Asks for confirmation before each network-visible step.

**Conditional**: the block runs only when \`published-contract/facade-id.txt\` is committed (one-time facade publish prereq). Until then it warns + skips so the rest of the release still runs. Once the snapshot lands (#206), Phase 3 becomes automatic per release.

**UI**: new \`FACADE_CONTRACT_ID\` constant populated by \`ui/build.rs\` from the snapshot via \`cargo:rustc-env\`. Uses \`option_env!\` so the offline UI build still compiles when build.rs early-returns. Logged on startup alongside \`WEB_CONTAINER_CONTRACT_ID\` so devtools shows which facade a build references.

## Changes

- \`scripts/release.sh\` — facade-flip block + updated post-release notes.
- \`ui/build.rs\` — emit \`FREENET_EMAIL_FACADE_ID\` env (empty when missing); rerun-if-changed.
- \`ui/src/lib.rs\` — \`FACADE_CONTRACT_ID\` constant + startup log.
- \`RELEASING.md\` — documents new auto-flip behavior + one-time facade publish steps.
- \`AGENTS.md\` — Phase 3 paragraph in §"Facade contract".

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test -p freenet-email-ui --no-default-features --features example-data,no-sync\` — 102 pass
- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy -p freenet-email-ui --no-default-features --features example-data,no-sync -- -D warnings\` clean
- [x] \`bash -n scripts/release.sh\` syntax ok
- [ ] CI: build-and-test passes
- [ ] Manual (post-merge): publish facade once, commit facade-id.txt, run a real release, verify the facade UPDATE goes through and the bookmarked URL serves the new app

## Related
